prompts.categories:
List 40 distinct categories of digital hardware building blocks. Together
they should cover, broadly and representatively, what digital designers
build: the kinds of blocks found across digital design textbooks and
open-source hardware libraries.

For each category give:
- name: a short name;
- description: one sentence saying what the blocks in it do.

Every category must be clearly different from the others.

kinds.Logic Gates:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "Logic Gates": Basic combinational primitives such as AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR that compute Boolean functions of their inputs.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

kinds.Decoders:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "Decoders": Convert an n-bit binary code into a one-hot activation of up to 2^n output lines.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant

kinds.Multipliers:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "Multipliers": Compute products of binary operands using array, Booth, Wallace-tree or sequential shift-add structures.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

kinds.Floating-Point Units:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "Floating-Point Units": Perform IEEE-754 style addition, multiplication, division, square root and conversion on floating-point numbers.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

kinds.RAM Blocks:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "RAM Blocks": Addressable read/write memory arrays, single- or dual-ported, synchronous or asynchronous.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

category "FIFOs and Queues": Buffer data in first-in first-out order, including synchronous and asynchronous dual-clock variants.

  keeps (its registers or memories).

  variant of another entry.

  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half

  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total

kinds.Memory Controllers:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "Memory Controllers": Translate system requests into timed command sequences for DRAM, SRAM or flash devices including refresh handling.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

kinds.High-Speed I/O and SerDes:
List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "High-Speed I/O and SerDes": Serialize, deserialize and line-encode data for high-speed links such as PCIe, Ethernet PHYs and 8b/10b channels.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

List 25 distinct kinds of digital hardware building blocks in the
category "Cryptographic Engines": Accelerate encryption, decryption and hashing algorithms such as AES, SHA and RSA, plus random number generation.

For each kind give:
- name: a short name for the block;
- description: one sentence saying what the block does and what state it
  keeps (its registers or memories).

Rules:
- Every entry is a different kind of block, not a size or parameter
  variant of another entry.
- Describe the block only. Do not state any correctness property, rule or
  relationship that its state must satisfy.
- Leave out these kinds, which are already covered:
  - a FIFO with separate write and read pointers plus an occupancy counter; full and empty are derived, and occupancy always equals the pointer difference
  - a credit counter: a producer spends credits, a consumer returns them; credits outstanding plus credits held always equals the configured total
  - a four-phase req/ack handshake with a busy register; req may not drop until ack rises, and the busy flag mirrors the phase
  - a valid/ready pipeline stage with a skid buffer; the buffered word is only meaningful while the stall flag is up
  - a two-flop synchronizer carrying a gray-coded pointer across clock domains; consecutive pointer samples differ in at most one bit
  - a round-robin arbiter over N requesters with a last-grant register; the grant is always one-hot and never lands on a non-requesting line
  - a fixed-priority arbiter with a lock bit that freezes the current winner until it releases
  - a one-hot FSM; exactly one state bit is ever set, and some transitions are only legal from specific states
  - a binary-encoded FSM whose state register has unreachable encodings; the design never enters them
  - a saturating up-counter that clamps at a maximum below what its register width admits
  - an up counter and a down counter stepped by the same enable; their sum is constant
  - a gray-code counter alongside its binary shadow; the gray value always equals binary XOR binary-shifted-right
  - a shift register tracking in-flight requests with a separate count of set bits
  - a token bucket that refills on a timer tick and drains on grants, capped at a burst size
  - a linear-feedback shift register that never reaches the all-zeros lockup state
  - a watchdog timer that must be kicked before a timeout; the expired flag implies the counter reached its limit
  - a debouncer requiring K identical consecutive samples before the clean output flips; a stability counter never exceeds K
  - a PWM generator with a period counter and duty register; the output is high exactly while the counter is below the duty value
  - a scoreboard counting issued vs retired transactions; retired never exceeds issued and the difference is bounded by the window
  - a ping-pong double buffer with a select bit; the writer and reader never address the same half
  - an elastic (two-entry) buffer with head/tail flags; the occupancy encoded by the flags matches the count register
  - a priority encoder with a registered valid flag; the encoded index is only meaningful while valid is set
  - an accumulator split into two carry-save halves; the halves always sum to the true total
  - a sequence detector for a fixed pattern with a match-progress register; progress never exceeds the pattern length
  - a triple-modular-redundancy voter with three shadow registers; the voted output always equals the majority
  - a sliding-window rate limiter: a shift register of recent grants plus a count of ones that mirrors it
  - a register slice protected by a parity bit; stored parity always matches the stored data
  - a stack pointer with a high-water-mark register; the mark never falls below the pointer and only ratchets upward
  - a DMA burst engine with a beats-remaining counter; the busy flag is up exactly while beats remain
  - a clock divider built from a phase counter; a divided-enable pulse fires exactly when the phase wraps
  - a histogram of N bin counters incremented one at a time; the bins always sum to the total-samples register
  - an in-flight tracker for a pipelined unit: issue increments, a fixed-latency shift register drains; occupancy equals the ones in the shift register

{"kinds":[{"name":"AND gate","description":"Outputs logic 1 only when all of its inputs are 1, and keeps no registers or memory."},{"name":"OR gate","description":"Outputs logic 1 when any of its inputs is 1, and holds no internal state."},{"name":"NOT gate (inverter)","description":"Outputs the logical complement of its single input, with no stored state."},{"name":"NAND gate","description":"Outputs the complement of the AND of its inputs, and keeps no registers or memory."},{"name":"NOR gate","description":"Outputs the complement of the OR of its inputs, and holds no internal state."},{"name":"XOR gate","description":"Outputs 1 when an odd number of its inputs are 1, and is purely combinational with no storage."},{"name":"XNOR gate","description":"Outputs 1 when an even number of its inputs are 1, with no registers or memory."},{"name":"Non-inverting buffer","description":"Passes its input to its output unchanged to restore drive strength, and keeps no state."},{"name":"Tri-state buffer","description":"Drives its input onto the output when enabled and leaves the output high-impedance otherwise, holding no stored state."},{"name":"AND-OR-Invert (AOI21) gate","description":"Computes the complement of (A AND B) OR C in a single compound stage, with no internal storage."},{"name":"OR-AND-Invert (OAI21) gate","description":"Computes the complement of (A OR B) AND C in a single compound stage, keeping no registers."},{"name":"AND-OR (AO22) gate","description":"Computes (A AND B) OR (C AND D) as a non-inverting compound gate, with no stored state."},{"name":"OR-AND (OA22) gate","description":"Computes (A OR B) AND (C OR D) as a non-inverting compound gate, holding no memory."},{"name":"Majority gate","description":"Outputs the value held by more than half of its odd number of inputs, and keeps no state."},{"name":"Minority gate","description":"Outputs the complement of the majority value of its inputs, with no registers or memory."},{"name":"Implication (IMPLY) gate","description":"Outputs NOT A OR B, realizing logical implication from A to B, and is stateless."},{"name":"Inhibit gate","description":"Outputs A AND NOT B so that one input vetoes the other, and holds no internal state."},{"name":"Muller C-element","description":"Sets its output to the common input value when all inputs agree and otherwise holds its previous output, keeping that one output bit as state."},{"name":"Threshold gate","description":"Outputs 1 when the weighted sum of its binary inputs reaches a fixed threshold, with no stored state."},{"name":"Transmission gate","description":"Acts as a bidirectional switch that connects or isolates two nodes under a control signal and its complement, keeping no memory."},{"name":"Open-drain driver","description":"Pulls its output low when its input is asserted and otherwise releases it for an external pull-up, enabling wired-AND buses, with no internal state."},{"name":"Schmitt-trigger inverter","description":"Inverts its input using separate rising and falling switching thresholds, its only state being the current output level that provides hysteresis."},{"name":"Toffoli gate","description":"A reversible three-input gate that passes two control inputs through and flips the third input when both controls are 1, holding no stored state."},{"name":"Fredkin gate","description":"A reversible controlled-swap gate that exchanges its two data inputs when the control input is 1, with no registers or memory."},{"name":"Bus keeper","description":"Weakly drives a shared line back to its last driven value when every driver goes high-impedance, storing that single last-seen bit."}]}

{"kinds":[{"name":"Registered-select multiplexer","description":"Routes one of N data inputs to the output using a select code that is captured into a select register on a load strobe, so the routing changes only when the register is updated."},{"name":"One-hot AND-OR multiplexer","description":"Combines inputs by ANDing each with its own bit of a one-hot select register and ORing the results into the output, holding only that one-hot select register."},{"name":"Time-division multiplexer","description":"Steps a slot counter through the inputs in a fixed repeating schedule and forwards the input owned by the current slot, keeping the slot counter and a programmable slot-count register."},{"name":"Priority multiplexer","description":"Forwards the data of the highest-priority input whose valid line is asserted, keeping a registered copy of the chosen data and the index of the input it came from."},{"name":"Tri-state bus multiplexer","description":"Lets one of several sources drive a shared bus by enabling a single tri-state driver, holding a register of per-source output-enable bits."},{"name":"Packet-boundary stream multiplexer","description":"Merges several packet streams onto one output and only changes source at end-of-packet, keeping a current-source register and an in-packet lock flag."},{"name":"Byte-lane steering multiplexer","description":"Routes each output byte lane from the input byte lane chosen by an address offset and transfer size, holding the registered offset and size that drive the lane selects."},{"name":"Output-registered multiplexer","description":"Selects one input combinationally and captures the result in an output data register every clock, so the selected value appears one cycle later."},{"name":"ADC channel scan multiplexer","description":"Steps through a programmed list of analog input channels to feed a converter, keeping a channel-list memory, a list-index pointer and a settle-delay counter."},{"name":"Test-mode multiplexer","description":"Switches a functional path between normal data and a test or scan source, keeping a test-mode control register that is set through the test interface."},{"name":"Redundancy repair multiplexer","description":"Steers data around a faulty memory column or lane to a spare, keeping a repair-address register loaded from fuses and a repair-enable bit."},{"name":"Sample-and-hold multiplexer","description":"Selects one input on a sample strobe and keeps presenting that captured value until the next strobe, storing the held data and the select code it was taken from."},{"name":"Debug observation multiplexer","description":"Routes a software-chosen group of internal signals onto a debug output bus, keeping a debug-select register written over a configuration port."},{"name":"Recirculating hold multiplexer","description":"Feeds a register either new input data or its own current value depending on an enable, keeping the stored data word."},{"name":"Zero-insertion multiplexer","description":"Forwards the selected input when it is marked valid and otherwise drives a constant default such as zero, keeping a select register and a per-input valid mask register."},{"name":"Break-before-make multiplexer","description":"Changes source by first deselecting all inputs for a programmable number of dead cycles and then enabling the new one, keeping the current select, the pending select and a dead-time counter."},{"name":"Context-select multiplexer","description":"Chooses which of several stored configuration contexts drives a datapath, keeping the context register banks and an active-context index register."},{"name":"LUT multiplexer","description":"Implements an arbitrary logic function by using its input signals as the select code into a set of configuration bits, keeping those configuration bits in a small SRAM."},{"name":"Read-response return multiplexer","description":"Routes read data back from whichever target answered a request to the requester, keeping a table of outstanding transaction IDs mapped to source ports."},{"name":"Latency-matched bank read multiplexer","description":"Selects the read data of the memory bank that was addressed several cycles earlier, keeping a pipeline of delayed bank-select codes."},{"name":"Failover source multiplexer","description":"Forwards a primary source and switches to a backup when the primary is reported faulty, keeping a health-status register and an active-source flag."},{"name":"Header insertion multiplexer","description":"Outputs words from a header register file first and then switches to the payload stream, keeping the header registers and a phase counter that tracks header progress."},{"name":"Loopback multiplexer","description":"Selects whether a receive path sees external line data or the device's own transmit data, keeping a loopback-mode control register."},{"name":"Bitwise masked merge multiplexer","description":"Builds each output bit from one of two inputs according to the matching bit of a mask register, keeping the per-bit mask register."},{"name":"Coefficient bank multiplexer","description":"Feeds a filter or arithmetic unit from one of several stored coefficient sets, keeping the coefficient banks and a bank-select register that is switched at frame boundaries."}]}

{"kinds":[{"name":"Registered 1-to-N demultiplexer","description":"Steers one input word onto the output chosen by a select code and holds every output in its own register, with the select itself captured in a select register."},{"name":"Addressable latch demultiplexer","description":"Writes a single data bit into whichever of N output latches the address selects, leaving all unselected latches holding their previous values in an N-bit latch bank."},{"name":"Packet-boundary stream demultiplexer","description":"Captures a destination field at start-of-packet into a route register and steers every beat of that packet to the chosen output until end-of-packet, tracking an in-packet flag."},{"name":"Valid/ready stream demultiplexer","description":"Forwards a handshaked input to one selected output channel, propagating that channel's ready back upstream, and keeps a registered select plus a per-output valid register."},{"name":"Time-division slot demultiplexer","description":"Distributes successive time slots of a single TDM stream to N output channels using a slot counter and a frame-sync flag, latching each slot's data into its channel register."},{"name":"Round-robin work distributor","description":"Sends each incoming item to the next output in rotation, keeping a next-output pointer register that advances on every accepted item."},{"name":"Least-loaded dispatcher","description":"Routes each incoming request to the output whose queue is currently least occupied, maintaining a per-output occupancy counter array and a registered chosen-index."},{"name":"First-free dispatcher","description":"Routes each incoming job to the lowest-numbered output not marked busy, keeping a busy-flag register per output that is set on dispatch and cleared on completion."},{"name":"Multicast mask demultiplexer","description":"Copies one input to any subset of outputs given by a destination bitmask, storing the mask register and a per-output delivered-flag register until all copies are accepted."},{"name":"Transaction-ID response demultiplexer","description":"Routes each returning response to the requester that issued it by looking up the response ID in an outstanding-ID table that records the requester index for every in-flight tag."},{"name":"Flow-hash steering demultiplexer","description":"Hashes header fields of each incoming packet and uses the hash to index an indirection table that names the destination queue, storing the hash register and the programmable table."},{"name":"EtherType protocol demultiplexer","description":"Extracts the protocol-type field from each frame header into a type register and steers the frame to the matching protocol queue via a programmable type-to-queue match table."},{"name":"Virtual-channel input demultiplexer","description":"Places each arriving flit into the buffer of the virtual channel named in its header, keeping per-VC flit buffers and a current-VC and periodically inserts alignment markers, keeping a lane pointer and a marker-interval counter."},{"name":"Break-before-make demultiplexer","description":"Switches its single output connection between targets by first disabling the old target, waiting a dead-time interval, then enabling the new one, using current-select, pending-select and dead-time counter registers."},{"name":"Shadowed-select demultiplexer","description":"Accepts a new select value into a shadow register at any time but copies it into the active select register only at a programmed safe boundary such as a frame or packet end."},{"name":"Event routing demultiplexer","description":"Delivers a single event or interrupt pulse to one of N target cores according to a programmable routing register, recording the event in a per-target pending flag."},{"name":"Cross-domain pulse demultiplexer","description":"Routes a pulse from a source clock domain to one of N outputs in a destination domain by flipping a per-output toggle register and detecting the toggle with synchronizer flops on the receiving side."},{"name":"Scan-chain select demultiplexer","description":"Directs the test scan-in stream to one of several internal scan chains chosen by a chain-select instruction register loaded through the test port."},{"name":"Trace sink demultiplexer","description":"Steers a debug trace stream to one selected sink such as an on-chip buffer, a trace port or a memory writer, keeping a configuration register for the sink choice and an enable bit."},{"name":"Pipelined demultiplexer tree","description":"Fans a single input out across several levels of small registered demultiplexer stages, each level carrying its own pipelined slice of the select code alongside the data register."},{"name":"Error-sinking demultiplexer","description":"Routes inputs to the output named by the select code but diverts any out-of-range select to a dedicated error sink, capturing the offending select value in an error-address register and setting an error flag."},{"name":"Auto-increment register loader","description":"Writes successive incoming words into consecutive destination registers by using an internal write-index register as the select code, which advances after each write and can be reloaded with a base index."},{"name":"Write-strobe demultiplexer","description":"Converts a registered register-bank address and a single write enable into a one-of-N write strobe for the addressed register, holding the captured address and data until the strobe fires."}]}

one-hot word."},{"name":"Cascadable enable-gated decoder","description":"A 3-to-8 style decoder with multiple active-high and active-low enable pins, so several can be tied together into a wider counter and decodes it into one-hot phase-enable strobes that sequence a multi-cycle operation, keeping the phase counter."},{"name":"Indexed bit set/clear decoder","description":"Decodes an index together with a set or clear command into a single-bit update mask applied to a target flag register, keeping that flag register."},{"name":"Pipelined two-stage decoder","description":"Decodes a wide address in two clocked stages, with a pipeline register holding the partial group decodes between the coarse and fine stages."},{"name":"Domino precharged decoder","description":"A dynamic-logic decoder that precharges every output node in one clock phase and lets only the selected line stay asserted in the evaluate phase, with its state held in the precharged output nodes and keeper devices."},{"name":"Configuration frame address decoder","description":"Decodes a programmable-logic frame address into one-hot enables for a configuration column and frame, keeping a frame address register that auto-increments as frames stream in."},{"name":"Power-domain enable decoder","description":"Decodes a domain identifier written by software into a one-hot request line for that domain's power switch, keeping a domain-select register and a request-pending flag."},{"name":"Keypad row-drive decoder","description":"Cycles a row counter and decodes it so one keypad row is driven low at a time while the columns are sampled, keeping the row counter and a per-row scan timer."},{"name":"Gray-coded input decoder","description":"Decodes a Gray-coded index directly into one-hot outputs, so {"kinds":[{"name":"Thermometer-to-binary encoder","description":"Converts a thermometer-coded input vector into the binary count of its asserted lines, optionally latching the result in an output register."},{"name":"Bubble-correcting flash ADC encoder","description":"Cleans isolated bubble errors in a comparator thermometer code with local majority voting before encoding it to binary, holding the sampled comparator word and encoded output in registers."},{"name":"One-hot-to-binary encoder with error flag","description":"Encodes a one-hot input into its binary index and raises a registered error flag when zero or several lines are active, keeping the last index and error bit."},{"name":"Cascadable priority encoder slice","description":"Encodes the highest active input within an 8-line group and provides enable-in, enable-out and group-select signals so slices chain into wider encoders, with no internal state beyond optional output flops."},{"name":"Hierarchical tree priority encoder","description":"Splits a wide request vector into sub-blocks, encodes each locally, then selects the winning block in a second level and concatenates block and local indices, optionally registering per-level results."},{"name":"Pipelined priority encoder","description":"Breaks priority encoding of a very wide vector across several clock stages, keeping partial winning indices and group-valid bits in inter-stage pipeline registers."},{"name":"Masked priority encoder","description":"Encodes the highest-priority input among those enabled by a software-writable mask register, keeping the mask and the last encoded index."},{"name":"Programmable-priority encoder","description":"Selects the active input with the highest configurable priority level, storing a per-input priority-level register file and the winning index."},{"name":"Threshold-gated priority encoder","description":"Encodes the highest-priority active input only if its level exceeds a current-threshold register, holding the threshold and a pending index output."},{"name":"Wraparound-search priority encoder","description":"Searches the input vector starting from a programmable start-index register and wrapping around, reporting the first active line found and keeping the start index."},{"name":"Bidirectional priority encoder","description":"Simultaneously reports the indices of both the lowest and highest active input lines, optionally registering both indices and an any-active bit."},{"name":"Top-two priority encoder","description":"Finds the first and second highest-priority active inputs in one pass, holding both indices and their individual valid bits in output registers."},{"name":"Iterative set-bit enumerator","description":"Emits the indices of all active inputs one per cycle by repeatedly encoding and clearing the lowest set bit of a residual-mask register loaded from the input."},{"name":"Serial scanning encoder","description":"Polls input lines one at a time with a scan counter and stops when it finds an active line, keeping the scan counter, a found flag and the captured index."},{"name":"Keypad matrix encoder","description":"Drives rows of a key matrix in turn, encoder","description":"Compresses a two-dimensional array of active cells into the row and column of the highest-priority active cell, using row-OR reduction and per-row encoding, with registered coordinate outputs."},{"name":"CAM match-line encoder","description":"Converts the match lines of a content-addressable array into the address of the winning entry plus a multiple-hit indicator, latching the address and hit flags."},{"name":"Field-granular priority encoder","description":"Treats the input as a vector of multi-bit fields and encodes the index of the first nonzero field together with that field's value, keeping both in output registers."},{"name":"Age-ordered priority encoder","description":"Picks the active input that has waited longest, maintaining a per-input age counter that grows while the line stays active and resets on selection, plus the winner index."},{"name":"First-arrival encoder","description":"Records the index of whichever input became active first after re-arming, holding a winner-index register and a captured flag until cleared."},{"name":"Most-recent-event encoder","description":"Tracks the index of the most recently asserted input line by detecting rising edges against a previous-sample register and updating a last-event index register."},{"name":"Change-detect encoder","description":"Compares the inputs with a stored snapshot register and encodes the index of the highest-priority line that changed, along with its new value, then updates the snapshot."},{"name":"Sticky latched priority encoder","description":"Captures incoming active lines into a pending-latch register so short pulses are not lost, encodes the highest pending line, and clears that pending bit on acknowledge."},{"name":"Comparator-bank level encoder","description":"Compares an input sample against a bank of programmable threshold registers and encodes which interval the sample falls into as a binary bin index."},{"name":"Combinatorial-number encoder","description":"Encodes an input vector with exactly K active lines into its compact rank in the combinatorial number system, accumulating partial
