PWM period around a nominal value to spread emitted EMI energy, keeping a period counter, a base-period register, a pseudo-random dither generator state and a dither-depth register."},{"name":"Dithered high-resolution PWM","description":"Achieves finer-than-clock duty resolution by alternating the duty between adjacent integer values across periods, keeping a period counter, an integer duty register, a fractional duty register and a fractional error accumulator."},{"name":"Pulse-train burst generator","description":"Emits a programmed count of pulses at a set spacing after a trigger and then stops, keeping a pulse-count register, a remaining-pulses counter, a spacing counter and a running flag."},{"name":"Programmable delay pulse generator","description":"Outputs a pulse of programmed width starting a programmed delay after an input trigger, keeping a delay register, a width register, a phase counter and a delay/width/idle phase register."},{"name":"Multi-phase interleaved PWM","description":"Generates several PWM channels sharing one period but each shifted by a programmable phase offset, keeping a master period counter, per-channel phase-offset registers and per-channel duty registers."},{"name":"PWM fault trip latch","description":"Forces PWM outputs to a safe state on an external fault input and holds them fixed-rate control pulses whose width encodes a hobby-servo target position, keeping a frame counter, a position-to-width register and a pulse-active flag."},{"name":"LED breathing {"kinds":[{"name":"CRC residue checker","description":"Runs received data and its appended CRC through a feedback shift register and flags an error at end of frame, keeping the running remainder register and a frame-done/error flag."},{"name":"Table-driven parallel CRC engine","description":"Updates a CRC several bytes per cycle by indexing precomputed lookup ROMs with the current remainder XORed with incoming data, holding the remainder register and the lookup tables."},{"name":"Fletcher checksum unit","description":"Computes a Fletcher checksum over a byte stream using two modular running-sum registers that are updated on every input word."},{"name":"Adler-32 checksum unit","description":"Computes an Adler-32 value with two modulo-65521 accumulator registers and a block counter that schedules deferred modular reductions."},{"name":"Reed-Solomon syndrome calculator","description":"Evaluates the received codeword at each root of the generator polynomial using a bank of Horner-rule GF multiply-accumulate registers, one per syndrome."},{"name":"Berlekamp-Massey solver","description":"Iteratively derives the error-locator polynomial from syndromes, keeping coefficient registers for the current and previous locator polynomials, a discrepancy register and a length/step counter."},{"name":"Chien search unit","description":"Tests every field element as a root of the error-locator polynomial by stepping per-coefficient GF multiplier registers each cycle and recording root positions in a position counter and hit flags."},{"name":"Forney error evaluator","description":"Computes error magnitudes at located positions from the error-evaluator polynomial and locator derivative, holding polynomial coefficient registers and a pending-correction output register."},{"name":"BCH encoder","description":"Generates binary BCH parity bits by dividing the message by a generator polynomial in a linear feedback shift register that holds the partial remainder."},{"name":"Golay code encoder/decoder","description":"Encodes 12-bit words into 24-bit extended Golay codewords and corrects up to three bit errors via syndrome lookup, keeping a syndrome register and a decode lookup table."},{"name":"LDPC check-node processor","description":"Computes min-sum check-to-variable messages for one parity-check row, storing the running minimum, second minimum, minimum index and sign-product registers."},{"name":"LDPC variable-node processor","description":"Sums channel log-likelihoods with incoming check messages to produce updated beliefs and hard decisions, keeping a per-node LLR memory and a posterior accumulator."},{"name":"Viterbi branch metric unit","description":"Computes Hamming or Euclidean distances between received soft symbols and each possible encoder output, latching the metrics in a branch-metric register bank."},{"name":"Viterbi traceback unit","description":"Walks backward through stored survivor decision bits from a chosen state to output decoded bits, holding a survivor-path memory, a traceback state register and a read pointer."},{"name":"Turbo SISO decoder","description":"Runs the max-log-MAP forward and backward recursions over a trellis to produce extrinsic information, storing alpha state-metric memory, beta registers and an extrinsic LLR buffer."},{"name":"Polar successive-cancellation decoder","description":"Decodes polar codes by traversing a binary tree of f/g LLR operations, keeping an LLR memory per tree stage, partial-sum registers and a frozen-bit mask ROM."},{"name":"Convolutional interleaver","description":"Spreads burst errors by delaying successive symbols through branches of increasing length, implemented with per-branch delay memories and a commutator branch counter."},{"name":"Memory scrubber","description":"Periodically reads each memory word through the ECC decoder and writes back corrected data, keeping a scrub address counter, an interval timer and a corrected-error count."},{"name":"ECC error logger","description":"Captures details of detected memory errors for software, holding syndrome, failing-address and error-type capture registers plus correctable and uncorrectable error counters."},{"name":"Two-dimensional parity checker","description":"Computes row and column parity over a data block to locate and flip a single erroneous bit, keeping a row-parity register and a column-parity accumulator register."},{"name":"Chipkill symbol-correcting decoder","description":"Corrects failure of an entire DRAM device by treating each chip's bits as one symbol of a symbol-based code, keeping a syndrome register and a failed-chip identifier register."},{"name":"RAID-6 P+Q parity engine","description":"Generates XOR parity P and Galois-field weighted parity Q across data stripes to tolerate two erasures, holding P and Q accumulator buffers and a stripe-index counter."},{"name":"ARQ retransmission controller","description":"Retransmits frames whose integrity check failed or were not acknowledged, keeping a retransmit buffer, sequence-number registers, a retry counter and an acknowledgment timer."},{"name":"Lockstep duplicate-and-compare checker","description":"Runs two copies of a logic block on the same inputs and raises a fault on any output mismatch, keeping a registered mismatch flag and a sticky error-status register."},{"name":"Residue-code arithmetic checker","description":"Checks adder or multiplier results by computing a mod-3 residue of the operands and result in parallel, holding operand residue registers and a residue-mismatch flag."}]}

{"kinds":[{"name":"Composite-field AES S-box","description":"Computes the AES SubBytes substitution by mapping bytes into GF((2^4)^2), inverting there and mapping back with the affine transform, optionally keeping pipeline registers between the isomorphism, inversion and output stages."},{"name":"GHASH multiplier","description":"Performs the GF(2^128) multiply-and-accumulate used for AES-GCM authentication, holding the hash subkey H and the running 128-bit tag accumulator."},{"name":"XTS tweak generator","description":"Produces per-block tweaks for AES-XTS storage encryption by repeatedly multiplying an encrypted sector tweak by alpha in GF(2^128), keeping the current tweak value and a block index register."},{"name":"CBC chaining controller","description":"Wraps a block cipher core to implement CBC encryption and decryption by XORing data with the previous ciphertext, storing the IV/chaining register and a mode/direction register."},{"name":"CTR counter-block generator","description":"Builds successive counter blocks from a nonce and an incrementing counter for counter-mode keystream generation, holding the nonce register, the counter register and a keystream buffer."},{"name":"Keccak-f permutation core","description":"Executes the theta, rho, pi, chi and iota steps of the Keccak-f[1600] permutation for SHA-3 and SHAKE, keeping the 5x5 lane state array and a round index counter."},{"name":"Sponge absorb/squeeze controller","description":"Manages rate-sized absorption of message blocks into a sponge state and later squeezing of output, tracking the byte offset within the rate, the domain-separation suffix and an absorb/squeeze phase register."},{"name":"SHA-2 message schedule expander","description":"Generates the per-round message words for SHA-256 from the input block using the sigma functions, keeping a sliding window of the 16 most recent schedule words."},{"name":"Hash padding unit","description":"Appends the Merkle-Damgard padding bit, zero fill and big-endian message length to the final message block, keeping a 64- or 128-bit total-length counter and a byte-position register."},{"name":"HMAC sequencer","description":"Drives an underlying hash core through the inner and outer passes of HMAC with ipad/opad-XORed keys, storing the padded key, the inner digest and a pass-phase register."},{"name":"MD5 round core","description":"Computes the 64 MD5 operations over a 512-bit block using the F, G, H, I functions and per-step constants, holding the four 32-bit chaining variables and a step counter."},{"name":"DES Feistel round unit","description":"Performs DES/3DES rounds with expansion, S-box substitution and P-permutation on the right half, keeping left and right half registers, the rotating C/D key halves and a round counter."},{"name":"SM4 round unit","description":"Executes the 32 unbalanced-Feistel rounds of the SM4 block cipher with its nonlinear tau and linear L transforms, holding four 32-bit word registers and the round-key schedule state."},{"name":"BLAKE2 G-function core","description":"Applies the BLAKE2 mixing function across columns and diagonals of the 4x4 working vector with permuted message words, storing the working vector, chaining value and byte offset counter."},{"name":"Trivium stream cipher core","description":"Generates keystream bits from three coupled nonlinear shift registers totaling 288 bits, holding that register state and a warm-up cycle counter used during initialization."},{"name":"Poly1305 accumulator","description":"Computes the Poly1305 one-time MAC by adding message blocks to an accumulator and multiplying by the clamped key r modulo 2^130-5, keeping the r and s key registers and the 130-bit accumulator."},{"name":"Barrett reduction unit","description":"Reduces wide products modulo a fixed modulus using a precomputed reciprocal constant and quotient estimate, storing the modulus, the mu constant and intermediate quotient/remainder registers."},{"name":"Elliptic-curve point adder/doubler","description":"Performs point addition and doubling in projective or Jacobian coordinates by sequencing field multiplications and additions, holding the X, Y, Z coordinate registers of the operands and temporaries."},{"name":"Montgomery ladder scalar multiplier","description":"Computes elliptic-curve scalar multiplication by scanning scalar bits and performing a uniform add-and-double step each bit, keeping the two ladder point registers, the scalar register and a bit-index counter."},{"name":"RSA CRT recombination unit","description":"Combines the two half-size exponentiation results modulo p and q into the full RSA result using Garner's formula, storing the partial results, the qInv coefficient and an output register."},{"name":"NTT butterfly unit","description":"Performs Cooley-Tukey/Gentleman-Sande butterflies modulo a small prime for lattice-based post-quantum schemes such as Kyber and Dilithium, holding coefficient operand registers, the current twiddle factor and stage/index counters."},{"name":"TRNG health-test monitor","description":"Runs continuous repetition-count and adaptive-proportion tests on raw entropy samples, keeping the last sample, a repeat counter, a window sample counter and an alarm flag."},{"name":"Von Neumann debiaser","description":"Removes bias from a raw random bitstream by examining non-overlapping bit pairs and emitting one bit for each unequal pair, storing the pending first bit of a pair and an output-valid flag."},{"name":"CTR_DRBG state engine","description":"Implements the NIST SP 800-90A counter-mode deterministic random bit generator with instantiate, reseed and generate operations, holding the internal key, the V counter block and a reseed counter."},{"name":"Secure key slot vault","description":"Stores cryptographic keys in a bank of write-only slots that feed cipher cores directly without software readback, keeping per-slot key registers, usage-permission bits and sticky lock bits."}]}

{"kinds":[{"name":"Halfband interpolator","description":"Doubles the sample rate by inserting filtered samples with a symmetric halfband FIR that skips its zero-valued taps, holding a tapped delay line of past inputs and a phase bit that selects the output branch."},{"name":"Lattice filter","description":"Filters a stream through cascaded lattice stages, each combining forward and backward prediction errors using reflection coefficients, and stores a backward-error delay register per stage plus a coefficient register file."},{"name":"LMS adaptive filter","description":"Runs an FIR filter whose taps are updated every sample from the product of the error signal, the step size and the delayed input, keeping an input delay line, a tap-weight register array and the latest error value."},{"name":"Goertzel tone detector","description":"Measures the energy of one frequency bin over a block of samples with a second-order recursion, keeping two state registers, a sample counter and a coefficient register."},{"name":"Hilbert transformer","description":"Produces a 90-degree phase-shifted quadrature copy of a real input with an antisymmetric FIR, holding a delay line of input samples and a matched delay that aligns the in-phase output."},{"name":"Complex digital mixer","description":"Multiplies incoming I/Q samples by a complex local-oscillator sample to shift the signal in frequency, holding pipeline registers for the four partial products and the summed outputs."},{"name":"DC-blocking filter","description":"Removes the DC offset from a stream with a first-order high-pass recursion, keeping the previous input sample and the previous output sample in registers."},{"name":"Farrow fractional-delay interpolator","description":"Produces samples at arbitrary fractional positions by evaluating a polynomial in the fractional delay over sub-filter outputs, keeping a shared input delay line, the sub-filter output registers and a fractional-mu register."},{"name":"Costas loop phase discriminator","description":"Estimates the carrier phase error from derotated I/Q samples using sign-and-multiply products for carrier recovery, keeping the last derotated sample pair and a registered error output."},{"name":"Gardner timing error detector","description":"Computes a symbol-timing error from the current and previous symbol samples and the midpoint sample between them, storing those samples in a small history register set and a strobe phase flag."},{"name":"Sliding DFT bin","description":"Updates one DFT bin on every new sample by adding the newest sample, subtracting the oldest and applying a complex twiddle rotation, keeping an N-deep sample history buffer and a complex bin accumulator."},{"name":"R2SDF FFT stage","description":"Performs one stage of a pipelined radix-2 single-delay-feedback FFT, routing samples through a feedback delay memory into a butterfly, with a stage control counter that toggles between fill and compute modes."},{"name":"Alpha-max-beta-min magnitude estimator","description":"Approximates the magnitude of a complex sample by taking the larger and smaller absolute components and combining them with fixed weights, holding registered absolute values and the estimate."},{"name":"RMS power meter","description":"Measures signal power by squaring samples, accumulating them over a programmable window and outputting the mean square or its root, keeping a sum-of-squares accumulator, a window counter and a result register."},{"name":"Exponential moving-average filter","description":"Smooths a stream with a leaky integrator that adds a shifted fraction of the difference between the input and the current average, keeping a single extended-precision average register and a shift-amount setting."},{"name":"Feedback comb filter","description":"Creates echo or resonance by adding a scaled, delayed copy of the output back to the input, keeping a circular delay memory, its write pointer and a feedback gain register."},{"name":"Schroeder allpass section","description":"Disperses phase without changing magnitude, as used in reverberators, by combining feedforward and feedback paths around a long delay, keeping a circular delay buffer, a pointer and a gain coefficient."},{"name":"TPDF dither generator","description":"Adds triangular-probability noise, formed from two pseudo-random values, to samples before word-length reduction, keeping the two random generator states and a registered dithered output."},{"name":"Overlap-add block convolver","description":"Convolves a long stream with a filter by processing input blocks and summing the overlapping tail of each block result into the next, keeping a block input buffer, an overlap tail memory and a block counter."},{"name":"Zero-crossing pitch estimator","description":"Estimates the fundamental period of a signal by timing the intervals between sign changes, keeping the previous sample sign, a running interval counter and the last measured period register."},{"name":"IQ imbalance corrector","description":"Compensates gain and phase mismatch between the I and Q branches by applying a correction matrix to each complex sample, holding programmable gain and phase coefficients and pipelined corrected outputs."},{"name":"Constellation slicer","description":"Maps each received complex symbol to the nearest constellation point and outputs the decided bits plus the decision error vector, holding the configured modulation order and registered decision and error values."},{"name":"Welch spectral averager","description":"Averages power spectra across successive FFT frames by accumulating squared bin magnitudes in per-bin memory, keeping the bin accumulation RAM, a bin index counter and a frame counter."},{"name":"Dynamic range compressor","description":"Reduces audio dynamic range by tracking the signal envelope and applying a gain reduction above a threshold with attack and release smoothing, keeping an envelope register, a current gain register and the threshold and ratio parameters."},{"name":"Distributed arithmetic filter","description":"Implements a multiplierless FIR by shifting input samples out bit-serially, using each bit-slice to address a precomputed coefficient-sum lookup table and shift-accumulating the results, keeping input shift registers, the coefficient-sum ROM, an accumulator and a bit counter."}]}

{"kinds":[{"name":"Tournament branch predictor","description":"Combines a local-history predictor and a global-history predictor through a chooser table of saturating counters that selects which component's prediction to use, keeping a local history table, two pattern tables and the chooser array."},{"name":"TAGE branch predictor","description":"Predicts branch direction from several tagged tables indexed by geometrically increasing global-history lengths, keeping per-entry tags, prediction counters, usefulness bits and a base bimodal table."},{"name":"Perceptron branch predictor","description":"Computes a dot product of signed weights with global history bits to predict a branch and trains the weights on mispredictions, keeping a table of weight vectors and a history register."},{"name":"Loop predictor","description":"Recognizes branches that close fixed-trip-count loops and predicts the exit iteration, keeping per-entry tags, learned trip counts, current iteration counts and confidence counters."},{"name":"Indirect target predictor","description":"Predicts targets of register-indirect jumps by hashing the branch address with path history into a tagged target table, keeping target addresses, tags and a path-history register."},{"name":"Speculative history checkpoint unit","description":"Updates the global branch history speculatively at prediction time and restores it on misprediction, keeping the speculative history register and a set of per-branch history snapshots."},{"name":"Fetch target queue","description":"Decouples the branch predictor from the instruction cache by queuing predicted fetch blocks, keeping per-entry start addresses, predicted targets and branch metadata for later resolution."},{"name":"Next-line predictor","description":"Provides a single-cycle guess of the next fetch address and way from the current fetch line, keeping a small table of next-line indices, way hints and valid bits."},{"name":"Compressed instruction expander","description":"Translates 16-bit compressed instruction encodings into their equivalent 32-bit forms ahead of decode, keeping a halfword holding register for instructions that straddle fetch boundaries."},{"name":"Instruction length decoder","description":"Scans a byte stream of variable-length instructions to mark instruction boundaries and extract aligned instructions, keeping a byte buffer, boundary marker bits and a carry-over offset register."},{"name":"Macro-op fusion unit","description":"Detects adjacent instruction pairs such as compare-and-branch and merges them into one internal operation, keeping a lookahead slot holding the previous decoded instruction."},{"name":"Micro-op cache","description":"Stores already-decoded micro-operations indexed by fetch address so that hot code bypasses the decoders, keeping tag arrays, micro-op data lines and valid bits."},{"name":"Loop stream buffer","description":"Captures the decoded instructions of a small tight loop and replays them without refetching, keeping an instruction buffer, loop start and end pointers and a replay-active flag."},{"name":"Branch mask allocator","description":"Assigns each in-flight speculative branch a tag bit and broadcasts kill or clear signals when branches resolve, keeping a free-tag vector and per-instruction branch dependency masks."},{"name":"Age matrix selector","description":"Picks the oldest ready instruction among issue queue entries using a pairwise older-than bit matrix, keeping the age matrix and per-entry ready bits."},{"name":"Dependency matrix wakeup unit","description":"Wakes waiting instructions when their producers issue by consulting a matrix of producer-consumer dependency bits, keeping the dependency matrix and per-entry pending-source flags."},{"name":"Register busy-bit table","description":"Tracks for each physical or architectural register whether its value is still being produced, keeping one busy bit per register that is set at dispatch and cleared at writeback."},{"name":"Store-set dependence predictor","description":"Predicts which loads depend on which earlier stores so loads can issue speculatively but wait on likely conflicts, keeping a store-set ID table and a last-fetched-store table."},{"name":"Load replay unit","description":"Re-issues loads and their dependents when a speculative cache-hit assumption or memory ordering check fails, keeping a replay queue of instruction tags and replay-reason codes."},{"name":"Branch resolution unit","description":"Evaluates branch conditions and targets in execute, compares them with the prediction and triggers redirect and flush, keeping the predicted target, prediction metadata and a redirect address register."},{"name":"Value predictor","description":"Predicts the result of long-latency instructions such as loads from their prior outcomes, keeping a table of last values, strides and confidence counters indexed by instruction address."},{"name":"Fine-grained thread scheduler","description":"Selects one hardware thread per cycle to fetch or issue in an interleaved multithreaded pipeline, keeping per-thread program counters, ready flags and a rotating selection pointer."},{"name":"Zero-overhead loop controller","description":"Executes hardware loops without branch instructions by redirecting fetch at the loop end address, keeping loop start, loop end and iteration count registers for each nesting level."},{"name":"LL/SC reservation monitor","description":"Supports load-linked and store-conditional atomics by recording a reserved address and clearing it on intervening writes, keeping a reservation address register and a reservation-valid flag."},{"name":"Writeback port arbiter","description":"Schedules which completing functional units may use the limited register-file write ports in each cycle, keeping a result-bus reservation shift register of booked future writeback slots."}]}

categories.name: Logic Gates
categories.description: Basic combinational primitives such as AND, OR, NOT, NAND, NOR, XOR and XNOR that compute Boolean functions of their inputs.

categories.name: Multiplexers
categories.description: Select one of several input signals to route to a single output based on a select code.

categories.name: Demultiplexers
categories.description: Route a single input signal to one of several outputs chosen by a select code.

categories.name: Decoders
categories.description: Convert an n-bit binary code into a one-hot activation of up to 2^n output lines.

categories.name: Encoders and Priority Encoders
categories.description: Compress a set of active input lines into a binary code, optionally resolving multiple active inputs by priority.

categories.name: Latches
categories.description: Level-sensitive storage elements that hold a bit while transparent or opaque according to an enable signal.

categories.name: Flip-Flops
categories.description: Edge-triggered single-bit storage elements such as D, JK, T and SR flip-flops with optional set and reset.

categories.name: Registers
categories.description: Groups of flip-flops that store multi-bit words with load enable, reset and parallel access.

categories.name: Shift Registers
categories.description: Register chains that move data serially or in parallel by one position per clock, including serial-to-parallel conversion.

categories.name: Counters
categories.description: Sequential circuits that step through binary, BCD, up/down, ring or Johnson count sequences.

categories.name: Adders and Subtractors
categories.description: Arithmetic circuits such as half, full, ripple-carry, carry-lookahead and carry-save adders that sum or difference binary numbers.

categories.name: Multipliers
categories.description: Compute products of binary operands using array, Booth, Wallace-tree or sequential shift-add structures.

categories.name: Dividers
categories.description: Compute quotients and remainders using restoring, non-restoring, SRT or iterative algorithms.

categories.name: Comparators
categories.description: Determine equality or magnitude relationships between two binary values.

categories.name: Arithmetic Logic Units
categories.description: Perform a selectable set of arithmetic and logical operations on operands and produce status flags.

categories.name: Barrel Shifters and Rotators
categories.description: Shift or rotate a word by an arbitrary number of bit positions in a single cycle.

categories.name: Floating-Point Units
categories.description: Perform IEEE-754 style addition, multiplication, division, square root and conversion on floating-point numbers.

categories.name: Finite State Machines
categories.description: Sequence control behavior through defined states and transitions as Moore or Mealy machines.

categories.name: Register Files
categories.description: Multi-ported arrays of registers providing simultaneous read and write access for processor datapaths.

categories.name: RAM Blocks
categories.description: Addressable read/write memory arrays, single- or dual-ported, synchronous or asynchronous.

categories.name: ROM and Lookup Tables
categories.description: Fixed or programmable read-only storage mapping addresses to precomputed data values.

categories.name: FIFOs and Queues
categories.description: Buffer data in first-in first-out order, including synchronous and asynchronous dual-clock variants.

categories.name: Content-Addressable Memories
categories.description: Search stored entries in parallel by content and return matching addresses.

categories.name: Caches
categories.description: Small fast memories with tag, replacement and coherence logic that hold recently used data from larger memories.

categories.name: Memory Controllers
categories.description: Translate system requests into timed command sequences for DRAM, SRAM or flash devices including refresh handling.

categories.name: Clock Generation and Division
categories.description: Produce, divide, gate or multiply clocks using dividers, clock gating cells, PLLs and DLLs.

categories.name: Clock Domain Crossing Synchronizers
categories.description: Safely transfer signals between asynchronous clock domains using multi-flop synchronizers, handshakes and Gray-code pointers.

categories.name: Reset and Power Management Logic
categories.description: Generate synchronized resets and control power gating, retention and voltage domains.

categories.name: Arbiters
categories.description: Grant access to a shared resource among competing requesters using fixed-priority, round-robin or weighted policies.

categories.name: Bus Interconnects and Crossbars
categories.description: Connect multiple masters and slaves via shared buses, crossbar switches or on-chip bus protocols like AXI and Wishbone.

categories.name: Network-on-Chip Routers
categories.description: Forward packets between on-chip nodes using routing, flow control and virtual channels.

categories.name: Serial Communication Interfaces
categories.description: Implement low-speed serial protocols such as UART, SPI and I2C for peripheral communication.

categories.name: High-Speed I/O and SerDes
categories.description: Serialize, deserialize and line-encode data for high-speed links such as PCIe, Ethernet PHYs and 8b/10b channels.

categories.name: DMA Controllers
categories.description: Move blocks of data between memory and peripherals without processor intervention.

categories.name: Interrupt Controllers
categories.description: Collect, prioritize and dispatch interrupt requests to processors.

categories.name: Timers and PWM Generators
categories.description: Measure time intervals, generate periodic events, watchdogs and pulse-width-modulated outputs.

categories.name: Error Detection and Correction
categories.description: Generate and check parity, CRC and ECC codes such as Hamming or Reed-Solomon to detect and correct data errors.

categories.name: Cryptographic Engines
categories.description: Accelerate encryption, decryption and hashing algorithms such as AES, SHA and RSA, plus random number generation.

categories.name: Digital Signal Processing Blocks
categories.description: Process sampled data streams with FIR/IIR filters, FFTs, MAC units, CORDIC and numerically controlled oscillators.

categories.name: Processor Cores and Pipelines
categories.description: Fetch, decode and execute instructions using pipelined datapaths with hazard detection, forwarding and branch prediction.

candidates.name: AND gate
candidates.description: Outputs logic 1 only when all of its inputs are 1, and keeps no registers or memory.

candidates.name: OR gate
candidates.description: Outputs logic 1 when any of its inputs is 1, and holds no internal state.

candidates.name: NOT gate (inverter)
candidates.description: Outputs the logical complement of its single input, with no stored state.

candidates.name: NAND gate
candidates.description: Outputs the complement of the AND of its inputs, and keeps no registers or memory.

candidates.name: NOR gate
candidates.description: Outputs the complement of the OR of its inputs, and holds no internal state.

candidates.name: XOR gate
candidates.description: Outputs 1 when an odd number of its inputs are 1, and is purely combinational with no storage.

candidates.name: XNOR gate
candidates.description: Outputs 1 when an even number of its inputs are 1, with no registers or memory.

candidates.name: Non-inverting buffer
candidates.description: Passes its input to its output unchanged to restore drive strength, and keeps no state.

candidates.name: Tri-state buffer
candidates.description: Drives its input onto the output when enabled and leaves the output high-impedance otherwise, holding no stored state.

candidates.name: AND-OR-Invert (AOI21) gate
candidates.description: Computes the complement of (A AND B) OR C in a single compound stage, with no internal storage.

candidates.name: OR-AND-Invert (OAI21) gate
candidates.description: Computes the complement of (A OR B) AND C in a single compound stage, keeping no registers.

candidates.name: AND-OR (AO22) gate
candidates.description: Computes (A AND B) OR (C AND D) as a non-inverting compound gate, with no stored state.

candidates.name: OR-AND (OA22) gate
candidates.description: Computes (A OR B) AND (C OR D) as a non-inverting compound gate, holding no memory.

candidates.name: Majority gate
candidates.description: Outputs the value held by more than half of its odd number of inputs, and keeps no state.

candidates.name: Minority gate
candidates.description: Outputs the complement of the majority value of its inputs, with no registers or memory.

candidates.name: Implication (IMPLY) gate
candidates.description: Outputs NOT A OR B, realizing logical implication from A to B, and is stateless.

candidates.name: Inhibit gate
candidates.description: Outputs A AND NOT B so that one input vetoes the other, and holds no internal state.

candidates.name: Muller C-element
candidates.description: Sets its output to the common input value when all inputs agree and otherwise holds its previous output, keeping that one output bit as state.

candidates.name: Threshold gate
candidates.description: Outputs 1 when the weighted sum of its binary inputs reaches a fixed threshold, with no stored state.

candidates.name: Transmission gate
candidates.description: Acts as a bidirectional switch that connects or isolates two nodes under a control signal and its complement, keeping no memory.

candidates.name: Open-drain driver
candidates.description: Pulls its output low when its input is asserted and otherwise releases it for an external pull-up, enabling wired-AND buses, with no internal state.

candidates.name: Schmitt-trigger inverter
candidates.description: Inverts its input using separate rising and falling switching thresholds, its only state being the current output level that provides hysteresis.

candidates.name: Toffoli gate
candidates.description: A reversible three-input gate that passes two control inputs through and flips the third input when both controls are 1, holding no stored state.

candidates.name: Fredkin gate
candidates.description: A reversible controlled-swap gate that exchanges its two data inputs when the control input is 1, with no registers or memory.

candidates.name: Bus keeper
candidates.description: Weakly drives a shared line back to its last driven value when every driver goes high-impedance, storing that single last-seen bit.

candidates.name: Registered-select multiplexer
candidates.description: Routes one of N data inputs to the output using a select code that is captured into a select register on a load strobe, so the routing changes only when the register is updated.

candidates.name: One-hot AND-OR multiplexer
candidates.description: Combines inputs by ANDing each with its own bit of a one-hot select register and ORing the results into the output, holding only that one-hot select register.

candidates.name: Time-division multiplexer
candidates.description: Steps a slot counter through the inputs in a fixed repeating schedule and forwards the input owned by the current slot, keeping the slot counter and a programmable slot-count register.

candidates.name: Priority multiplexer
candidates.description: Forwards the data of the highest-priority input whose valid line is asserted, keeping a registered copy of the chosen data and the index of the input it came from.

candidates.name: Tri-state bus multiplexer
candidates.description: Lets one of several sources drive a shared bus by enabling a single tri-state driver, holding a register of per-source output-enable bits.

candidates.name: Packet-boundary stream multiplexer
candidates.description: Merges several packet streams onto one output and only changes source at end-of-packet, keeping a current-source register and an in-packet lock flag.

candidates.name: Byte-lane steering multiplexer
candidates.description: Routes each output byte lane from the input byte lane chosen by an address offset and transfer size, holding the registered offset and size that drive the lane selects.

candidates.name: Output-registered multiplexer
candidates.description: Selects one input combinationally and captures the result in an output data register every clock, so the selected value appears one cycle later.

candidates.name: ADC channel scan multiplexer
candidates.description: Steps through a programmed list of analog input channels to feed a converter, keeping a channel-list memory, a list-index pointer and a settle-delay counter.

candidates.name: Test-mode multiplexer
candidates.description: Switches a functional path between normal data and a test or scan source, keeping a test-mode control register that is set through the test interface.

candidates.name: Redundancy repair multiplexer
candidates.description: Steers data around a faulty memory column or lane to a spare, keeping a repair-address register loaded from fuses and a repair-enable bit.

candidates.name: Sample-and-hold multiplexer
candidates.description: Selects one input on a sample strobe and keeps presenting that captured value until the next strobe, storing the held data and the select code it was taken from.

candidates.name: Debug observation multiplexer
candidates.description: Routes a software-chosen group of internal signals onto a debug output bus, keeping a debug-select register written over a configuration port.

candidates.name: Recirculating hold multiplexer
candidates.description: Feeds a register either new input data or its own current value depending on an enable, keeping the stored data word.

candidates.name: Zero-insertion multiplexer
candidates.description: Forwards the selected input when it is marked valid and otherwise drives a constant default such as zero, keeping a select register and a per-input valid mask register.

candidates.name: Break-before-make multiplexer
candidates.description: Changes source by first deselecting all inputs for a programmable number of dead cycles and then enabling the new one, keeping the current select, the pending select and a dead-time counter.

candidates.name: Context-select multiplexer
candidates.description: Chooses which of several stored configuration contexts drives a datapath, keeping the context register banks and an active-context index register.

candidates.name: LUT multiplexer
candidates.description: Implements an arbitrary logic function by using its input signals as the select code into a set of configuration bits, keeping those configuration bits in a small SRAM.

candidates.name: Read-response return multiplexer
candidates.description: Routes read data back from whichever target answered a request to the requester, keeping a table of outstanding transaction IDs mapped to source ports.

candidates.name: Latency-matched bank read multiplexer
candidates.description: Selects the read data of the memory bank that was addressed several cycles earlier, keeping a pipeline of delayed bank-select codes.

candidates.name: Failover source multiplexer
candidates.description: Forwards a primary source and switches to a backup when the primary is reported faulty, keeping a health-status register and an active-source flag.

candidates.name: Header insertion multiplexer
candidates.description: Outputs words from a header register file first and then switches to the payload stream, keeping the header registers and a phase counter that tracks header progress.

candidates.name: Loopback multiplexer
candidates.description: Selects whether a receive path sees external line data or the device's own transmit data, keeping a loopback-mode control register.

candidates.name: Bitwise masked merge multiplexer
candidates.description: Builds each output bit from one of two inputs according to the matching bit of a mask register, keeping the per-bit mask register.

candidates.name: Coefficient bank multiplexer
candidates.description: Feeds a filter or arithmetic unit from one of several stored coefficient sets, keeping the coefficient banks and a bank-select register that is switched at frame boundaries.

candidates.name: Registered 1-to-N demultiplexer
candidates.description: Steers one input word onto the output chosen by a select code and holds every output in its own register, with the select itself captured in a select register.

candidates.name: Addressable latch demultiplexer
candidates.description: Writes a single data bit into whichever of N output latches the address selects, leaving all unselected latches holding their previous values in an N-bit latch bank.

candidates.name: Packet-boundary stream demultiplexer
candidates.description: Captures a destination field at start-of-packet into a route register and steers every beat of that packet to the chosen output until end-of-packet, tracking an in-packet flag.

candidates.name: Valid/ready stream demultiplexer
candidates.description: Forwards a handshaked input to one selected output channel, propagating that channel's ready back upstream, and keeps a registered select plus a per-output valid register.

candidates.name: Time-division slot demultiplexer
candidates.description: Distributes successive time slots of a single TDM stream to N output channels using a slot counter and a frame-sync flag, latching each slot's data into its channel register.

candidates.name: Round-robin work distributor
candidates.description: Sends each incoming item to the next output in rotation, keeping a next-output pointer register that advances on every accepted item.

candidates.name: Least-loaded dispatcher
candidates.description: Routes each incoming request to the output whose queue is currently least occupied, maintaining a per-output occupancy counter array and a registered chosen-index.

candidates.name: First-free dispatcher
candidates.description: Routes each incoming job to the lowest-numbered output not marked busy, keeping a busy-flag register per output that is set on dispatch and cleared on completion.

candidates.name: Multicast mask demultiplexer
candidates.description: Copies one input to any subset of outputs given by a destination bitmask, storing the mask register and a per-output delivered-flag register until all copies are accepted.

candidates.name: Transaction-ID response demultiplexer
candidates.description: Routes each returning response to the requester that issued it by looking up the response ID in an outstanding-ID table that records the requester index for every in-flight tag.

candidates.name: Flow-hash steering demultiplexer
candidates.description: Hashes header fields of each incoming packet and uses the hash to index an indirection table that names the destination queue, storing the hash register and the programmable table.

candidates.name: EtherType protocol demultiplexer
candidates.description: Extracts the protocol-type field from each frame header into a type register and steers the frame to the matching protocol queue via a programmable type-to-queue match table.

candidates.name: Virtual-channel input demultiplexer
candidates.description: Places each arriving flit into the buffer of the virtual channel named in its header, keeping per-VC flit buffers and a current-VC register for multi-flit packets.

candidates.name: Memory bank-steering demultiplexer
candidates.description: Routes each memory request to one of several interleaved banks chosen by low-order address bits, holding a per-bank pending-request register and the decoded bank index.

candidates.name: Multi-lane striping distributor
candidates.description: Spreads a single word stream across several physical lanes in fixed rotation and periodically inserts alignment markers, keeping a lane pointer and a marker-interval counter.

candidates.name: Break-before-make demultiplexer
candidates.description: Switches its single output connection between targets by first disabling the old target, waiting a dead-time interval, then enabling the new one, using current-select, pending-select and dead-time counter registers.

candidates.name: Shadowed-select demultiplexer
candidates.description: Accepts a new select value into a shadow register at any time but copies it into the active select register only at a programmed safe boundary such as a frame or packet end.

candidates.name: Event routing demultiplexer
candidates.description: Delivers a single event or interrupt pulse to one of N target cores according to a programmable routing register, recording the event in a per-target pending flag.

candidates.name: Cross-domain pulse demultiplexer
candidates.description: Routes a pulse from a source clock domain to one of N outputs in a destination domain by flipping a per-output toggle register and detecting the toggle with synchronizer flops on the receiving side.

candidates.name: Scan-chain select demultiplexer
candidates.description: Directs the test scan-in stream to one of several internal scan chains chosen by a chain-select instruction register loaded through the test port.

candidates.name: Trace sink demultiplexer
candidates.description: Steers a debug trace stream to one selected sink such as an on-chip buffer, a trace port or a memory writer, keeping a configuration register for the sink choice and an enable bit.

candidates.name: Pipelined demultiplexer tree
candidates.description: Fans a single input out across several levels of small registered demultiplexer stages, each level carrying its own pipelined slice of the select code alongside the data register.

candidates.name: Error-sinking demultiplexer
candidates.description: Routes inputs to the output named by the select code but diverts any out-of-range select to a dedicated error sink, capturing the offending select value in an error-address register and setting an error flag.

candidates.name: Auto-increment register loader
candidates.description: Writes successive incoming words into consecutive destination registers by using an internal write-index register as the select code, which advances after each write and can be reloaded with a base index.

candidates.name: Write-strobe demultiplexer
candidates.description: Converts a registered register-bank address and a single write enable into a one-of-N write strobe for the addressed register, holding the captured address and data until the strobe fires.

candidates.name: Registered-output one-hot decoder
candidates.description: Decodes an n-bit input into 2^n lines and captures the result in an output flip-flop bank each clock, keeping only that registered one-hot word.

candidates.name: Cascadable enable-gated decoder
candidates.description: A 3-to-8 style decoder with multiple active-high and active-low enable pins, so several can be tied together into a wider decoder; it is purely combinational and holds no state.

candidates.name: Two-level predecoder
candidates.description: Splits the address into fields, decodes each field into small one-hot groups, and ANDs the groups to form the final lines, with an optional latch holding the predecoded group outputs.

candidates.name: SRAM wordline decoder with pulse latch
candidates.description: Decodes a row address into a single wordline and fires it for a self-timed pulse, keeping a latched row address and a pulse-active flip-flop.

candidates.name: Column select decoder
candidates.description: Decodes the low address bits into one-hot bitline-mux selects for a memory column group, holding the column address in an input latch.

candidates.name: DRAM row decoder with RAS address latch
candidates.description: Captures the row address on the row strobe and decodes it to drive one row line until precharge, keeping the latched row address and a row-open flag.

candidates.name: Redundancy-steering row decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a row address but compares it against fuse-loaded repair addresses and activates a spare row instead on a match, keeping the repair address registers and their enable bits.

candidates.name: Binary-to-thermometer decoder
candidates.description: Converts an n-bit value into a 2^n-line thermometer code in which all lines up to the value are asserted, typically driving unary DAC segments, with an optional output register.

candidates.name: Byte-lane strobe decoder
candidates.description: Turns the low address bits and an access-size field into per-byte write-enable strobes for a wide data bus, holding a registered copy of the strobes for the data phase.

candidates.name: Register-file write-port decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a destination register index qualified by write-enable into one-hot per-register write enables, keeping a pipelined copy of the index and enable.

candidates.name: Bank-select decoder
candidates.description: Decodes upper address bits into one-hot enables for memory banks, keeping a bank-select register that holds the active bank for the duration of a burst.

candidates.name: Latched-address chip-select decoder
candidates.description: Captures a multiplexed address/data bus on an address-latch-enable strobe and decodes the latched high bits into peripheral chip selects, keeping the address latch.

candidates.name: Cache way-enable decoder
candidates.description: Converts an encoded way index from the hit or replacement logic into one-hot way enables for the data arrays, keeping a registered way index for the write-back cycle.

candidates.name: Bus-grant line decoder
candidates.description: Expands an arbiter's encoded grant number into individual one-hot grant wires to the masters, holding the current grant number in a register.

candidates.name: Shift-amount stage decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a shift count into one-hot or per-stage select signals that steer the rows of a logarithmic or crossbar shifter, holding a registered shift count.

candidates.name: Range mask decoder
candidates.description: Takes start and end bit indices and produces a contiguous mask of asserted lines between them, as used for bit-field insert and extract, holding the start and end index registers.

candidates.name: Priority-level mask decoder
candidates.description: Decodes the current interrupt priority level into a mask that blocks all equal and lower priorities, keeping the current-level register.

candidates.name: Timing-phase decoder
candidates.description: Steps a small binary phase counter and decodes it into one-hot phase-enable strobes that sequence a multi-cycle operation, keeping the phase counter.

candidates.name: Indexed bit set/clear decoder
candidates.description: Decodes an index together with a set or clear command into a single-bit update mask applied to a target flag register, keeping that flag register.

candidates.name: Pipelined two-stage decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a wide address in two clocked stages, with a pipeline register holding the partial group decodes between the coarse and fine stages.

candidates.name: Domino precharged decoder
candidates.description: A dynamic-logic decoder that precharges every output node in one clock phase and lets only the selected line stay asserted in the evaluate phase, with its state held in the precharged output nodes and keeper devices.

candidates.name: Configuration frame address decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a programmable-logic frame address into one-hot enables for a configuration column and frame, keeping a frame address register that auto-increments as frames stream in.

candidates.name: Power-domain enable decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a domain identifier written by software into a one-hot request line for that domain's power switch, keeping a domain-select register and a request-pending flag.

candidates.name: Keypad row-drive decoder
candidates.description: Cycles a row counter and decodes it so one keypad row is driven low at a time while the columns are sampled, keeping the row counter and a per-row scan timer.

candidates.name: Gray-coded input decoder
candidates.description: Decodes a Gray-coded index directly into one-hot outputs, so that a single-bit input change moves the active line without intermediate glitches, keeping a registered copy of the Gray input.

candidates.name: Thermometer-to-binary encoder
candidates.description: Converts a thermometer-coded input vector into the binary count of its asserted lines, optionally latching the result in an output register.

candidates.name: Bubble-correcting flash ADC encoder
candidates.description: Cleans isolated bubble errors in a comparator thermometer code with local majority voting before encoding it to binary, holding the sampled comparator word and encoded output in registers.

candidates.name: One-hot-to-binary encoder with error flag
candidates.description: Encodes a one-hot input into its binary index and raises a registered error flag when zero or several lines are active, keeping the last index and error bit.

candidates.name: Cascadable priority encoder slice
candidates.description: Encodes the highest active input within an 8-line group and provides enable-in, enable-out and group-select signals so slices chain into wider encoders, with no internal state beyond optional output flops.

candidates.name: Hierarchical tree priority encoder
candidates.description: Splits a wide request vector into sub-blocks, encodes each locally, then selects the winning block in a second level and concatenates block and local indices, optionally registering per-level results.

candidates.name: Pipelined priority encoder
candidates.description: Breaks priority encoding of a very wide vector across several clock stages, keeping partial winning indices and group-valid bits in inter-stage pipeline registers.

candidates.name: Masked priority encoder
candidates.description: Encodes the highest-priority input among those enabled by a software-writable mask register, keeping the mask and the last encoded index.

candidates.name: Programmable-priority encoder
candidates.description: Selects the active input with the highest configurable priority level, storing a per-input priority-level register file and the winning index.

candidates.name: Threshold-gated priority encoder
candidates.description: Encodes the highest-priority active input only if its level exceeds a current-threshold register, holding the threshold and a pending index output.

candidates.name: Wraparound-search priority encoder
candidates.description: Searches the input vector starting from a programmable start-index register and wrapping around, reporting the first active line found and keeping the start index.

candidates.name: Bidirectional priority encoder
candidates.description: Simultaneously reports the indices of both the lowest and highest active input lines, optionally registering both indices and an any-active bit.

candidates.name: Top-two priority encoder
candidates.description: Finds the first and second highest-priority active inputs in one pass, holding both indices and their individual valid bits in output registers.

candidates.name: Iterative set-bit enumerator
candidates.description: Emits the indices of all active inputs one per cycle by repeatedly encoding and clearing the lowest set bit of a residual-mask register loaded from the input.

candidates.name: Serial scanning encoder
candidates.description: Polls input lines one at a time with a scan counter and stops when it finds an active line, keeping the scan counter, a found flag and the captured index.

candidates.name: Keypad matrix encoder
candidates.description: Drives rows of a key matrix in turn, samples columns, and encodes the pressed key's row and column into a key code, storing the row-scan counter, key-code register and key-pressed flag.

candidates.name: 2D grid coordinate encoder
candidates.description: Compresses a two-dimensional array of active cells into the row and column of the highest-priority active cell, using row-OR reduction and per-row encoding, with registered coordinate outputs.

candidates.name: CAM match-line encoder
candidates.description: Converts the match lines of a content-addressable array into the address of the winning entry plus a multiple-hit indicator, latching the address and hit flags.

candidates.name: Field-granular priority encoder
candidates.description: Treats the input as a vector of multi-bit fields and encodes the index of the first nonzero field together with that field's value, keeping both in output registers.

candidates.name: Age-ordered priority encoder
candidates.description: Picks the active input that has waited longest, maintaining a per-input age counter that grows while the line stays active and resets on selection, plus the winner index.

candidates.name: First-arrival encoder
candidates.description: Records the index of whichever input became active first after re-arming, holding a winner-index register and a captured flag until cleared.

candidates.name: Most-recent-event encoder
candidates.description: Tracks the index of the most recently asserted input line by detecting rising edges against a previous-sample register and updating a last-event index register.

candidates.name: Change-detect encoder
candidates.description: Compares the inputs with a stored snapshot register and encodes the index of the highest-priority line that changed, along with its new value, then updates the snapshot.

candidates.name: Sticky latched priority encoder
candidates.description: Captures incoming active lines into a pending-latch register so short pulses are not lost, encodes the highest pending line, and clears that pending bit on acknowledge.

candidates.name: Comparator-bank level encoder
candidates.description: Compares an input sample against a bank of programmable threshold registers and encodes which interval the sample falls into as a binary bin index.

candidates.name: Combinatorial-number encoder
candidates.description: Encodes an input vector with exactly K active lines into its compact rank in the combinatorial number system, accumulating partial binomial sums in a rank register when computed sequentially.

candidates.name: NOR SR latch
candidates.description: Two cross-coupled NOR gates that set or reset on active-high S and R inputs and keep one stored bit, Q, in the feedback loop while both inputs are low.

candidates.name: NAND SR-bar latch
candidates.description: Two cross-coupled NAND gates driven by active-low set and reset inputs that keep a single stored bit in their feedback loop while both inputs are high.

candidates.name: Gated SR latch
candidates.description: An SR latch whose set and reset inputs pass only while an enable level is asserted, so it keeps its stored bit whenever the enable is inactive.

candidates.name: Set-dominant SR latch
candidates.description: An SR latch with extra logic that resolves simultaneous set and reset in favor of set, and it holds one state bit.

candidates.name: Reset-dominant SR latch
candidates.description: An SR latch with extra logic that resolves simultaneous set and reset in favor of reset, and it holds one state bit.

candidates.name: Gated D latch (active-high)
candidates.description: A transparent latch that passes D to Q while the enable is high and freezes the last value in its storage node when the enable falls.

candidates.name: Gated D latch (active-low)
candidates.description: A transparent latch that passes D to Q while the enable is low and keeps the captured bit in its storage node while the enable is high.

candidates.name: Gated JK latch
candidates.description: A level-enabled latch whose J and K inputs set, reset or invert the stored bit while the enable is asserted, and it holds that bit otherwise.

candidates.name: Earle latch
candidates.description: A hazard-free two-level AND-OR latch with a redundant consensus term that holds its stored bit glitch-free across enable transitions.

candidates.name: Polarity-hold latch
candidates.description: A latch built from complementary data and clock paths that tracks the data while the clock is active and keeps one stored bit while the clock is inactive.

candidates.name: Mux-feedback latch
candidates.description: A 2:1 multiplexer whose output feeds back to one input, selecting new data while enabled and recirculating its single stored bit otherwise.

candidates.name: Transmission-gate static latch
candidates.description: A CMOS latch that uses a transmission gate to admit data during the enable phase and a gated back-to-back inverter loop to keep the bit statically.

candidates.name: Dynamic latch
candidates.description: A latch that samples data through a pass transistor onto a capacitive node and keeps the bit as stored charge only for a limited time after the enable closes.

candidates.name: Latch with asynchronous clear
candidates.description: A D latch with an overriding clear input that forces the stored bit to zero regardless of the enable, and it otherwise holds its single bit.

candidates.name: Latch with asynchronous preset
candidates.description: A D latch with an overriding preset input that forces the stored bit to one regardless of the enable, and it otherwise holds its single bit.

candidates.name: Pulsed latch
candidates.description: A transparent latch opened by a narrow pulse generated from a clock edge, so it captures data in a short window and holds one bit between pulses.

candidates.name: Scan lockup latch
candidates.description: A latch placed between scan segments in different clock domains that holds the shifted bit for half a cycle to prevent hold races during scan shift.

candidates.name: LSSD shift-register latch
candidates.description: A level-sensitive scan design latch pair in which an L1 latch with separate system and scan clocks feeds an L2 latch, and each latch keeps one bit.

candidates.name: Dual-port latch
candidates.description: A latch with two independently enabled data inputs that each write one shared stored bit, which it holds when neither enable is active.

candidates.name: Bus-keeper latch
candidates.description: A weak feedback inverter pair attached to a tri-state bus that retains the last driven logic level as its stored bit when all drivers float.

candidates.name: Tri-state output transparent latch
candidates.description: A multi-bit transparent latch bank with a latch-enable and an independent output-enable that holds a captured bus word and can release its outputs to high impedance.

candidates.name: Addressable latch
candidates.description: A bank of individually addressed bit latches in which an address and data input update one selected bit while enabled, and every bit holds its own stored value.

candidates.name: State-retention balloon latch
candidates.description: An always-powered shadow latch that saves the bit of a power-gated register on a save signal, keeps it during power-down, and restores it on wake-up.

candidates.name: Razor shadow latch
candidates.description: A delayed-clock shadow latch beside a main storage element that recaptures late-arriving data and keeps that sampled bit for comparison with the main value.

candidates.name: Positive-edge D flip-flop
candidates.description: Captures the D input into its single state bit Q on each rising clock edge and holds it until the next rising edge.

candidates.name: Negative-edge D flip-flop
candidates.description: Captures the D input into its single stored bit on each falling clock edge, holding the value through the following clock cycle.

candidates.name: D flip-flop with asynchronous reset
candidates.description: Stores one bit sampled from D on the clock edge, and forces that bit to zero immediately whenever its reset input is asserted, independent of the clock.

candidates.name: D flip-flop with synchronous reset
candidates.description: Stores one bit that is loaded from D on each clock edge, or loaded with zero on the clock edge when the reset input is asserted.

candidates.name: D flip-flop with asynchronous preset and clear
candidates.description: Keeps one state bit loaded from D on the clock edge, which can also be forced high by an asynchronous preset input or low by an asynchronous clear input.

candidates.name: Clock-enable D flip-flop
candidates.description: Holds one stored bit that is updated from D on a clock edge only when its enable input is high, and otherwise recirculates its current value.

candidates.name: JK flip-flop
candidates.description: Keeps one state bit that on each clock edge holds, sets, resets, or toggles according to the J and K inputs.

candidates.name: T flip-flop
candidates.description: Keeps one state bit that inverts on each clock edge when the T input is high and holds its value otherwise.

candidates.name: Clocked SR flip-flop
candidates.description: Keeps one state bit that is set by the S input or cleared by the R input, with changes taking effect only on the active clock edge.

candidates.name: Set-dominant SR flip-flop
candidates.description: Stores one bit updated on the clock edge from set and reset inputs, choosing to set the bit when both inputs are asserted together.

candidates.name: Reset-dominant SR flip-flop
candidates.description: Stores one bit updated on the clock edge from set and reset inputs, choosing to clear the bit when both inputs are asserted together.

candidates.name: Dual-edge-triggered flip-flop
candidates.description: Samples its D input into one stored output bit on both rising and falling clock edges, using two internal latches whose outputs are multiplexed by the clock level.

candidates.name: Master-slave D flip-flop
candidates.description: Builds edge-triggered storage from a master latch that is transparent in one clock phase and a slave latch transparent in the other, each holding one internal bit.

candidates.name: Pulse-triggered flip-flop
candidates.description: Uses a short pulse generated from the clock edge to briefly open a single latch, which then holds the captured D bit for the rest of the cycle.

candidates.name: Sense-amplifier flip-flop
candidates.description: Resolves the differential D input with a precharged sense-amplifier stage at the clock edge and keeps the result in a following set-reset latch.

candidates.name: Complementary-output D flip-flop
candidates.description: Stores one bit captured from D on the clock edge and drives both the true output Q and its inverted output Qn from that stored state.

candidates.name: Muxed-input D flip-flop
candidates.description: Selects between two data inputs with a select line and captures the chosen bit into its single state register on the clock edge.

candidates.name: State-retention flip-flop
candidates.description: Holds a normal one-bit register plus an always-powered balloon latch that saves the bit before power-down and restores it on wake-up.

candidates.name: Razor timing-error flip-flop
candidates.description: Captures D into a main flop on the clock edge and again into a delayed-clock shadow latch, raising an error flag register when the two captured bits disagree.

candidates.name: DICE radiation-hardened flip-flop
candidates.description: Stores one bit redundantly across four interlocked storage nodes so that a transient upset on a single node is restored by the others.

candidates.name: Metastability-hardened flip-flop
candidates.description: Captures one asynchronous input bit on the clock edge using a high-gain, fast-resolving storage cell designed to settle quickly from metastable states.

candidates.name: Sticky-bit flip-flop
candidates.description: Keeps one status bit that is set on the clock edge whenever an event input fires and stays set until an explicit clear input is applied.

candidates.name: Write-1-to-clear flip-flop
candidates.description: Holds one status bit set by a hardware event input and cleared on the clock edge when software writes a one to its bit position.

candidates.name: Write-1-to-toggle flip-flop
candidates.description: Holds one control bit that inverts on the clock edge whenever a register write delivers a one to its bit position and otherwise keeps its value.

candidates.name: Event-clocked capture flip-flop
candidates.description: Uses an asynchronous event signal as its clock so that the rising edge of the event latches a one or a data bit into its single stored bit until reset.

candidates.name: Load-enable parallel register
candidates.description: Captures an N-bit input word in parallel on a clock edge when its load enable is asserted, and otherwise keeps its stored word in a bank of D flip-flops.

candidates.name: Synchronous-reset register
candidates.description: Stores an N-bit word in flip-flops that are forced to a configured reset value on the clock edge when a synchronous reset input is active, and loads new data otherwise.

candidates.name: Asynchronous-reset register
candidates.description: Holds an N-bit word in flip-flops that return to their reset value as soon as an asynchronous reset is asserted, without waiting for a clock edge.

candidates.name: Parallel-in serial-out shift register
candidates.description: Loads a full word in parallel and then shifts it out one bit per clock on a serial output, keeping the partly shifted word in its flip-flop chain.

candidates.name: Serial-in serial-out delay register
candidates.description: Passes a serial bit stream through a chain of flip-flops so that each bit comes out a fixed number of cycles later, keeping the in-transit bits as its state.

candidates.name: Circular rotate register
candidates.description: Rotates its stored word left or right by one position per enabled clock, feeding the bit that falls off one end back into the other, and keeps the current rotated word.

candidates.name: Byte-enable register
candidates.description: Stores a multi-byte word and updates only the bytes whose write-strobe bits are set during a write, keeping the other bytes unchanged.

candidates.name: Write-one-to-clear status register
candidates.description: Holds status bits that hardware events set and that software clears by writing a 1 to the matching bit positions.

candidates.name: Write-one-to-set register
candidates.description: Keeps a word of control bits in which a software write of 1 sets the matching bits, while writes of 0 leave those bits as they are.

candidates.name: Read-to-clear register
candidates.description: Accumulates event bits or a count in flip-flops and returns its contents on a bus read, resetting them as a side effect of that read.

candidates.name: Sticky error register
candidates.description: Latches error or exception flags the first time each condition occurs and keeps them set until an explicit clear, storing one sticky bit per condition.

candidates.name: Set/clear/toggle alias register
candidates.description: Exposes one stored word through separate set, clear and toggle write addresses, so individual bits can be changed atomically without a read-modify-write.

candidates.name: Snapshot capture register
candidates.description: Copies the value of a live signal such as a running counter into a holding register when a trigger occurs, and keeps that captured value stable for later reading.

candidates.name: Tri-state bus register
candidates.description: Stores a word loaded from a shared bidirectional bus and drives it back onto the bus through tri-state buffers only while its output enable is active.

candidates.name: Ring counter
candidates.description: Circulates a single set bit through a closed loop of flip-flops, advancing one position per enabled clock, and stores the current token position as its state.

candidates.name: Bit-addressable register
candidates.description: Holds a word in which a single bit chosen by an index input can be set, cleared or written per cycle, while the remaining bits keep their values.

candidates.name: Lockable configuration register
candidates.description: Stores a configuration word together with a lock bit; once the lock is set, further writes to the word are ignored until reset.

candidates.name: Write-once register
candidates.description: Accepts the first write after reset into its data flip-flops, records that it has been written in a status flag, and ignores later writes.

candidates.name: Masked-write register
candidates.description: Updates its stored word using a write-data value and a per-bit mask supplied with each write, replacing only the masked bit positions.

candidates.name: Exchange register pair
candidates.description: Holds two words in separate registers that can each be loaded on their own or swapped with each other in a single clock cycle on a swap command.

candidates.name: Endian-swap register
candidates.description: Stores a multi-byte word and presents it on its output in either its natural or byte-reversed order, depending on an endianness control bit it also keeps.

candidates.name: Bypass register
candidates.description: Stores a word but can steer its input straight to its output through a bypass multiplexer when a bypass control is set, keeping the stored copy unchanged.

candidates.name: Hardware/software shared register
candidates.description: Keeps a word that can be written both by software over a bus and by internal hardware update logic, with a fixed priority choosing the winner when both write in the same cycle.

candidates.name: State-retention register
candidates.description: Pairs each main flip-flop with an always-powered shadow latch, saving the word before power-down and restoring it on power-up under save and restore controls.

candidates.name: Self-clearing command register
candidates.description: Lets software write command bits that stay high for exactly one clock to start an action and then clear themselves automatically, storing only the pending pulse bits.

candidates.name: Latch-based register
candidates.description: Stores a multi-bit word in level-sensitive latches that pass their input while the enable level is active and hold the last value when it goes inactive.

candidates.name: Serial-in serial-out delay line
candidates.description: Passes a serial bit stream through a chain of N flip-flops so each bit reappears N clocks later, keeping only the chain of stage registers.

candidates.name: Parallel-in parallel-out shift register
candidates.description: Captures a word in parallel and shifts it one position per clock while all stages remain visible as a parallel output, storing the word in an N-bit register.

candidates.name: Bidirectional shift register
candidates.description: Shifts its contents left or right by one position per clock under a direction control, taking new bits from the left or right serial input, and keeps an N-bit data register.

candidates.name: Rotate-through-carry register
candidates.description: Rotates a data word one position per clock through an extra carry flip-flop that sits between the two ends, storing the N-bit word plus the carry bit.

candidates.name: Addressable tap shift register
candidates.description: Shifts serial data through a chain of stages and outputs the stage selected by a tap address to give a run-time programmable delay, keeping the stage chain and the tap-select register.

candidates.name: Fall-through shift FIFO
candidates.description: Queues words in a column of stage registers where each entry moves toward the output whenever the stage ahead is empty, keeping per-stage data registers and per-stage occupied flags.

candidates.name: Nonlinear feedback shift register
candidates.description: Shifts a register by one position per clock and feeds back a nonlinear Boolean function of selected taps into the input to generate sequences, holding the N-bit state register.

candidates.name: Double-data-rate shift register
candidates.description: Shifts in serial data on both rising and falling clock edges into two interleaved stage chains that are merged into a parallel word, keeping a rising-edge chain and a falling-edge chain.

candidates.name: Word-wide lane shift register
candidates.description: Moves multi-bit words rather than single bits one stage per clock through a chain of word registers, keeping an array of word-wide stage registers.

candidates.name: Latched-output shift register
candidates.description: Shifts serial data into an internal shift stage and copies it to a separate output storage register on a latch strobe so outputs change only on update, keeping both the shift register and the storage latch register.

candidates.name: Bit-slip alignment register
candidates.description: Holds a window of incoming serial bits across two consecutive words and selects an output word at a slip offset that can be advanced one bit at a time to align word boundaries, keeping the window register and the slip-offset counter.

candidates.name: Sticky-bit right-shift register
candidates.description: Shifts a mantissa-style word right one position per clock while ORing every bit that falls off the low end into a sticky flip-flop, storing the data register and the sticky bit.

candidates.name: Sequential arithmetic shift register
candidates.description: Shifts a signed word right one position per clock while replicating the sign bit into the vacated top position, or left with zero fill, keeping an N-bit signed data register.

candidates.name: Thermometer-code shift register
candidates.description: Fills ones in from one end one position per clock on an increment and drains them from the same end on a decrement to represent a level as a thermometer code, keeping the N-bit thermometer register.

candidates.name: Global history shift register
candidates.description: Shifts each newly resolved outcome bit, such as a branch taken or not-taken result, into the low end of a register so the register holds the most recent N outcomes, storing the history bits.

candidates.name: Data/valid delay pipeline
candidates.description: Carries a data word together with its valid bit through a fixed number of stages one stage per clock to match the latency of a parallel path, keeping per-stage data and valid registers.

candidates.name: Pre-trigger capture shift register
candidates.description: Continuously shifts in samples of monitored signals and freezes on a trigger event so the history leading up to the trigger can be read out, keeping the sample chain and a frozen flag.

candidates.name: Majority-vote sample filter
candidates.description: Shifts the most recent N samples of a noisy input into a short register and drives a filtered output equal to the majority value of that window, keeping the sample window register and the registered output.

candidates.name: Bit-stuffing shift register
