candidates.description: Shifts out a serial stream and inserts an extra zero after a run of consecutive ones, stalling the input while it does so, keeping the outgoing shift register and a run-length counter of recent ones.

candidates.name: Manchester-encoding shift register
candidates.description: Shifts out data bits one per bit period and expands each into a two-half-period transition pattern on the line, keeping the data shift register and a half-bit phase flip-flop.

candidates.name: Two-dimensional shift matrix
candidates.description: Arranges registers in a grid where the whole array shifts one row or one column per clock under a mode control, keeping an R-by-C array of stage registers.

candidates.name: Sentinel-bit word assembler
candidates.description: Preloads a single marker bit at one end of a register and shifts serial data in behind it so a complete word is recognized when the marker reaches the far end, keeping the shift register including the marker position and a word-ready flag.

candidates.name: Asynchronous ripple counter
candidates.description: A chain of toggle flip-flops in which each stage is clocked by the previous stage's output, so the count advances in binary with ripple delay; its state is the bank of toggle flip-flops.

candidates.name: Synchronous binary up counter
candidates.description: Increments a binary count register by one on every enabled clock edge, using a common clock and parallel carry logic; it keeps a single N-bit count register.

candidates.name: Synchronous binary down counter
candidates.description: Decrements a binary count register by one on each enabled clock edge and signals a borrow when it passes zero; it keeps an N-bit count register.

candidates.name: Up/down counter
candidates.description: Increments or decrements its count register on each enabled clock depending on a direction input; it keeps the count register and optionally a registered direction bit.

candidates.name: Dual-clock up/down counter
candidates.description: Counts up on pulses from one clock input and down on pulses from a separate clock input, producing carry and borrow outputs; it keeps a count register and edge-capture flops for the two count inputs.

candidates.name: BCD decade counter
candidates.description: Steps a 4-bit register through decimal digits 0 to 9 and emits a carry when it rolls over to 0; it keeps one 4-bit BCD digit register.

candidates.name: Cascaded multi-digit BCD counter
candidates.description: Chains several decade stages so that each digit's rollover advances the next, giving a multi-digit decimal count; it keeps one 4-bit BCD register per digit.

candidates.name: Excess-3 counter
candidates.description: Steps through the ten excess-3 codes for decimal digits and produces a carry on wraparound; it keeps a 4-bit excess-3 code register.

candidates.name: Modulo-N counter
candidates.description: Counts from zero up to a programmed terminal value and then wraps back to zero, asserting a terminal-count output; it keeps a count register and a modulus register.

candidates.name: Presettable loadable counter
candidates.description: Counts normally but can be loaded in parallel with an arbitrary value from an input bus on a load strobe; it keeps a count register.

candidates.name: Auto-reload down counter
candidates.description: Counts down from a reload value and automatically reloads it upon reaching zero, pulsing an underflow output each cycle of the sequence; it keeps a count register and a reload register.

candidates.name: Cascadable counter slice
candidates.description: A fixed-width counter with count-enable-in and ripple-carry-out ports designed to be chained with identical slices into wider counters; it keeps its slice's count bits.

candidates.name: Pipelined split counter
candidates.description: Divides a wide counter into a low and a high segment with a registered carry between them so the high segment increments one cycle after the low segment wraps, enabling high clock rates; it keeps the low segment, the high segment and a carry pipeline flop.

candidates.name: One-hot ring counter
candidates.description: Circulates a single set bit around a closed shift register, advancing one position per clock to produce N decoded phases; it keeps an N-bit circular shift register.

candidates.name: Thermometer-code counter
candidates.description: Represents the count in unary by shifting ones into a register from one end on increment and removing them on decrement; it keeps an N-bit thermometer-coded register.

candidates.name: Dual-modulus prescaler
candidates.description: Divides an input pulse stream by either P or P+1 as selected by a mode control, used in front of slower counters; it keeps a small internal state counter and the registered mode select.

candidates.name: Pulse-swallow counter
candidates.description: Combines a dual-modulus prescaler with a program counter and a swallow counter to realize an overall division ratio of N times P plus S; it keeps the program count register and the swallow count register.

candidates.name: Mixed-radix counter
candidates.description: Advances a set of digits in which each digit has its own modulus (for example 60, 60, 24), carrying into the next digit on wraparound; it keeps one count register per digit.

candidates.name: Nested loop index counter
candidates.description: Generates multi-dimensional iteration indices by incrementing an inner index and advancing outer indices when inner ones reach their programmed bounds; it keeps one index register and one bound register per loop level.

candidates.name: Programmable stride counter
candidates.description: Adds a programmable step value to its count on each enabled clock instead of a fixed increment of one; it keeps a count register and a stride register.

candidates.name: Event counter with capture
candidates.description: Counts external events continuously and copies the running count into a capture register when a capture trigger arrives; it keeps a running count register and a captured-value register.

candidates.name: Compare-match counter
candidates.description: Runs a free counter and asserts a match output or interrupt whenever the count equals a programmed compare value; it keeps a count register, a compare register and a match flag.

candidates.name: Wrapping counter with sticky overflow
candidates.description: Increments freely and wraps on reaching its maximum, setting a sticky overflow flag that stays set until software clears it; it keeps a count register and an overflow flag bit.

candidates.name: Retriggerable one-shot counter
candidates.description: Produces an output pulse of a programmed number of clocks after a trigger, restarting the countdown if retriggered during the pulse; it keeps a down-count register and an output-active flag.

candidates.name: Arbitrary-sequence counter
candidates.description: Steps through a user-defined non-binary sequence of codes by looking up each next state in a small table indexed by the current state; it keeps a state register and a next-state lookup memory.

candidates.name: Half adder
candidates.description: Adds two single bits to produce a sum bit and a carry-out bit, purely combinationally with no stored state.

candidates.name: Full adder
candidates.description: Adds two operand bits plus a carry-in to produce a sum bit and a carry-out bit, combinationally with no registers.

candidates.name: Half subtractor
candidates.description: Subtracts one bit from another, producing a difference bit and a borrow-out bit, with no internal state.

candidates.name: Full subtractor
candidates.description: Subtracts a subtrahend bit and a borrow-in from a minuend bit, producing a difference and borrow-out, with no stored state.

candidates.name: Carry-skip adder
candidates.description: Splits a ripple chain into blocks whose group-propagate signals let the carry bypass whole blocks, holding no registers.

candidates.name: Conditional-sum adder
candidates.description: Recursively computes sums for both possible carry-ins at every level and selects with multiplexers as carries resolve, keeping no state.

candidates.name: Sklansky prefix adder
candidates.description: Computes carries with a divide-and-conquer parallel-prefix tree of minimal depth and high fan-out, purely combinationally.

candidates.name: Han-Carlson adder
candidates.description: Uses a hybrid prefix network that computes odd-bit carries in a sparse Kogge-Stone tree and fills even bits in a final stage, with no registers.

candidates.name: Ladner-Fischer adder
candidates.description: Builds its carry network from a parallel-prefix structure trading depth against fan-out between Sklansky and Brent-Kung styles, with no stored state.

candidates.name: Knowles adder
candidates.description: Uses a parallel-prefix carry tree with configurable fan-out per level to balance wiring and logic depth, holding no state.

candidates.name: Ling adder
candidates.description: Computes a simplified pseudo-carry signal in its lookahead logic and recovers true sums at the end to shorten the critical path, without registers.

candidates.name: Sparse-tree adder
candidates.description: Generates only every k-th carry with a prefix tree and feeds them to small carry-select blocks that form the sums, keeping no state.

candidates.name: Carry-increment adder
candidates.description: Computes each block's sum assuming zero carry-in and then conditionally increments it when the incoming block carry arrives, with no registers.

candidates.name: Manchester carry-chain adder
candidates.description: Propagates carries along a chain of pass-transistor switches controlled by per-bit propagate, generate and kill signals, with dynamic precharge nodes but no clocked registers.

candidates.name: Adder-subtractor
candidates.description: Adds or subtracts two operands under a mode control by XOR-inverting the second operand and feeding the mode bit as carry-in, also flagging carry and overflow, with no stored state.

candidates.name: Pipelined adder
candidates.description: Breaks a wide carry chain into segments separated by pipeline registers that hold partial sums, operand slices and inter-segment carries.

candidates.name: Digit-serial adder
candidates.description: Adds two operands several bits per clock cycle, keeping a carry flip-flop between digits and shift registers for the operand and sum digits.

candidates.name: 4:2 compressor
candidates.description: Reduces four operand bits plus a carry-in to a sum bit, a carry bit and a lateral carry-out for multi-operand addition, with no stored state.

candidates.name: Multi-operand adder tree
candidates.description: Sums many input words at once through a tree of two-input or compressor adders ending in a carry-propagate adder, optionally with pipeline registers between levels.

candidates.name: Incrementer
candidates.description: Adds one to an input word using a half-adder chain or prefix AND tree to form the carries, with no internal state.

candidates.name: Decrementer
candidates.description: Subtracts one from an input word by propagating a borrow through trailing zeros, with no internal registers.

candidates.name: End-around-carry adder
candidates.description: Adds two one's-complement operands and feeds the carry-out back into the least-significant carry-in, holding no state.

candidates.name: Signed-digit redundant adder
candidates.description: Adds two numbers in redundant signed-digit representation with carry propagation limited to adjacent digits, producing a redundant result without registers.

candidates.name: Excess-3 adder
candidates.description: Adds two excess-3 coded decimal digits using a binary adder and a correction stage that adds or subtracts three, with no stored state.

candidates.name: Sum-of-absolute-differences unit
candidates.description: Computes absolute differences of paired operand elements with subtractors and conditional negation and sums them, holding an accumulator register for the running total.

candidates.name: Dadda tree multiplier
candidates.description: Reduces the partial-product matrix with the minimum number of full and half adders at each column height stage, then uses a final carry-propagate adder; it keeps registered input operands and a registered product output.

candidates.name: Baugh-Wooley multiplier
candidates.description: Multiplies two's-complement operands in an array by inverting selected partial-product bits and adding correction constants so no sign extension is needed; it keeps operand input registers and a product output register.

candidates.name: Radix-2 Booth sequential multiplier
candidates.description: Examines one multiplier bit pair per cycle and adds, subtracts or skips the multiplicand into a running partial product; it keeps a multiplicand register, a combined accumulator/multiplier shift register, an extra Booth bit and an iteration counter.

candidates.name: Radix-8 Booth multiplier
candidates.description: Recodes the multiplier into overlapping 4-bit groups that select multiples from minus four to plus four times the multiplicand, so it generates one-third as many partial products; it keeps a precomputed triple-multiplicand register and pipeline registers between the recoding, reduction and final-add stages.

candidates.name: Serial-parallel multiplier
candidates.description: Takes one multiplier bit per clock against a parallel multiplicand and shifts the product out serially through a chain of carry-save adder cells; it keeps the parallel multiplicand register, per-cell sum and carry flops, and a bit counter.

candidates.name: Digit-serial multiplier
candidates.description: Processes the multiplier several bits per cycle, adding a digit-by-multiplicand product into a shifted accumulator; it keeps a multiplicand register, a multiplier digit shift register, an accumulator and a digit counter.

candidates.name: Karatsuba multiplier
candidates.description: Splits each operand into high and low halves and forms the product from three half-width multiplications plus additions and subtractions; it keeps registers for the three sub-products and the recombined output.

candidates.name: Toom-Cook multiplier
candidates.description: Splits operands into k limbs, evaluates them as polynomials at several points, multiplies the evaluations pointwise and interpolates the result; it keeps evaluation-point registers, pointwise-product registers and an interpolation accumulator.

candidates.name: Constant-coefficient CSD multiplier
candidates.description: Multiplies an input by a fixed constant using hardwired shifts and add/subtract operations derived from the constant's canonical-signed-digit form; it keeps an input register and an output product register.

candidates.name: Multiple-constant multiplier block
candidates.description: Computes the products of one input with a set of fixed coefficients through a shared shift-add graph that reuses intermediate terms; it keeps the input register and one output register per coefficient.

candidates.name: Squarer unit
candidates.description: Computes the square of a single operand using a folded partial-product array that merges symmetric terms to roughly halve the adder count; it keeps an operand register and a result register.

candidates.name: Pipelined array multiplier
candidates.description: Lays out the adder rows of an array multiplier as pipeline stages so a new operand pair can enter every cycle; it keeps inter-stage registers holding partial sums, carries and delayed operand bits, plus a valid bit per stage.

candidates.name: Carry-save iterative multiplier
candidates.description: Adds one partial product per cycle into a redundant sum/carry accumulator and runs a carry-propagate addition only at the end; it keeps sum and carry accumulator registers, a multiplier shift register and a step counter.

candidates.name: Mitchell logarithmic multiplier
candidates.description: Approximates a product by finding each operand's leading-one position, adding the approximated logarithms and taking an approximate antilogarithm; it keeps registers for the leading-one positions, the fractional mantissas and the approximate product.

candidates.name: Truncated fixed-width multiplier
candidates.description: Produces only the upper half of the product by omitting low-order partial-product columns and adding a compensation bias; it keeps operand registers and an n-bit result register.

candidates.name: Complex multiplier
candidates.description: Multiplies two complex numbers using three real multiplications and five additions in the Gauss arrangement; it keeps registers for the real and imaginary inputs, the intermediate products and the complex result.

candidates.name: Distributed-arithmetic multiplier
candidates.description: Computes a sum of products with fixed coefficients by using the input bits, one bit position per cycle, to address a precomputed table and shift-accumulating the outputs; it keeps the coefficient-sum ROM, input shift registers, an accumulator and a bit counter.

candidates.name: Quarter-square LUT multiplier
candidates.description: Forms a product as the difference of looked-up quarter-squares of the operand sum and difference; it keeps the quarter-square lookup ROM, sum and difference registers and a product register.

candidates.name: SIMD partitioned multiplier
candidates.description: Can be configured to perform one full-width multiply or several independent narrower lane multiplies by breaking carry and partial-product paths at lane boundaries; it keeps a mode register, operand registers and a lane-packed result register.

candidates.name: Vedic Urdhva multiplier
candidates.description: Generates all vertical and crosswise partial products of the operand digits in parallel and sums them column by column with carries, following the Urdhva-Tiryagbhyam scheme; it keeps operand registers and a result register.

candidates.name: Stochastic bitstream multiplier
candidates.description: Multiplies two probabilities encoded as random bitstreams by ANDing them bit by bit and counting the ones in the output stream; it keeps two stream-generator state registers, an output ones counter and a stream-length counter.

candidates.name: RNS channel multiplier
candidates.description: Multiplies operands held as residues modulo a set of co-prime moduli, with one independent modular multiplier per channel; it keeps per-channel residue input registers and per-channel residue product registers.

candidates.name: Systolic linear-array multiplier
candidates.description: Pipes multiplier bits through a one-dimensional chain of identical cells, each holding one multiplicand bit and adding into a passing partial sum; it keeps per-cell multiplicand bit, partial-sum, carry and control-token flops.

candidates.name: Tiled multi-precision multiplier
candidates.description: Builds a wide product by scheduling narrower hardware multiplies over operand limb pairs and accumulating them at the correct shifted offsets; it keeps limb index counters, operand limb buffers and a wide multi-word accumulator.

candidates.name: Interleaved modular multiplier
candidates.description: Computes A times B mod N by scanning B bit by bit, doubling and conditionally adding A to a partial result, then subtracting N when the partial result reaches or exceeds N; it keeps the A, B and modulus registers, a partial-result register and a bit counter.

candidates.name: Goldschmidt divider
candidates.description: Iteratively multiplies the dividend and divisor by the same correction factor until the divisor approaches one, keeping numerator, denominator, correction-factor and iteration-count registers.

candidates.name: Constant reciprocal-multiply divider
candidates.description: Divides by a fixed or preloaded divisor by multiplying with a stored magic reciprocal and shifting, holding the magic constant, shift amount and pipelined product registers.

candidates.name: Bit-serial divider
candidates.description: Computes a quotient from serially arriving operand bits using a one-bit subtractor per cycle, keeping a partial-remainder shift register, divisor register, borrow flip-flop and bit counter.

candidates.name: Combinational array divider
candidates.description: Computes quotient and remainder in a single combinational pass through rows of controlled subtract cells, with only optional input and output operand registers.

candidates.name: Non-performing divider
candidates.description: Performs a trial subtraction each cycle but writes the difference back only when it is non-negative, keeping partial-remainder, divisor, quotient and step-counter registers.

candidates.name: Pipelined unrolled divider
candidates.description: Spreads the digit-recurrence steps across pipeline stages so a new division can start every cycle, keeping per-stage partial-remainder, divisor, quotient-bits and valid registers.

candidates.name: Online MSB-first divider
candidates.description: Produces signed-digit quotient digits most-significant first after a small online delay as operand digits stream in, keeping redundant residual, accumulated operand and digit-position registers.

candidates.name: Modulo-by-constant reducer
candidates.description: Computes the remainder of a wide input modulo a fixed constant by folding chunks with precomputed weights, keeping a folded-residue accumulator and chunk index register.

candidates.name: Divide-by-three FSM
candidates.description: Computes the quotient and remainder of a serial binary stream divided by three using a small remainder-state register that also emits quotient bits into an output shift register.

candidates.name: Barrett reduction unit
candidates.description: Reduces a product modulo a fixed modulus by estimating the quotient with a precomputed scaled reciprocal and applying final correction subtractions, keeping modulus, reciprocal, quotient-estimate and residue registers.

candidates.name: GF(2) polynomial divider
candidates.description: Performs polynomial long division over GF(2) by XOR-shifting the divisor polynomial into the dividend, keeping a remainder register, divisor polynomial register, quotient shift register and degree counter.

candidates.name: Binary-field divider
candidates.description: Computes a/b in GF(2^m) using a binary extended-Euclid style iteration, keeping four polynomial registers for the working pairs, degree-difference register and iteration control state.

candidates.name: BCD decimal divider
candidates.description: Divides packed-BCD operands digit by digit using repeated decimal subtraction with multiples of the divisor, keeping a decimal partial-remainder, divisor-multiple table, quotient-digit and digit-position registers.

candidates.name: Early-termination normalizing divider
candidates.description: Normalizes operands with leading-zero counts to skip unnecessary iterations and finishes in a variable number of cycles, keeping shift-amount, partial-remainder, quotient, remaining-iterations and done registers.

candidates.name: Carry-save remainder divider
candidates.description: Holds the partial remainder in redundant carry-save form so each iteration avoids a full carry propagation, keeping sum and carry remainder registers, a divisor register and on-the-fly quotient conversion registers.

candidates.name: Signed division wrapper
candidates.description: Wraps an unsigned divide core with operand absolute-value conversion, sign recording, and quotient/remainder sign fix-up, keeping saved sign flags, divide-by-zero and overflow status registers.

candidates.name: Repeated-subtraction divider
candidates.description: Subtracts the divisor from the dividend once per cycle while incrementing a quotient counter, keeping a running-remainder register, divisor register and quotient counter.

candidates.name: Combined divide/square-root unit
candidates.description: Shares one digit-recurrence datapath for both division and square root, selecting the operation per request and keeping operation-mode, partial-remainder, root/quotient, divisor and iteration registers.

candidates.name: Prescaled digit-recurrence divider
candidates.description: Scales the divisor and dividend by a table-derived factor so quotient digits can be selected by simple rounding of the residual, keeping scale-factor, scaled-operand, residual and quotient registers.

candidates.name: Exact divider
candidates.description: Computes the quotient when the divisor is known to divide the dividend evenly using LSB-first modular-inverse multiplication, keeping the divisor inverse, working dividend and quotient shift registers.

candidates.name: Modular inverse unit
candidates.description: Computes the inverse of a value modulo an odd modulus using a binary extended-Euclidean iteration, keeping u, v, x1, x2 working registers, the modulus and a busy flag.

candidates.name: Mitchell logarithmic approximate divider
candidates.description: Approximates a quotient by converting operands to piecewise-linear logarithms, subtracting them and taking the antilogarithm, keeping leading-one position, mantissa-fraction and result registers.

candidates.name: Multi-word long divider
candidates.description: Divides multi-precision integers word by word with normalized quotient-digit estimation and add-back correction, keeping a scratch memory for the remainder words, divisor words, quotient words and word-index counters.

candidates.name: SIMD partitioned divider
candidates.description: Performs several independent narrow divisions in parallel lanes of one wide iterative datapath, keeping per-lane partial-remainder, divisor and quotient fields plus a lane-width mode register.

candidates.name: Table-lookup reciprocal approximation unit
candidates.description: Produces a low-precision reciprocal seed from a ROM indexed by leading divisor bits plus a linear interpolation term, keeping the ROM table, index register and interpolated output register.

candidates.name: Window comparator
candidates.description: Reports whether an input value lies between a lower and an upper bound, holding both bounds in programmable registers and latching the in-range result in an output flag register.

candidates.name: Hysteresis threshold comparator
candidates.description: Compares an input against separate rising and falling thresholds so the output changes only on a decisive crossing, keeping both threshold registers and a registered output-state bit.

candidates.name: MSB-first serial comparator
candidates.description: Compares two operands one bit per clock starting from the most significant bit, keeping a small decided/less-than/greater-than state register that freezes once the first differing bit is seen.

candidates.name: LSB-first serial comparator
candidates.description: Compares two operands one bit per clock starting from the least significant bit, overwriting a running relation register whenever the current bit pair differs so the final value reflects the most significant difference.

candidates.name: Mode-selectable signed/unsigned comparator
candidates.description: Produces less-than, equal and greater-than flags for two operands under either two's-complement or unsigned interpretation, with a mode register selecting the interpretation and a registered flag output.

candidates.name: Masked equality comparator
candidates.description: Tests two words for equality only on bit positions enabled by a programmable mask, storing the mask and reference pattern in registers and latching a match flag.

candidates.name: Min/max selector
candidates.description: Routes the smaller and the larger of two inputs to separate outputs using a single magnitude decision, holding the selected results in output registers.

candidates.name: Compare-exchange cell
candidates.description: Takes two keys with attached payloads and swaps them if they are out of order, registering the ordered key/payload pairs and a swapped flag for use as a node inside larger ordering structures.

candidates.name: Threshold crossing detector
candidates.description: Flags when a sampled signal crosses a programmed level and indicates the direction of the crossing, keeping the threshold register, the previous-sample register, and a crossing-event flag.

candidates.name: Hamming-distance threshold comparator
candidates.description: Counts the bit positions in which two words differ and compares that count to a programmable tolerance, holding the tolerance register and a registered near-match flag.

candidates.name: Memory-protection region checker
candidates.description: Compares an access address against several base/limit region pairs to decide whether it falls inside a permitted region, storing per-region base, limit and permission registers plus a registered fault flag.

candidates.name: Timer compare-match unit
candidates.description: Compares a free-running count against a programmed compare value and raises a match event when they are equal, keeping the compare register and a sticky match-pending flag.

candidates.name: Prefix-length matcher
candidates.description: Checks whether the leading N bits of an input address equal those of a stored prefix, where N comes from a prefix-length register, and stores the prefix and its length alongside a registered hit flag.

candidates.name: Lexicographic multi-word comparator
candidates.description: Orders two long keys by comparing them one word per cycle from the most significant word downward, keeping a word index counter and a running relation register until a difference or the end is reached.

candidates.name: Wraparound sequence-number comparator
candidates.description: Decides whether one modular sequence number is ahead of another using half-range serial-number arithmetic, holding a reference sequence register and a registered newer/older/equal result.

candidates.name: Tolerance comparator
candidates.description: Reports approximate equality when the absolute difference of two values does not exceed a programmable epsilon, storing the epsilon register and a registered within-tolerance flag.

candidates.name: Fraction cross-multiply comparator
candidates.description: Orders two ratios a/b and c/d by comparing the products a*d and c*b without performing division, holding the two product registers and a registered relation result.

candidates.name: Gray-code magnitude comparator
candidates.description: Determines the ordering of two Gray-coded values directly by scanning bits with a running parity that tracks inversion, keeping a registered relation output and no binary conversion stage.

candidates.name: BCD magnitude comparator
candidates.description: Compares two packed binary-coded-decimal numbers digit by digit from the most significant digit, registering the less-than/equal/greater-than result.

candidates.name: Carry-save sum-equality checker
candidates.description: Tests whether the sum of two operands equals a target value without a carry-propagating addition, using per-bit carry prediction logic, with the target held in a register and a latched equality flag.

candidates.name: Cascadable comparator slice
candidates.description: Compares a fixed-width nibble or byte of two operands and combines its result with less/equal/greater cascade inputs from a lower-order slice, optionally registering its cascade outputs for chaining wider compares.

candidates.name: Pipelined wide comparator
candidates.description: Splits a very wide comparison into chunks evaluated in parallel and merged over several pipeline stages, keeping per-stage registers of partial equal/greater results and a valid bit per stage.

candidates.name: Sign-magnitude comparator
candidates.description: Orders two sign-magnitude encoded numbers by handling the sign bits and then comparing magnitudes with order reversed for negatives, treating the two zero encodings as equal and registering the result.

candidates.name: Vector predicate comparator
candidates.description: Compares corresponding lanes of two packed vectors in parallel under a selected relation code and writes one result bit per lane into a predicate mask register, keeping the relation-select register as well.

candidates.name: FIFO watermark comparator
candidates.description: Compares a queue's fill level against programmable almost-full and almost-empty thresholds, storing both threshold registers and registered watermark status flags.

candidates.name: Bit-slice ALU
candidates.description: A cascadable 4-bit ALU slice that performs a function-selected arithmetic or logic operation on its operand nibbles and emits carry-generate, carry-propagate and zero outputs for chaining; it keeps an optional registered result nibble and carry-out flop.

candidates.name: SIMD packed ALU
candidates.description: Performs one selected add, subtract or logic operation in parallel on byte, halfword or word lanes of a wide operand, breaking carries at lane boundaries per a lane-size control; it keeps a result register and a per-lane flag vector register.

candidates.name: Accumulator-based ALU
candidates.description: Combines an incoming operand with an internal accumulator using a selected operation such as add, subtract, AND, OR or XOR and writes the result back; it keeps the accumulator register and a status register of carry, zero, negative and overflow flags.

candidates.name: Boolean function unit
candidates.description: Computes any of the sixteen two-input bitwise logic functions on two operands, choosing the function with a 4-bit truth-table code; it keeps a registered result and a zero flag.

candidates.name: Three-input ternary-logic unit
candidates.description: Applies an arbitrary 8-bit truth table bitwise across three operands to produce one result word in a single operation; it keeps the truth-table immediate register and the output register.

candidates.name: Rotate-through-carry unit
candidates.description: Rotates an operand left or right by one or more positions with the carry flag inserted as an extra bit in the rotation path; it keeps the carry flag register and the rotated result register.

candidates.name: Bit-field extract/insert unit
candidates.description: Extracts a field of given start position and width from a source word with zero or sign extension, or inserts a field into a destination word; it keeps position and width control registers and a result register.

candidates.name: Rotate-and-mask unit
candidates.description: Rotates an operand by a shift amount and then ANDs it with a mask generated from begin and end bit indices, optionally merging it into a destination; it keeps the mask-bounds registers and the result register.

candidates.name: Min/max unit
candidates.description: Selects the smaller or larger of two operands under signed or unsigned comparison according to an opcode; it keeps the selected result register and a flag recording which operand won.

candidates.name: Clamp unit
candidates.description: Bounds an input value between programmable lower and upper limits, outputting the limit when exceeded; it keeps the lower-limit, upper-limit and result registers plus a clipped status flag.

candidates.name: Conditional-select unit
candidates.description: Chooses between two operands based on a condition code evaluated against the current flags, implementing conditional move and select instructions; it keeps the selected result register.

candidates.name: Condition-code evaluator
candidates.description: Decodes a condition field such as equal, less-than or carry-set against stored N, Z, C and V flags to produce a single taken or true signal; it keeps the flags register that ALU operations update.

candidates.name: Address generation unit
candidates.description: Computes effective addresses as base plus scaled index plus displacement with optional base writeback for auto-increment modes; it keeps the computed address register and an alignment-fault flag.

candidates.name: Multi-precision add-with-carry unit
candidates.description: Adds or subtracts word-sized limbs of large integers over successive operations using the carry or borrow from the previous limb; it keeps the carry flag register between operations and a per-limb result register.

candidates.name: Byte-permute unit
candidates.description: Rearranges the bytes of one or two source words according to a selector vector to implement byte swap, broadcast and shuffle operations; it keeps the selector register and the permuted result register.

candidates.name: Increment/decrement unit
candidates.description: Adds or subtracts one or a small constant step from an operand with fast carry handling and produces zero and wrap flags; it keeps the result register and the flag bits.

candidates.name: Single-bit manipulation unit
candidates.description: Sets, clears, inverts or tests one bit of an operand selected by an index operand, producing the modified word and the tested bit as a flag; it keeps the result register and the test flag.

candidates.name: Halving average unit
candidates.description: Adds two operands with one extra bit of precision and shifts right by one, with selectable round-up or truncation, per lane; it keeps the averaged result register.

candidates.name: Flagged adder-subtractor
candidates.description: Adds or subtracts two operands under a mode bit by conditionally inverting the second operand and injecting carry-in, generating carry, overflow, zero and sign flags; it keeps the sum register and the four-flag status register.

candidates.name: Residue number system ALU
candidates.description: Performs addition, subtraction and multiplication independently in several small moduli channels with no carry between them; it keeps one residue register per modulus channel.

candidates.name: Stochastic computing ALU
candidates.description: Operates on random bitstreams whose density encodes values, using AND gates for multiplication and multiplexers for scaled addition, then counts output ones to recover a result; it keeps the output ones counter and a stream-length counter.

candidates.name: Bit-serial ALU
candidates.description: Executes add, subtract and logic operations one bit per clock on operands shifted in least-significant bit first, using a selected one-bit function; it keeps the operand and result shift registers and a carry flop.

candidates.name: SIMD compare-mask unit
candidates.description: Compares corresponding lanes of two packed operands for equal, greater-than or less-than and outputs an all-ones or all-zeros mask per lane plus a packed bitmask summary; it keeps the mask result register.

candidates.name: Vector reduction ALU
candidates.description: Combines all elements of a vector into one scalar by repeated application of a selected operation such as sum, min, max, AND or OR over multiple cycles; it keeps the partial-result register and an element index counter.

candidates.name: Logarithmic rotator
candidates.description: Rotates a word by any amount using log2(N) cascaded 2:1 mux stages, each stage rotating by a power of two, and holds the rotated word in an output register.

candidates.name: Bidirectional single-network rotator
candidates.description: Performs left or right rotation on one left-only rotate network by converting right amounts to their width complement, and keeps registered copies of the direction bit, amount and result.

candidates.name: Pipelined barrel shifter
candidates.description: Splits the shift stages across several clock stages for high frequency, and keeps the pipeline registers holding partially shifted data, remaining amount bits and a valid bit per stage.

candidates.name: Crossbar shifter
candidates.description: Decodes the shift amount to one-hot and drives an N-by-N switch matrix so every output bit selects its source in one level, with a registered one-hot select vector and output word.

candidates.name: Coarse-fine two-level shifter
candidates.description: Shifts first by whole bytes or words in a coarse stage and then by the residual bit count in a fine stage, and holds the intermediate coarse-shifted word in a register.

candidates.name: Bitfield extract unit
candidates.description: Right-shifts a source to bring a field of given offset and length to bit zero, then zero- or sign-fills the upper bits, and holds the offset, length and extracted-field registers.

candidates.name: Bitfield insert unit
candidates.description: Left-shifts a field to a given offset and merges it into a destination word under a generated mask, keeping the destination, field, offset and length registers.

candidates.name: Shifter operand unit with carry-out
candidates.description: Applies LSL, LSR, ASR or ROR by an immediate or register amount to an ALU operand and produces the last bit shifted out, keeping a registered shifted operand and shifter carry-out flag.

candidates.name: Floating-point alignment shifter
candidates.description: Right-shifts the smaller significand by the exponent difference and ORs all shifted-out bits into guard, round and sticky bits, holding the aligned significand and the GRS register.

candidates.name: Rounding right shifter
candidates.description: Shifts a fixed-point value right by a variable amount and adds a rounding increment derived from the dropped bits, keeping the shifted value and a registered rounding-mode setting.

candidates.name: Saturating left shifter
candidates.description: Shifts a signed value left by a variable amount and clamps to the most positive or negative value when significant bits would be lost, keeping the result register and a sticky saturation flag.

candidates.name: Overrange-clamping shifter
candidates.description: Treats shift amounts at or beyond the word width specially by forcing zero or sign-fill output instead of wrapping the count, and keeps the result plus an out-of-range indicator register.

candidates.name: SIMD lane-partitioned shifter
candidates.description: Shifts or rotates a wide word as independent 8-, 16- or 32-bit lanes by breaking cross-lane paths according to a lane-size setting, and holds the lane-mode register and per-lane results.

candidates.name: Byte-lane load aligner
candidates.description: Rotates a fetched memory word by the low address bits so the addressed byte, halfword or word lands at bit zero, then zero- or sign-extends it, holding the address offset and size registers and the aligned result.

candidates.name: Store data steering rotator
candidates.description: Rotates store data up to the byte position given by the address offset and generates matching byte-enable strobes, keeping registered aligned data and the byte-enable vector.

candidates.name: Stream byte realigner
candidates.description: Shifts incoming bus beats by a byte offset so a misaligned stream comes out aligned, carrying the leftover bytes of each beat in a residue register along with the current offset register.

candidates.name: Wide segmented shifter
candidates.description: Shifts a multi-word value by splitting it into segments that each shift locally and pass spill-over bits to their neighbor, keeping per-segment registers and the inter-segment spill registers.

candidates.name: QC-LDPC circulant shifter
candidates.description: Cyclically rotates a block of Z soft values by a per-entry shift taken from a parity-check base matrix for a configurable lifting size, keeping the lifting-size register, the shift-value ROM and the rotated block register.

candidates.name: Fixed multi-rotation XOR network
candidates.description: Computes the XOR of several constant-amount rotations and shifts of a word, as in hash sigma functions, in one cycle, and keeps only the input and output word registers.

candidates.name: Vector element slide unit
candidates.description: Moves whole elements of a vector register up or down by a scalar offset, filling vacated positions from a scalar or leaving them unchanged, and holds the offset register and destination element buffer.

candidates.name: Vector lane rotator
candidates.description: Rotates the elements of a vector across lanes by a variable element count in a single pass, keeping the element count, element-width setting and rotated vector registers.

candidates.name: Inverse-butterfly rotator
candidates.description: Implements arbitrary rotation through a log-depth inverse butterfly network whose per-stage swap controls are computed from the rotate amount, keeping the control-bit register and output register.

candidates.name: Reverse-shift-reverse shifter
candidates.description: Performs right shifts on left-only shift hardware by bit-reversing the input, shifting left and reversing the result, keeping a direction register and the registered output.

candidates.name: Fused multiply-add unit
candidates.description: Computes a*b+c with a single final rounding, keeping pipeline registers for the unrounded product, aligned addend, wide intermediate sum and the result sign and exponent.

candidates.name: Leading-zero anticipator
candidates.description: Predicts the normalization shift amount in parallel with mantissa addition from the two aligned operands, holding a registered indicator string and predicted shift count.

candidates.name: Alignment shifter with sticky generator
candidates.description: Right-shifts the smaller operand's significand by the exponent difference and ORs the shifted-out bits into guard, round and sticky bits held in an output register.

candidates.name: Exponent compare and operand swap unit
candidates.description: Subtracts the operand exponents, swaps the operands so the larger magnitude comes first, and registers the swapped significands, exponent difference and swap flag.

candidates.name: Near/far path adder selector
candidates.description: Routes a floating-point add to either a close path for small exponent differences with cancellation or a far path for large shifts, keeping both path result registers and a path-select bit.

candidates.name: Subnormal pre-normalizer
candidates.description: Detects subnormal inputs and left-shifts their significands while adjusting an extended-range exponent, storing the normalized significand, widened exponent and a subnormal flag per operand.

candidates.name: Floating-point classify unit
candidates.description: Examines a value's sign, exponent and fraction fields and outputs a registered category mask marking zero, subnormal, normal, infinity, signaling NaN or quiet NaN with sign.

candidates.name: NaN propagation and canonicalization unit
candidates.description: Selects which input NaN, if any, propagates to the result, quiets signaling NaNs or replaces them with a canonical NaN, and registers the chosen payload and an invalid indication.

candidates.name: Floating-point min/max unit
candidates.description: Returns the minimum or maximum of two operands with IEEE handling of signed zeros and NaNs, keeping a registered result and invalid-operation flag.

candidates.name: Sign-injection unit
candidates.description: Builds a result from one operand's magnitude and a sign taken, inverted or XORed from another operand, holding the output value in a result register.

candidates.name: Precision format converter
candidates.description: Converts between floating-point formats such as double, single, half and bfloat16 by rebiasing the exponent and rounding or extending the significand, storing the converted value and overflow, underflow and inexact flags.

candidates.name: Round-to-integral unit
candidates.description: Rounds a floating-point value to an integer-valued floating-point number under a selected rounding mode, holding the masked significand, increment bit and inexact flag in pipeline registers.

candidates.name: Exponent scaling unit
candidates.description: Adds a signed integer to a value's exponent to implement scaleB/ldexp with overflow and gradual-underflow handling, registering the adjusted exponent, shifted significand and status flags.

candidates.name: Exception flag accumulator
candidates.description: Collects invalid, divide-by-zero, overflow, underflow and inexact indications from completing operations and ORs them into a sticky status register that software can read and clear.

candidates.name: Rounding mode control register
candidates.description: Holds the dynamic rounding-mode field and per-instruction override decode, supplying the effective rounding mode to the arithmetic pipelines from a small configuration register.

candidates.name: Underflow tininess detector
candidates.description: Determines whether a result is tiny before or after rounding by evaluating the unbounded-exponent result, keeping registered tininess, exactness and underflow-flag outputs.

candidates.name: Stochastic rounding unit
candidates.description: Rounds a significand up or down with probability proportional to the discarded fraction by comparing those bits against a random value, keeping a pseudorandom state register and a rounded-output register.

candidates.name: Goldschmidt divide/square-root unit
candidates.description: Iteratively multiplies numerator and denominator by convergence factors to compute quotients or square roots, keeping numerator, denominator and factor registers plus an iteration counter.

candidates.name: Reciprocal square-root estimate unit
candidates.description: Produces a low-precision 1/sqrt(x) seed from a lookup table indexed by exponent parity and leading significand bits, storing the table ROM and a registered estimate.

candidates.name: Floating-point log2 approximation unit
candidates.description: Computes log2 of a floating-point input by taking the unbiased exponent as the integer part and a table-plus-polynomial evaluation of the significand, holding coefficient ROM and partial-result pipeline registers.

candidates.name: Floating-point exp2 unit
candidates.description: Computes 2^x by splitting x into integer and fractional parts, evaluating the fractional power from a table and polynomial, and placing the integer part into the exponent, with coefficient ROM and staged registers.

candidates.name: Horner polynomial evaluator
candidates.description: Evaluates a polynomial approximation of a transcendental function by repeated fused multiply-adds, keeping a coefficient memory, a running accumulator register and a degree counter.

candidates.name: Kulisch exact accumulator
candidates.description: Accumulates floating-point products exactly into a very wide fixed-point register spanning the full exponent range, keeping that long accumulator and a final round-to-float output register.

candidates.name: Interleaved floating-point accumulator
candidates.description: Hides adder latency by rotating additions across several partial-sum registers selected by a slot counter and reducing them into one sum at the end of a sequence.

candidates.name: Packed SIMD floating-point adder
candidates.description: Performs several narrow-precision floating-point additions in parallel by splitting a wide datapath into lanes, keeping per-lane exponent, significand and flag registers plus a lane-mode configuration register.

candidates.name: Traffic light controller
candidates.description: Cycles an intersection through green, yellow and red phases for each road, holding the current phase in a state register and a dwell timer counting down the time remaining in that phase.

candidates.name: Vending machine controller
candidates.description: Accepts coin inputs, tracks deposited value in a credit register and the transaction step in a state register, and issues vend and change-return outputs when a selection is made.

candidates.name: Elevator controller
candidates.description: Moves a car between floors by serving pending calls, keeping a current-floor register, a direction bit, a pending-request bit vector and a door-state register.

candidates.name: Combination lock FSM
candidates.description: Compares keypad digits against a stored code one at a time, holding a digit-position register, a failed-attempt counter and a lockout timer.

candidates.name: Keypad matrix scanner
candidates.description: Drives keypad columns one at a time and samples the rows to identify a pressed key, keeping a column-index register, a scan-phase state and a latched key-code register.

candidates.name: Manchester encoder
candidates.description: Converts each data bit into a mid-bit transition pattern, keeping a half-bit phase register and the currently held data bit.

candidates.name: HDLC bit-stuffing inserter
candidates.description: Inserts a zero after a run of consecutive ones in an outgoing bitstream, holding a ones-run counter and a stall flag that marks the cycle used for the inserted bit.

candidates.name: Exponential backoff controller
candidates.description: Schedules retransmission after collisions in a shared-medium protocol, holding a collision-attempt counter, a randomly loaded backoff slot counter and a waiting/transmitting state.

candidates.name: Link training state machine
candidates.description: Steps a serial link through detect, polling, configuration and active states, keeping a state register, a timeout counter and a count of consecutive training sequences received.

candidates.name: Multi-rail power-up sequencer
candidates.description: Enables supply rails in a fixed order with delays and power-good checks, holding a step-index register, an inter-step delay counter and a fault state.

candidates.name: DRAM initialization sequencer
candidates.description: Issues the power-up command sequence (reset, clock-enable, mode-register writes, ZQ calibration) to a memory device, keeping a command-index register and a wait-cycle counter.

candidates.name: PLL lock detector
candidates.description: Declares a clock loop locked or unlocked by watching phase-error samples, keeping a lock state bit and a counter of consecutive in-window samples.

candidates.name: Frame delineation synchronizer
candidates.description: Finds frame boundaries in a serial stream by moving through hunt, presync and sync states, holding the state register plus counters of consecutive good and bad frame headers.

candidates.name: Ethernet auto-negotiation arbiter
candidates.description: Exchanges capability pages with a link partner and selects a common operating mode, keeping a negotiation state register, a link timer and a received-abilities register.

candidates.name: I2C bus recovery FSM
candidates.description: Frees a stuck I2C bus by toggling the clock line until the data line is released and then issuing a stop, holding a pulse counter and a recovery-phase state register.

candidates.name: Transaction retry controller
candidates.description: Reissues a failed bus or network request up to a limit, keeping an outstanding-request state, a retry counter and a response-timeout timer.

candidates.name: Token ring station controller
candidates.description: Captures, holds and forwards a circulating token on a ring network, keeping a token-held flag, a token-hold timer and a transmit/repeat state register.

candidates.name: Battery charge controller
candidates.description: Moves a charger through precharge, constant-current, constant-voltage and done phases based on measured voltage and current, keeping a phase register and a safety timer.

candidates.name: Hysteresis thermostat FSM
candidates.description: Switches a heater or fan on and off around a setpoint with separate on and off thresholds, keeping an output-state bit and the programmed threshold registers.

candidates.name: Appliance cycle sequencer
candidates.description: Runs a timed program of steps such as fill, wash, drain and spin, holding a program-step register, a step timer and a paused flag.

candidates.name: Startup calibration sequencer
candidates.description: Steps an analog block through trim codes and compares measurements at each step to pick the best setting, keeping a step register, a candidate trim register and a best-result register.

candidates.name: LED pattern sequencer
candidates.description: Plays a stored sequence of light patterns, holding a pattern-index register, a dwell counter for the current pattern and a loop-mode flag.

candidates.name: Morse code decoder
candidates.description: Classifies on/off durations into dots, dashes and gaps and assembles characters, keeping a duration counter, a symbol shift register and a symbol-count register.

candidates.name: Serial two's-complementer
candidates.description: A Mealy machine that negates a number fed in least-significant bit first by passing bits through until the first one and then inverting, holding a single seen-first-one state bit.

candidates.name: Serial divisibility-by-3 checker
candidates.description: Reads a binary number most-significant bit first and reports whether the value so far is a multiple of three, holding a two-bit remainder state register.

candidates.name: Banked register file
candidates.description: Splits the architectural registers across several single- or dual-ported SRAM banks selected by register-index bits, holding the register values in per-bank arrays plus a bank-conflict detect register for the current cycle.

candidates.name: Windowed register file
candidates.description: Exposes a sliding window of in, local and out registers over a large circular physical array, keeping the register contents together with a current-window-pointer and a window-invalid mask used to trigger spill and fill traps.

candidates.name: Rotating register file
candidates.description: Renames a region of registers by adding a rotating register base to each index on every loop iteration for software pipelining, storing the register array and the rotating base offset.

candidates.name: Unified physical register file
candidates.description: Holds all speculative and committed values of an out-of-order core in a large multi-ported array indexed by physical tag, along with a per-entry ready bit read by the wakeup logic.

candidates.name: Vector register file
candidates.description: Stores wide vector registers sliced into lanes, each lane with its own read and write ports feeding a vector ALU lane, plus per-register element-length configuration state.

candidates.name: Predicate register file
candidates.description: Holds a small set of one-bit or per-element mask registers written by compare instructions and read to guard execution or lane enables.

candidates.name: Matrix tile register file
candidates.description: Holds two-dimensional tiles of rows by columns accessed row-wise for loads and stores and as whole operands by a matrix engine, keeping the tile data and a per-tile shape configuration register.

candidates.name: Mode-banked shadow register file
candidates.description: Provides duplicate copies of selected registers for privileged or fast-interrupt modes, switching the visible copy on mode change, and keeps both the shared and mode-private register arrays plus the current mode field.

candidates.name: Multithreaded context register file
candidates.description: Replicates the full architectural register set once per hardware thread and selects a context with a thread-ID field each cycle, storing every thread's registers in a single array indexed by thread and register number.

candidates.name: Operand-collector register file
candidates.description: Serves a GPU's many warps from single-ported banks by buffering requested operands in collector units until all sources arrive, keeping the banked register array, collector entry buffers and per-operand valid bits.

candidates.name: Register file cache
candidates.description: Places a small, heavily ported cache of recently written or soon-to-be-read values in front of a large main register file, storing cached values with their register tags and replacement state.

candidates.name: Replicated register file
candidates.description: Achieves many read ports by keeping several identical copies of the register array, each with a subset of the read ports, all receiving every write.

candidates.name: Live-value-table register file
candidates.description: Builds a multi-write-port memory from one bank per write port and a small live-value table recording which bank last wrote each address, used to steer each read to the correct bank.

candidates.name: XOR-based multi-port register file
candidates.description: Implements multiple write ports by storing in each write port's bank the XOR of the new data with the other banks' contents, so a read XORs all banks at an address to recover the latest value.

candidates.name: Latch-based register file
candidates.description: Uses level-sensitive latches with clock-gated write enables instead of flip-flops for each register word, storing the data in latch rows plus a write-data staging register.

candidates.name: Write-through bypassed register file
candidates.description: Forwards data written in the current cycle directly to any read port that addresses the same register, keeping the register array and a captured copy of the incoming write address and data.

candidates.name: Clustered register file
candidates.description: Partitions registers between execution clusters, each with a local register file and a small number of inter-cluster copy ports, storing per-cluster register arrays and a pending cross-cluster transfer queue.

candidates.name: Checkpointed register file
candidates.description: Takes shadow snapshots of the register state at branch points so it can restore on misprediction, keeping the active register array plus several checkpoint copies and a checkpoint-allocation mask.

candidates.name: Future file
candidates.description: Maintains the most recent speculative value of each architectural register for fast operand reads alongside a separate in-order architectural copy, keeping both arrays and per-register pending-writer tags.

candidates.name: Retirement register file
candidates.description: Holds the committed architectural register values written only when instructions retire from the reorder buffer, plus a per-register flag indicating whether the latest value currently lives in the reorder buffer.

candidates.name: Stack-organized register file
candidates.description: Addresses registers relative to a top-of-stack pointer as in an x87-style floating-point unit, storing the register array, the top pointer and a per-register tag word marking empty or valid slots.

candidates.name: Belt register file
candidates.description: Replaces named destinations with a fixed-length queue of recent results addressed by position from the front, storing the belt slots and a head index advanced as each result drops onto it.

candidates.name: DSP address register file
candidates.description: Holds address, index and modifier registers for a digital signal processor's address generation units, including base and length registers that support circular buffer and bit-reversed addressing.

candidates.name: Deferred-exception tagged register file
candidates.description: Stores each general register together with a not-a-thing poison bit set by speculative loads that faulted, so later consumers can propagate or check the deferred exception.

candidates.name: Uniform scalar register file
candidates.description: Holds values shared by all threads of a GPU warp in a narrow separate array with its own read ports, storing per-warp scalar registers used for addresses, constants and loop counters.

candidates.name: Asynchronous-read distributed RAM
candidates.description: A small flip-flop or LUT-based memory array written on the clock edge but read combinationally, so the addressed word appears without a clock delay; it keeps only the storage array.

candidates.name: Byte-enable write RAM
candidates.description: A synchronous RAM whose write port takes a per-byte enable mask so only selected byte lanes of the addressed word are updated; it keeps the data array and a registered read-data output.

candidates.name: Bit-mask write RAM
candidates.description: A RAM that accepts a full-width write mask so individual bits of a word can be updated while the rest keep their old values; it keeps the data array and an output register.

candidates.name: Registered-output pipelined RAM
candidates.description: A synchronous RAM with an extra output pipeline register so read data emerges two cycles after the address, improving clock speed; it keeps the array, an address register and the output data register.

candidates.name: Dual-clock simple dual-port RAM
candidates.description: A RAM with a write port in one clock domain and a read port in another, used to pass data between domains; it keeps the array plus per-domain address and read-data registers.

candidates.name: Asymmetric-width RAM
candidates.description: A RAM whose write and read ports have different data widths, such as writing 8-bit words and reading 32-bit words, with address mapping between the two aspect ratios; it keeps the shared array and per-port registers.

candidates.name: Quad-port RAM
candidates.description: A memory array offering two independent read ports and two independent write ports each cycle; it keeps the storage array and per-port address and data registers.

candidates.name: Live-value-table multi-write RAM
candidates.description: A multi-write-port memory built from one bank per write port plus a small table recording which bank last wrote each address, steering reads to the newest copy; it keeps the replicated banks and the live-value table.

candidates.name: XOR-encoded multi-port RAM
candidates.description: A multi-write-port memory where each write port stores its data XORed with the other banks' contents so a read recovers the latest value by XORing all banks; it keeps several encoded bank arrays.

candidates.name: Double-pumped time-multiplexed RAM
candidates.description: A single-port physical array clocked at twice the system rate to present two logical ports per system cycle; it keeps the array, a phase toggle and holding registers for each logical port's request and result.

candidates.name: Banked interleaved RAM
candidates.description: A memory split into several independent banks selected by low address bits so concurrent accesses to different banks proceed in parallel; it keeps the bank arrays and per-bank request and output registers.

candidates.name: Read-modify-write RAM with bypass
candidates.description: A RAM that reads a word, applies an operation such as increment or OR, and writes it back, forwarding in-flight results to back-to-back accesses on the same address; it keeps the array, pipeline stage registers and a bypass address/data register.

candidates.name: Counter memory
candidates.description: A RAM where each word is a counter and a single command increments or adds to the addressed entry in a pipelined fashion, as used for statistics; it keeps the counter array and pipeline holding registers.

candidates.name: Flash-clear valid-bit RAM
candidates.description: A RAM paired with a flip-flop array of per-entry valid bits that can all be cleared in one cycle, making reads of uncleared entries return a default; it keeps the data array and the valid-bit vector.

candidates.name: Epoch-tagged RAM
candidates.description: A RAM where each word stores a generation tag and a global epoch register is bumped to logically invalidate all contents at once; it keeps the data-plus-tag array and the current epoch register.

candidates.name: Zero-initializing RAM
candidates.description: A RAM with a built-in sequencer that sweeps every address writing zeros after reset or on request before accepting normal traffic; it keeps the array, a sweep address counter and an init-busy flag.

candidates.name: RAM-based delay line
candidates.description: A circular RAM written and read at addresses a fixed offset apart to delay a sample stream by many cycles; it keeps the array and a single rolling address counter.

candidates.name: Checkpoint shadow RAM
candidates.description: A RAM duplicated into a working copy and a shadow copy, where a snapshot command records which copy holds committed data so state can be rolled back; it keeps both arrays and a per-entry or global copy-select register.

candidates.name: Paged RAM with bank register
candidates.description: A RAM larger than the address bus can reach, accessed through a window whose upper address bits come from a programmable page register; it keeps the array and the page register.

candidates.name: Auto-increment burst RAM
candidates.description: A RAM with an internal address counter loaded once and then advanced on every access so streams of words can be read or written without supplying addresses; it keeps the array, the address counter and a burst length register.

candidates.name: Bit-addressable RAM
candidates.description: A RAM that, besides word access, supports an alias region in which each address maps to a single bit of an underlying word for atomic bit set and clear; it keeps the word array and a read-modify-write staging register.

candidates.name: Dirty-bit tracking RAM
candidates.description: A RAM that sets a per-block dirty flag whenever any word in that block is written so software can find modified regions; it keeps the data array and a dirty-bit array.

candidates.name: Retention-mode low-power RAM
candidates.description: A RAM wrapper with active, light-sleep and retention modes that gates access and periphery power while preserving contents; it keeps the array, a power-mode register and a wake-up delay counter.

candidates.name: Address-scrambled RAM
candidates.description: A RAM that passes addresses through a keyed permutation and optionally XORs data with a keyed mask to obscure physical layout; it keeps the array and the scrambling key registers.

candidates.name: Posted-write RAM
candidates.description: A synchronous RAM front end that accepts a write into a one-entry pending-write register and commits it to the array on a later idle cycle, matching reads against the pending entry; it keeps the array and the pending address, data and valid registers.

candidates.name: Quarter-wave sine ROM
candidates.description: Stores one quadrant of a sine wave and uses address folding and sign inversion logic to return full-period sine or cosine samples, keeping the quadrant table and an optional registered output word.

candidates.name: FFT twiddle factor ROM
candidates.description: Holds precomputed complex exponential coefficients indexed by butterfly stage and position, keeping real and imaginary coefficient tables and a registered coefficient output pair.

candidates.name: FPGA k-input LUT cell
candidates.description: Implements any Boolean function of k inputs by using the inputs as a mux select into a configuration memory of 2^k bits loaded at configuration time, with an optional output flip-flop.

candidates.name: Reciprocal seed table
candidates.description: Maps the leading mantissa bits of a divisor to an initial reciprocal approximation for iterative refinement, keeping the seed table and a registered seed output.

candidates.name: Inverse square-root seed table
candidates.description: Returns a coarse 1/sqrt(x) estimate indexed by exponent parity and leading mantissa bits, keeping separate even- and odd-exponent seed tables and an output register.

candidates.name: Log2 lookup table
candidates.description: Converts a normalized mantissa fragment into a fixed-point base-2 logarithm fraction, keeping the logarithm table and a pipeline register for the combined integer-plus-fraction result.

candidates.name: Antilog (exp2) lookup table
candidates.description: Converts a fixed-point fractional exponent into a mantissa of 2^f for log-domain arithmetic, keeping the exponential table and a registered mantissa output.

candidates.name: Piecewise-linear interpolating LUT
candidates.description: Selects a segment from the upper input bits, fetches that segment's base value and slope, and multiplies-and-adds with the lower bits to interpolate, keeping base and slope tables plus pipeline registers.

candidates.name: Bipartite table function unit
candidates.description: Approximates a smooth function by adding outputs of a coarse table-of-initial-values and a smaller table-of-offsets indexed by different input bit fields, keeping both tables and the sum register.

candidates.name: Boot ROM with lockout
candidates.description: Supplies the first-stage boot code to the processor after reset and can be hidden from the address map by a sticky disable bit, keeping the code image and the lockout register.

candidates.name: AES S-box ROM
candidates.description: Implements the byte substitution nonlinearity of a block cipher as a 256-entry byte table, keeping the forward (and optionally inverse) substitution tables and a registered output byte.

candidates.name: Filter coefficient ROM
candidates.description: Delivers fixed tap weights to a filter datapath in tap order as an index counter advances, keeping the coefficient table and the tap index register.

candidates.name: Distributed-arithmetic LUT
candidates.description: Stores all precomputed partial sums of fixed filter coefficients addressed by one bit-slice of each input sample, keeping the partial-sum table and a shift-accumulate register for the bit-serial result.

candidates.name: Programmable logic array
candidates.description: Generates sum-of-products outputs from a programmable AND plane feeding a programmable OR plane, keeping the configuration bits of both planes and optionally registered outputs.

candidates.name: Color palette LUT
candidates.description: Translates indexed pixel values into full RGB colors for display, keeping a host-writable palette memory and a registered color output.

candidates.name: Table-driven CRC lookup
candidates.description: Advances a CRC by a whole byte per cycle by indexing a 256-entry remainder table with the XOR of the incoming byte and the current CRC high byte, keeping the remainder table and the running CRC register.

candidates.name: Arbitrary waveform wavetable
candidates.description: Plays back a user-loaded sample memory addressed by the upper bits of a phase accumulator, keeping the waveform memory, the phase accumulator, and the frequency tuning word register.

candidates.name: Device identification ROM
candidates.description: Exposes read-only vendor, part, revision, and feature-capability words at fixed register addresses, keeping the hardwired ID constants and a read-data output register.

candidates.name: Sensor linearization calibration LUT
candidates.description: Corrects nonlinear raw sensor codes into calibrated values using a per-device table written at factory trim, keeping the calibration table and a registered corrected output.

candidates.name: ROM patch unit
candidates.description: Compares fetch addresses against a set of patch address registers and substitutes replacement words when a slot matches, keeping the patch address registers, replacement data registers, and per-slot enable bits.

candidates.name: Galois-field log/antilog ROM
candidates.description: Performs GF(2^m) multiplication and division by looking up discrete logarithms, adding or subtracting them modulo 2^m-1, and looking up the antilog, keeping the log table, antilog table, and an exponent sum register.

candidates.name: Constant-coefficient LUT multiplier
candidates.description: Multiplies a variable input by a fixed constant by splitting the input into nibbles that each index a table of precomputed constant multiples and summing the shifted results, keeping the multiple tables and an adder pipeline register.

candidates.name: Quarter-square multiplier table
candidates.description: Computes a product as the difference of two table lookups of floor(n^2/4) indexed by the sum and difference of the operands, keeping the square table and the result register.

candidates.name: CORDIC arctangent constant ROM
candidates.description: Provides the per-iteration angle constants atan(2^-i) to a rotation datapath indexed by the iteration counter, keeping the angle table and the iteration index register.

candidates.name: Constellation mapper ROM
candidates.description: Maps groups of coded bits to in-phase and quadrature amplitude levels for a selected modulation scheme, keeping I and Q level tables per modulation and a modulation-select register.

candidates.name: Wrap-bit pointer FIFO
candidates.description: Buffers words in a circular RAM using write and read pointers that each carry one extra wrap bit, keeping only the two extended pointers and the storage array, with no separate occupancy counter.

candidates.name: Shift-register FIFO
candidates.description: Stores entries in a chain of registers that all shift toward the output on each pop, with new data written at the position given by a fill-level register.

candidates.name: Fall-through bubble FIFO
candidates.description: Passes each word stage by stage through a chain of data registers, each with its own valid bit, until it reaches the first occupied slot near the output.

candidates.name: First-word-fall-through FIFO
candidates.description: Wraps a RAM-based FIFO with an output prefetch register and its valid flag so the head word is visible on the output before a read is requested.

candidates.name: Gray-pointer asynchronous FIFO
candidates.description: Moves data between two clock domains through a dual-port RAM, keeping binary and Gray-coded write and read pointers in their own domains plus synchronized copies of the opposite pointer.

candidates.name: Handshake-synchronized dual-clock FIFO
candidates.description: Crosses clock domains by transferring binary pointer snapshots through a request/acknowledge toggle exchange, holding the local pointers, snapshot holding registers and toggle flags on each side.

candidates.name: Token-ring mixed-clock FIFO
candidates.description: Implements a dual-clock queue as a ring of cells, each with a data register and full/empty bit, where one-hot put and get tokens circulate to select the active cell in each domain.

candidates.name: Mesochronous FIFO
candidates.description: Absorbs a fixed but unknown phase offset between two same-frequency clocks with a small register ring, a write pointer and a read pointer started at a fixed initial separation.

candidates.name: Micropipeline asynchronous FIFO
candidates.description: Forms a clockless queue from a chain of latch stages controlled by Muller C-elements, each stage holding a data latch and a request/acknowledge phase state.

candidates.name: Programmable-watermark FIFO
candidates.description: Adds configurable almost-full and almost-empty threshold registers to a FIFO and keeps registered flags that update when the fill level crosses those thresholds.

candidates.name: Commit/rollback packet FIFO
candidates.description: Supports store-and-forward packet buffering by keeping a speculative write pointer alongside a committed write pointer so a partially written packet can be accepted or discarded at its end.

candidates.name: Asymmetric-width FIFO
candidates.description: Accepts words of one width and delivers words of a different width, keeping a storage array, pointers at the narrow granularity and a sub-word lane index for packing or unpacking.

candidates.name: Overwrite-oldest ring buffer
candidates.description: Continuously records incoming data into a circular array and advances the read pointer past the oldest entry when the array fills, keeping write and read pointers and an overflow flag.

candidates.name: Multi-push FIFO
candidates.description: Accepts several words per cycle through multiple write ports into banked storage, keeping a write pointer that advances by the number of words written and a single read pointer.

candidates.name: Multi-pop FIFO
candidates.description: Delivers up to several consecutive head entries per cycle from banked storage, keeping a read pointer that advances by the number of words consumed and a write pointer.

candidates.name: Peekable lookahead FIFO
