candidates.description: Lets the consumer read any of the first several queued entries by offset without dequeuing them, keeping the storage array, head and tail pointers and a peek-offset input path.

candidates.name: Linked-list shared-buffer multi-queue
candidates.description: Holds several logical FIFOs in one shared memory, keeping per-queue head and tail pointers, a next-pointer link array and a free-cell list.

candidates.name: Virtual output queue set
candidates.description: Keeps a separate FIFO for each output destination at an input port so blocked traffic for one destination does not hold up others, with per-queue pointers and nonempty flags.

candidates.name: Multicast multi-reader FIFO
candidates.description: Lets several consumers read the same written stream at their own pace, keeping one write pointer, a per-reader read pointer, and the shared storage array.

candidates.name: Replay retransmission buffer
candidates.description: Holds transmitted frames until acknowledged so they can be resent, keeping a write pointer, an acknowledged pointer, a replay pointer and a replay-active flag.

candidates.name: Clock-compensation elastic buffer
candidates.description: Bridges a recovered receive clock and a local clock in a serial link by inserting or deleting skip symbols, keeping a circular data array, write and read pointers and skip-insert/delete control flags.

candidates.name: Collapsing queue
candidates.description: Allows entries to be removed from any position while remaining entries shift down to close the gaps, keeping an ordered array of entry registers each with a valid bit.

candidates.name: Double-ended queue
candidates.description: Supports push and pop at both the head and the tail of a circular buffer, keeping front and back pointers and the storage array.

candidates.name: Timestamped delay queue
candidates.description: Holds each entry with a release time and lets the head leave only once a free-running time counter reaches that time, keeping per-entry data and timestamp fields, pointers and the time counter.

candidates.name: Hybrid flop-SRAM cascaded FIFO
candidates.description: Combines a small register FIFO in front of and behind a large SRAM FIFO to hide RAM latency, keeping the head and tail flop stages, the SRAM pointers and a bypass-select state.

candidates.name: Longest-prefix-match engine
candidates.description: Stores prefix/length entries in parallel comparators and returns the address of the matching entry with the longest prefix, keeping a prefix array, a length array and per-entry valid bits.

candidates.name: Range-match CAM
candidates.description: Compares a search key against stored lower and upper bounds in every entry at once and reports which entries contain the key, keeping low-bound registers, high-bound registers and valid bits.

candidates.name: Precomputation-filter CAM
candidates.description: Stores a small precomputed signature such as a ones-count beside each key so that only entries with a matching signature run the full compare, keeping key, signature and valid arrays.

candidates.name: Banked hierarchical CAM
candidates.description: Splits entries into banks chosen by a few key bits and searches only the selected bank in parallel, keeping per-bank key arrays, valid bits and a bank-occupancy register.

candidates.name: Multi-match bitmap CAM
candidates.description: Returns a full bitmap of every entry that matches the search key instead of a single address, keeping key storage, valid bits and a registered match-vector output.

candidates.name: Key-value associative memory
candidates.description: Searches stored keys in parallel and on a hit reads out the paired data word, keeping a key array, a value array, valid bits and a registered hit/data result.

candidates.name: Sorted-array binary-search CAM emulator
candidates.description: Emulates CAM lookup by keeping keys sorted in RAM and running a multi-cycle binary search, holding the sorted key RAM, an entry count and low/high/mid search pointers.

candidates.name: SRAM bit-slice CAM emulator
candidates.description: Splits the key into slices that each index a RAM of per-entry match vectors and ANDs the vectors to find matches, keeping one match-vector table per slice and a valid-entry mask.

candidates.name: Hamming-distance approximate CAM
candidates.description: Counts mismatched bits between the search key and every stored entry in parallel and flags entries within a programmable distance, keeping key storage, valid bits and a threshold register.

candidates.name: Nearest-neighbor associative memory
candidates.description: Computes a distance from the query to every stored vector and returns the address of the closest one, keeping the vector array, valid bits and registered best-index and best-distance values.

candidates.name: Global-mask search CAM
candidates.description: Applies a programmable search mask so selected key bits are ignored across all entries during a lookup, keeping a key array, valid bits and a global mask register.

candidates.name: Age-stamped CAM
candidates.description: Attaches an insertion timestamp to each entry so the oldest match or oldest entry can be chosen for reporting or eviction, keeping key, timestamp and valid arrays plus a global time counter.

candidates.name: Round-robin replacement CAM
candidates.description: Fully associative lookup table that writes new keys into the slot named by a rotating insertion pointer, keeping key storage, valid bits and the insertion-pointer register.

candidates.name: Tag-broadcast wakeup array
candidates.description: Compares broadcast result tags against the source-operand tags of waiting entries in parallel and sets their ready bits on a match, keeping source tag fields, ready bits and entry valid bits.

candidates.name: Pipelined CAM
candidates.description: Splits the key comparison across pipeline stages so each stage narrows a partial match vector, keeping the key array, valid bits and per-stage partial-match and key registers.

candidates.name: Multi-port search CAM
candidates.description: Runs two or more independent key searches against the same entry set in one cycle, keeping a shared key array, valid bits and a separate match-result register for each port.

candidates.name: Searchable FIFO
candidates.description: An in-order queue whose entries can also be searched in parallel by content to report the position of a matching element, keeping entry data, valid bits and head/tail pointers.

candidates.name: Layer-2 MAC learning table
candidates.description: Learns source addresses with their ingress ports and looks up destination addresses in parallel to return a port, keeping MAC keys, port fields, valid bits and per-entry aging bits refreshed on hits.

candidates.name: Flow match table with hit counters
candidates.description: Matches packet header fields against stored flow keys and returns the matching rule while bumping that rule's packet and byte counters, keeping key, action, counter and valid arrays.

candidates.name: Sliding-window string-match CAM
candidates.description: Shifts an input byte stream through a window register and compares it against all stored patterns in parallel each cycle, keeping the pattern array, pattern valid bits and the window shift register.

candidates.name: Bit-serial associative processor
candidates.description: Searches all words in parallel one bit column at a time, narrowing a per-word response tag, keeping the word array, a comparand register, a mask register and the response-tag register.

candidates.name: Outstanding transaction ID CAM
candidates.description: Records the IDs of issued bus transactions and finds the matching slot when a response returns, keeping ID fields, per-slot metadata and allocated bits.

candidates.name: Heavy-hitter counting CAM
candidates.description: Looks up incoming keys in parallel, increments the count of a matching entry or replaces the lowest-count entry on a miss, keeping key, count and valid arrays.

candidates.name: Search-and-update CAM
candidates.description: Performs a parallel search and in the same operation overwrites the data or flags of the matching entry, keeping key and data arrays, valid bits and a pending-update register.

candidates.name: Bidirectional associative map
candidates.description: Holds paired fields that can each be searched in parallel, so a lookup by either key or value returns the address and the partner field, keeping two content arrays and valid bits.

candidates.name: Fully-associative cache
candidates.description: Stores lines in any entry by comparing the request address against every stored tag in parallel, keeping per-entry tag, valid, dirty and data registers plus replacement state.

candidates.name: Sector cache
candidates.description: Shares one address tag across several sub-blocks of a line, keeping one tag per sector and separate valid and dirty bits per sub-block so that sub-blocks can be filled independently.

candidates.name: Skewed-associative cache
candidates.description: Indexes each way with a different hash of the address to spread conflicting lines, keeping per-way tag, valid and data arrays along with the hash function configuration.

candidates.name: Column-associative cache
candidates.description: Probes a primary set and then a rehashed alternate set in a direct-mapped array, keeping tag and data arrays plus a per-line rehash bit that records which index function placed the line.

candidates.name: Write-back eviction buffer
candidates.description: Holds dirty lines evicted from the cache until they drain to the next memory level, keeping entries of victim address, data and valid flags that later requests can match against.

candidates.name: Write-combining buffer
candidates.description: Merges multiple partial stores to the same line into one burst write, keeping a line address, data bytes and a per-byte write mask for each entry.

candidates.name: MESI line state controller
candidates.description: Updates a cache line's coherence state on local reads, writes and incoming snoops, keeping a two-bit Modified/Exclusive/Shared/Invalid state per line and issuing bus or interconnect requests.

candidates.name: Snooping bus cache controller
candidates.description: Watches the shared bus for other masters' transactions, looks up their addresses in a duplicate tag copy and supplies data, invalidates or downgrades lines, keeping the duplicate tags and a pending-snoop register.

candidates.name: Way predictor
candidates.description: Guesses which way of a set-associative cache will hit so that only one data way needs to be read, keeping a table of predicted way numbers indexed by address or PC bits.

candidates.name: Next-line prefetcher
candidates.description: Issues a fetch for the line following each demand miss, keeping the last miss address and a small queue of outstanding prefetch addresses.

candidates.name: Stream buffer
candidates.description: Prefetches sequential lines after a miss into a small FIFO beside the cache and supplies them on later misses, keeping the stream head address, entry tags, valid bits and line data.

candidates.name: Loop buffer
candidates.description: Captures the instructions of a short backward-branching loop so that fetch can replay them without accessing the instruction cache, keeping instruction entries, the loop start and end addresses, and a capture or replay mode flag.

candidates.name: Trace cache
candidates.description: Stores dynamic instruction sequences that span taken branches as single lines, keeping per-line start address, branch outcome flags, instruction slots and the next fetch address.

candidates.name: Micro-op cache
candidates.description: Caches decoded micro-operations keyed by instruction fetch address so the decoders can be bypassed, keeping tag, valid, micro-op slot and replacement registers for each way.

candidates.name: Random replacement unit
candidates.description: Selects a victim way pseudo-randomly on each fill, keeping a free-running pseudo-random state register and a mask of ways eligible for replacement.

candidates.name: Round-robin replacement pointer
candidates.description: Chooses victims in a fixed rotating order within each set, keeping a per-set next-victim way pointer that advances on every fill.

candidates.name: RRIP replacement unit
candidates.description: Predicts how soon each line will be reused and evicts a line predicted to be reused far in the future, keeping a small re-reference prediction counter per line that ages when no candidate is found.

candidates.name: LFU replacement unit
candidates.description: Evicts the least frequently accessed line in a set, keeping a per-line access-frequency counter that increments on hits and is periodically halved.

candidates.name: Set-dueling policy monitor
candidates.description: Dedicates a few sample sets to each of two replacement or insertion policies and steers the remaining sets toward the policy that misses less, keeping a policy-selection counter and the sample-set designations.

candidates.name: Dead-block predictor
candidates.description: Predicts when a cached line will not be referenced again so it can be evicted early or bypassed, keeping a table of signature-indexed confidence counters and a per-line signature field.

candidates.name: Cache maintenance engine
candidates.description: Walks the cache by set and way to clean, invalidate or flush lines on software command, keeping current set and way index registers, the operation type and a busy status bit.

candidates.name: Cache lockdown controller
candidates.description: Pins selected lines or ways so they are excluded from replacement, keeping a way-lock mask register and per-line lock bits set by software.

candidates.name: Way-partitioning controller
candidates.description: Restricts which cache ways each requester or quality-of-service class may allocate into, keeping a per-class allocation way-mask register file.

candidates.name: Inclusive back-invalidation unit
candidates.description: Sends invalidations to upper-level caches whenever the lower-level inclusive cache evicts a line, keeping a queue of pending back-invalidate addresses and per-line presence bits for the upper caches.

candidates.name: Cache ECC scrubber
candidates.description: Periodically reads cache lines in the background, corrects single-bit errors and writes the corrected data back, keeping a scrub address pointer, an interval timer and error count registers.

candidates.name: FR-FCFS DRAM command scheduler
candidates.description: Picks the next DRAM command from a pending request queue, favoring row-buffer hits and then the oldest request, and keeps per-entry age stamps, target bank/row fields and a ready mask.

candidates.name: Open-row bank state table
candidates.description: Tracks for each DRAM bank whether a row is open and which row it is, holding a per-bank valid bit and open-row address register used to classify requests as hit, miss or conflict.

candidates.name: DRAM timing constraint tracker
candidates.description: Gates ACT, RD, WR and PRE issue per bank using countdown timers for tRCD, tRP, tRAS, tRC and tWR, loaded on each command and decremented every cycle.

candidates.name: Four-activate window (tFAW) tracker
candidates.description: Limits row activations per rank by holding timestamps of the most recent four ACT commands in a small circular history and a pointer to the oldest one.

candidates.name: Bus turnaround controller
candidates.description: Inserts read-to-write, write-to-read and rank-to-rank gaps on the shared data bus, keeping the last command type, last rank ID and turnaround countdown registers such as tWTR and tRTW.

candidates.name: DDR initialization sequencer
candidates.description: Drives the power-up sequence of reset deassertion, CKE enable, mode register writes, ZQ init and DLL lock waits, holding a step index and a wait-cycle counter.

candidates.name: Mode register programming unit
candidates.description: Issues MRS/MRW commands that load CAS latency, burst length, ODT and drive-strength settings into the DRAM, keeping shadow copies of each mode register and a pending-update flag set.

candidates.name: Physical address mapper
candidates.description: Splits a system address into channel, rank, bank group, bank, row and column fields with optional XOR bank hashing, holding configurable field-position and hash-mask registers.

candidates.name: Write-drain watermark controller
candidates.description: Switches the scheduler between read mode and write-drain mode based on write queue occupancy, holding high and low watermark registers and a current-mode flag.

candidates.name: Read-after-write hazard detector
candidates.description: Compares incoming read addresses against pending entries in the write queue and forwards or stalls on a match, keeping an address/byte-mask array of queued writes and a match vector.

candidates.name: Read response reorder buffer
candidates.description: Returns DRAM read data to the requester in original order despite out-of-order scheduling, storing data beats in tagged slots with a per-slot filled flag and an in-order retire pointer.

candidates.name: Adaptive page-close timer
candidates.description: Precharges idle open rows after a programmable idle interval, keeping a per-bank idle counter and a timeout register adjusted by observed hit and conflict counts.

candidates.name: Power-down and self-refresh controller
candidates.description: Puts ranks into precharge power-down or self-refresh after sustained idleness and wakes them on demand, holding idle counters, the current low-power state per rank and exit-latency timers.

candidates.name: ZQ calibration scheduler
candidates.description: Periodically issues ZQ short calibration commands to retune DRAM output impedance, keeping an interval counter, a calibration-in-progress flag and a blocking-period timer.

candidates.name: Temperature-compensated refresh adjuster
candidates.description: Polls the DRAM temperature status mode register and scales the refresh interval, holding the last read temperature code, a poll timer and the active refresh-rate multiplier.

candidates.name: Row-hammer activation counter table
candidates.description: Counts activations to recently used rows and triggers targeted neighbor-row refreshes when a threshold is reached, keeping a small table of row addresses with per-row activate counters.

candidates.name: Write leveling training engine
candidates.description: Sweeps DQS output delay relative to CK during write leveling mode and samples the DRAM feedback on DQ, keeping a delay tap register, sampled result history and the found-edge setting per byte lane.

candidates.name: Read DQS gate training unit
candidates.description: Searches for the correct receive-enable window for the read strobe by stepping coarse and fine delay settings, holding current delay taps, pass/fail records and the chosen gate setting per lane.

candidates.name: Read eye centering unit
candidates.description: Sweeps per-bit DQ capture delays against a known pattern to find the left and right eye edges, storing edge tap registers and the computed center delay for each data bit.

candidates.name: DFI PHY interface aligner
candidates.description: Translates controller commands and write data onto the DFI interface with programmed write-latency and read-enable delays, keeping latency configuration registers and delay pipelines for command and data-enable signals.

candidates.name: Command/address parity retry unit
candidates.description: Computes parity on each issued command and address, logs commands in a replay history and re-issues them after the DRAM signals a parity alert, holding the history buffer, a replay pointer and an error status register.

candidates.name: Data bus inversion encoder
candidates.description: Inverts a byte lane on write when more than half its bits would be driven low and restores data on read, keeping the per-lane DBI flag registers for the current beat.

candidates.name: Memory patrol scrubber
candidates.description: Walks all memory addresses in the background issuing reads so ECC can correct and rewrite latent errors, holding the current scrub address, a rate interval timer and a corrected-error count.

candidates.name: Asynchronous SRAM/NOR bus controller
candidates.description: Generates chip-select, output-enable and write-enable strobes with programmable setup, access and hold wait states for external parallel memories, keeping per-chip-select timing registers and a phase counter.

candidates.name: HyperBus/PSRAM controller
candidates.description: Serializes requests into command-address phases, latency waits and DDR data bursts for HyperRAM or OctalSPI PSRAM, honoring the maximum chip-select low time, and holds latency configuration, a burst byte counter and a CS-low duration timer.

candidates.name: Odd-ratio 50% duty divider
candidates.description: Divides a clock by an odd integer with a symmetric output by combining a rising-edge modulo counter with a falling-edge retimed copy, keeping the count register and the rising- and falling-edge phase flops.

candidates.name: Half-integer clock divider
candidates.description: Produces a clock at the input frequency divided by N.5 by alternating edge selection between rising and falling input edges, keeping a modulo counter and an edge-select toggle bit.

candidates.name: Fractional-N modulus controller
candidates.description: Generates a per-cycle divide-ratio sequence whose average equals an integer plus a fraction using a multi-stage sigma-delta modulator, keeping the integer and fraction setting registers and the modulator accumulator registers.

candidates.name: Rational M/N clock-enable generator
candidates.description: Emits an enable pulse on exactly M of every N input cycles using a Bresenham-style error accumulator, keeping the M and N configuration registers and the running error register.

candidates.name: Ripple toggle-flop divider chain
candidates.description: Divides a clock by successive powers of two through a cascade of toggle flip-flops, each clocked by the previous stage, with each stage's toggle flop as its state.

candidates.name: Programmable divider with shadowed ratio
candidates.description: Divides a clock by a software-set ratio that only takes effect at a period boundary, keeping a shadow ratio register, an active ratio register and the period counter.

candidates.name: Quadrature clock generator
candidates.description: Derives four clocks spaced 90 degrees apart by dividing a 2x or 4x input clock through a twisted-ring of flops, keeping those phase flops as its state.

candidates.name: Multi-output phase-offset clock generator
candidates.description: Produces several divided clocks from one source, each with its own programmable phase offset relative to a shared cycle counter, keeping the shared counter and per-output divide and offset registers.

candidates.name: Phase-frequency detector
candidates.description: Compares reference and feedback clock edges and asserts UP or DOWN pulses proportional to their phase difference, keeping the UP and DN flops that are cleared together by a reset path.

candidates.name: Bang-bang phase detector
candidates.description: Samples the reference clock with the feedback clock (or vice versa) to produce a single early/late decision per cycle, keeping the sampling flop and a registered early/late output.

candidates.name: Digitally controlled oscillator control word
candidates.description: Converts a tuning code into enables for capacitor or inverter banks in a digitally controlled ring or LC oscillator, keeping the coarse, medium and fine tuning code registers.

candidates.name: DCO band calibration engine
candidates.description: Selects the coarse frequency band of a digitally controlled oscillator by successive-approximation search against a reference count, keeping the trial code register, the bit-position pointer and the measured count.

candidates.name: Frequency-locked loop counter comparator
candidates.description: Counts oscillator cycles over a fixed reference window and nudges the oscillator code up or down toward a target count, keeping the cycle counter, the window timer, the target register and the oscillator code.

candidates.name: PLL startup sequencer
candidates.description: Steps a PLL through power-up, band calibration, loop closure and lock wait before releasing the output clock, keeping a sequence state register and a settle-time counter.

candidates.name: Spread-spectrum clock modulator
candidates.description: Periodically sweeps a PLL's fractional divide setting along a triangular profile to spread the clock's spectral energy, keeping the profile step counter, direction bit and current offset register.

candidates.name: Missing-clock detector
candidates.description: Watches a monitored clock with a counter running on an independent clock and flags a failure when no monitored edge arrives within a timeout, keeping the timeout counter, a synchronized edge-toggle sample and a failure flag.

candidates.name: Clock failover switch controller
candidates.description: Automatically moves the system clock from a primary to a backup source when the primary is reported failed, keeping a selected-source register, a switch-in-progress flag and a sticky failover status bit.

candidates.name: Ring oscillator clock source
candidates.description: Generates a free-running clock from an odd chain of inverters gated by an enable, keeping only the enable register and a trim register selecting the chain length.

candidates.name: Edge-combining frequency doubler
candidates.description: Produces a clock at twice the input frequency by XORing the input with a delayed copy of itself, keeping a delay-select register that sets the output pulse width.

candidates.name: Clock pulse swallower
candidates.description: Removes selected cycles from a clock stream according to a programmed skip pattern to lower its effective frequency, keeping the pattern register, a pattern position counter and the gating latch.

candidates.name: Adaptive clock stretcher
candidates.description: Lengthens the next clock cycles when a supply-droop detector fires and restores normal period afterward, keeping a stretch-active flag, a recovery counter and a stretch-amount register.

candidates.name: Clock burst generator
candidates.description: Emits exactly N clock pulses on request and then holds the output idle, keeping the requested-count register, a remaining-pulse counter and a burst-active flag.

candidates.name: Single-bit level synchronizer
candidates.description: Passes a slowly changing level signal into a destination clock domain through a chain of back-to-back flip-flops, keeping only the stage registers of that chain.

candidates.name: Toggle pulse synchronizer
candidates.description: Converts a source-domain pulse into a toggle of a source register, synchronizes that toggle through destination flops, and XORs the last two stages to regenerate a destination pulse.

candidates.name: Two-phase (NRZ) handshake synchronizer
candidates.description: Signals transfers by toggling a request register in the sender and an acknowledge register in the receiver, each synchronized into the opposite domain through flop chains.

candidates.name: Mux-recirculation data synchronizer
candidates.description: Holds a multi-bit bus in a source register and synchronizes only a load-enable bit, which selects a destination capture register to load the bus or recirculate its current value.

candidates.name: MCP bus synchronizer with acknowledge feedback
candidates.description: Launches a held data word with a toggled enable, synchronizes the enable to capture the word in the destination, and returns a synchronized acknowledge toggle that frees the source holding register.

candidates.name: Feedback pulse synchronizer with busy
candidates.description: Forwards an event pulse across domains via a toggle, returns a synchronized acknowledge, and keeps a source-side busy register that blocks new pulses until the round trip completes.

candidates.name: Asynchronous FIFO flag generator
candidates.description: Compares a local pointer with a synchronized copy of the remote Gray pointer to produce registered full, empty, almost-full and almost-empty flags, keeping the synchronizer stages and flag registers.

candidates.name: Gray-coded event counter synchronizer
candidates.description: Counts source-domain events in a Gray-coded counter register, synchronizes it into the destination, and converts it back to binary in a destination register to obtain the event total.

candidates.name: Clock-gate enable synchronizer
candidates.description: Synchronizes a gating request into the target clock domain and latches it on the inactive clock phase so the integrated clock gate receives a stable enable, keeping the sync flops and the enable latch.

candidates.name: Metastability-detecting synchronizer
candidates.description: Samples an asynchronous input in parallel flops and flags disagreement between the main and a shadow sampling register, keeping both sample registers and an error-flag register.

candidates.name: Mesochronous phase-select synchronizer
candidates.description: Captures data from a same-frequency, unknown-phase clock into two alternately clocked registers and uses a calibrated phase-select register to pick the safe one for the receiver.

candidates.name: Ratiochronous transfer-window scheduler
candidates.description: For clocks with a known rational frequency ratio, uses a phase counter register to predict safe sampling edges and enables direct transfers only within those windows.

candidates.name: Sticky status bit synchronizer with clear handshake
candidates.description: Latches asynchronous status events into a sticky register in the source domain, synchronizes it to software's domain, and clears it via a synchronized clear-request toggle.

candidates.name: Quasi-static configuration synchronizer
candidates.description: Holds configuration values in a shadow register written in one domain and copies them to an active register in another domain when a synchronized update strobe arrives.

candidates.name: Snapshot capture synchronizer
candidates.description: On a destination request toggle, freezes a source-domain running value into a snapshot register and returns a completion toggle so the destination can safely read the frozen value.

candidates.name: Pulse-pending counter synchronizer
candidates.description: Accumulates bursts of fast-domain pulses in a pending counter and drains them one at a time through a handshake into a slower domain, keeping the counter and handshake toggle registers.

candidates.name: Asynchronous-set wakeup synchronizer
candidates.description: Uses a flop asynchronously set by an external wake event with no clock running, then synchronizes it into the newly started clock domain and clears it on a synchronized acknowledge.

candidates.name: Cross-domain register access bridge
candidates.description: Carries bus read/write transactions between domains by holding address, write data and read data in registers and exchanging request and response toggles through synchronizers.

candidates.name: Clock-presence detector
candidates.description: Toggles a register in a monitored clock domain and synchronizes it into a reference domain, where a timeout counter flags when no toggles have been observed.

candidates.name: Token-ring pointer FIFO synchronizer
candidates.description: Implements a dual-clock FIFO whose read and write positions are one-hot token rings, with the tokens synchronized across domains to detect full and empty conditions.

candidates.name: Source-synchronous input capture
candidates.description: Samples incoming data with a forwarded clock into capture registers and writes them into a small dual-clock buffer read by the local clock, keeping capture flops and buffer slots.

candidates.name: Johnson-code pointer synchronizer
candidates.description: Encodes a short FIFO or sequence pointer as a Johnson (twisted-ring) code register and synchronizes it through flop chains into the other domain for decoding.

candidates.name: Pausible clock controller
candidates.description: Stretches or pauses a local ring-oscillator clock while an asynchronous handshake is resolved by a mutual-exclusion element, keeping the clock-enable state and the handshake latch.

candidates.name: Mutual-exclusion request arbiter
candidates.description: Resolves two asynchronous requests with a cross-coupled latch followed by a metastability filter, holding which requester currently owns the shared resource.

candidates.name: Multi-domain reset sequencer
candidates.description: Releases resets to several domains in a programmed order with configurable delays, keeping a step index, a delay counter and a per-domain reset-asserted register.

candidates.name: Reset cause recorder
candidates.description: Captures which source triggered the most recent reset (power-on, brown-out, watchdog, software, pin), holding sticky cause flags in an always-on register that software reads and clears.

candidates.name: Software reset control block
candidates.description: Exposes per-peripheral reset bits that software sets and clears to hold or release individual blocks, keeping a reset-control register and an optional self-clearing pulse timer.

candidates.name: Reset glitch filter
candidates.description: Rejects short spurious pulses on an external reset pin by requiring the input to stay asserted for a minimum time, keeping a sample counter and a filtered reset output flop.

candidates.name: Reset escalation controller
candidates.description: Promotes repeated local fault resets to a broader subsystem or chip-wide reset, keeping a fault occurrence counter, an escalation level register and a decay timer.

candidates.name: Warm reset quiesce handshaker
candidates.description: Before applying a warm reset it requests bus masters to drain and blocks new transactions, keeping a quiesce-request flag, per-port idle acknowledgment bits and a timeout counter.

candidates.name: Reset domain crossing gate
candidates.description: Clamps signals leaving a domain that is in reset so they do not corrupt a domain still running, keeping a registered reset-state indicator and the clamp-enable flop.

candidates.name: Brown-out detector filter
candidates.description: Digitally qualifies a comparator's low-voltage indication and raises a brown-out event or reset, keeping a debounce counter, a threshold-select register and a brown-out status flag.

candidates.name: Power-good qualifier
candidates.description: Synchronizes and validates power-good signals from regulators before letting dependent logic proceed, keeping per-rail synchronizer flops, stability counters and a qualified-good register.

candidates.name: State retention controller
candidates.description: Sequences save and restore strobes to retention flip-flops around a power-down, keeping a retention phase register, a save-done flag and a restore-pending flag.

candidates.name: SRAM low-power mode controller
candidates.description: Drives memory macros between active, light-sleep, deep-sleep (retention) and shutdown modes, keeping the current mode register, a target mode register and a wake-up settle counter.

candidates.name: Staggered power-switch enabler
candidates.description: Turns on power-switch segments of a domain one group at a time to limit in-rush current, keeping a segment index, an inter-step delay counter and the switch-enable shift chain.

candidates.name: Power mode state machine
candidates.description: Moves the chip among run, idle, sleep and deep-sleep modes on software and wake requests, keeping the current power mode, a pending request register and per-mode configuration registers.

candidates.name: Wake-up event controller
candidates.description: Collects wake sources such as GPIO edges, timers and interrupts during sleep, keeping a wake-enable mask, a sticky wake-pending register and edge-polarity configuration bits.

candidates.name: Always-on wake timer
candidates.description: Counts on a slow always-on clock to wake the system after a programmed interval, keeping a running counter, a compare register and a wake-fired flag.

candidates.name: Low-power interface channel controller
candidates.description: Implements a request/accept/deny low-power handshake (Q-channel/P-channel style) with a device before cutting its clock or power, keeping the channel state, requested power state and accept/deny status.

candidates.name: Idle-based auto power-down unit
candidates.description: Watches a block's activity and requests clock or power removal after a programmable idle period, keeping an idle counter, a threshold register and a power-down-requested flag.

candidates.name: Power domain dependency tracker
candidates.description: Keeps parent domains powered while any child domain or requester needs them, holding per-domain usage reference counts and a domain-on vector.

candidates.name: Adaptive voltage scaling monitor
candidates.description: Measures silicon speed with replica-path or ring-oscillator counts and requests voltage up or down steps, keeping a measurement counter, target margin registers and the last adjustment code.

candidates.name: Voltage ramp sequencer
candidates.description: Steps a regulator setpoint gradually from current to target voltage at a programmed slew rate, keeping the current setpoint code, the target code and a step interval timer.

candidates.name: Power capping throttle controller
candidates.description: Estimates power from activity counters and throttles issue rate or clock frequency to stay within a budget, keeping an accumulated energy estimate, a budget register and a throttle level.

candidates.name: Voltage droop response unit
candidates.description: Reacts to a fast supply-droop alert by briefly stretching or skipping clock pulses, keeping a droop event latch, a stretch duration counter and an event occurrence counter.

candidates.name: Body-bias controller
candidates.description: Selects forward or reverse well bias levels per domain for speed or leakage trade-offs and sequences transitions, keeping the bias mode register, a target level code and a settle timer.

candidates.name: Power-switch acknowledge monitor
candidates.description: Tracks the daisy-chained acknowledge returning from a domain's power switches and reports when the domain is fully on or off, keeping the ack synchronizer flops, a domain status register and a timeout counter.

candidates.name: Debug power request handler
candidates.description: Holds selected power domains on and blocks sleep while an external debugger requests access, keeping a debug power-up request register, a per-domain keep-alive mask and an acknowledgment flag.

candidates.name: Matrix arbiter
candidates.description: Grants the least-recently-served requester by consulting an N-by-N priority matrix of flip-flops, updating the winner's row and column after each grant.

candidates.name: Weighted round-robin arbiter
candidates.description: Cycles through requesters in turn but lets each hold the grant for several consecutive slots, keeping a rotating pointer, per-requester weight registers and a remaining-slots counter.

candidates.name: Deficit round-robin scheduler
candidates.description: Serves variable-size requests in rotation by adding a quantum to each requester's deficit counter per round and granting while the head request fits, keeping per-requester deficit registers and a round pointer.

candidates.name: Lottery arbiter
candidates.description: Picks a winner randomly in proportion to programmable ticket counts, holding per-requester ticket registers and an LFSR that supplies the random draw.

candidates.name: Age-based oldest-first arbiter
candidates.description: Grants the requester that has waited longest, keeping a saturating wait-age counter per requester that increments while pending and resets on grant.

candidates.name: FIFO queuing arbiter
candidates.description: Grants requesters in the order their requests arrived, recording arriving requester IDs in a small order queue with head and tail pointers.

candidates.name: Programmable priority arbiter
candidates.description: Selects the pending requester with the highest software-assigned priority level, keeping a writable priority register for each requester.

candidates.name: Hierarchical tree arbiter
candidates.description: Splits requesters into groups with a local arbiter per group and a root arbiter choosing among groups, keeping a priority pointer in each local and root node.

candidates.name: Separable input-first switch allocator
candidates.description: Matches router inputs to outputs in two stages, first picking one request per input then one input per output, keeping a round-robin pointer register in every input and output arbiter.

candidates.name: iSLIP allocator
candidates.description: Performs iterative request-grant-accept matching between switch inputs and outputs, keeping a grant pointer per output and an accept pointer per input that advance only on accepted matches.

candidates.name: Wavefront allocator
candidates.description: Computes a crossbar matching by sweeping priority diagonally across a request matrix of cells, keeping a register that selects which diagonal starts with top priority each cycle.

candidates.name: TDMA slot arbiter
candidates.description: Grants the resource according to a fixed time-division schedule, keeping a slot counter and a programmable schedule table mapping each slot to an owner.

candidates.name: Bus parking arbiter
candidates.description: Leaves the grant on a default or most-recent master when no one requests, keeping a park-master register and the current owner register to avoid re-arbitration latency.

candidates.name: Token-passing ring arbiter
candidates.description: Circulates a single token among requesters so only the holder may use the resource, keeping a token-position register that moves forward when the holder releases or has no request.

candidates.name: Aging-promotion priority arbiter
candidates.description: Uses strict priority but raises a low-priority requester's effective level once it has waited too long, keeping per-requester starvation timers and promoted-level flags.

candidates.name: Burst-hold arbiter
candidates.description: Keeps the grant on the current winner until its multi-beat transaction finishes, holding an owner register and a beats-remaining counter loaded from the burst length.

candidates.name: Mutual-exclusion element
candidates.description: Resolves two asynchronous requests into a single grant using a cross-coupled latch followed by a metastability filter, storing which side currently owns the resource.

candidates.name: K-of-N multi-grant arbiter
candidates.description: Issues up to K simultaneous grants to distinct requesters per cycle for a K-ported resource, keeping a rotating start pointer and a grant vector register.

candidates.name: FR-FCFS DRAM command arbiter
candidates.description: Prioritizes queued memory requests that hit an already-open row and otherwise picks the oldest, keeping open-row registers per bank and arrival timestamps per queue entry.

candidates.name: Earliest-deadline-first arbiter
candidates.description: Grants the pending requester whose deadline is nearest, keeping a countdown deadline register per requester reloaded from a programmable period on each grant.

candidates.name: Read/write turnaround arbiter
candidates.description: Chooses between read and write queues while batching same-direction accesses to limit bus turnarounds, keeping a current-direction register and a batch-length counter.

candidates.name: Banked memory conflict arbiter
candidates.description: Resolves simultaneous accesses from many ports to multiple memory banks by arbitrating separately per bank, keeping a priority pointer per bank and a per-port stall register.

candidates.name: Exponential backoff arbiter
candidates.description: Makes losing requesters wait a randomized, doubling delay before retrying, keeping per-requester backoff counters, collision-count registers and an LFSR for jitter.

candidates.name: Stride proportional-share scheduler
candidates.description: Grants the requester with the smallest pass value and then advances that pass by its stride, keeping per-requester stride and pass registers.

candidates.name: Bandwidth-regulated QoS arbiter
candidates.description: Lets real-time requesters win by priority only while their per-period byte budgets last, keeping per-requester consumed-bytes counters and a regulation-period timer that resets them.

candidates.name: Wishbone shared-bus intercon
candidates.description: Connects several Wishbone masters to several slaves over one shared bus, holding a current-owner register and a cycle-active flag that keeps the owning master on the bus while CYC is asserted.

candidates.name: Wishbone-to-AXI bridge
candidates.description: Converts Wishbone classic or pipelined cycles into AXI4 read and write transactions, keeping a pending-request register, an address/data holding latch and a phase-state register for the AW/W/B or AR/R sequence.

candidates.name: AHB-to-AXI bridge
candidates.description: Translates AHB-Lite address and data phases into AXI channel transactions, storing the captured HADDR/HSIZE/HBURST control, a write-data buffer and a waiting-for-response state register used to drive HREADY.

candidates.name: AHB multilayer input stage
candidates.description: Sits at each master port of an AHB bus matrix and captures an address phase when the target slave layer is busy, holding the pending transfer's control signals and a pending-valid flag until the layer accepts it.

candidates.name: AHB default slave
candidates.description: Answers accesses to unmapped AHB addresses with a two-cycle ERROR response, keeping a small response-phase state register.

candidates.name: AXI default slave
candidates.description: Terminates AXI transactions routed to unmapped regions with DECERR responses, storing the accepted ID, a burst-length countdown for returning read beats and a pending write-response flag.

candidates.name: AXI4-Lite to AXI4 upconverter
candidates.description: Lets an AXI4-Lite master reach a full AXI4 fabric by adding fixed ID, length and burst fields, keeping registered copies of the in-flight read and write requests.

candidates.name: AXI4-to-AXI4-Lite downconverter
candidates.description: Breaks full AXI4 bursts into single-beat AXI4-Lite accesses, holding the original ID, a beat-remaining counter, the running address and an accumulated worst-case response register.

candidates.name: AXI ID remapper
candidates.description: Compresses wide upstream transaction IDs into a smaller downstream ID space, keeping a table of remapped-ID entries each with its original ID and an outstanding-transaction count.

candidates.name: AXI data-width upsizer
candidates.description: Packs narrow AXI write beats into wider downstream beats and unpacks wide read beats, storing a packing buffer with byte-strobe mask, a lane-offset pointer and the captured burst size and length.

candidates.name: AXI data-width downsizer
candidates.description: Splits wide AXI beats into multiple narrow beats for a narrower slave, keeping the wide data word being drained, a sub-beat index and a re-merge register for assembling read responses.

candidates.name: AXI clock-domain crossing bridge
candidates.description: Carries all five AXI channels between asynchronous clock domains using per-channel dual-clock storage, holding the payload memories plus write and read pointers on each side.

candidates.name: AXI 4KB boundary burst splitter
candidates.description: Divides incoming AXI bursts that would cross a 4KB page into legal sub-bursts, storing the remaining length, next start address and a count of sub-bursts whose responses must be merged.

candidates.name: AXI write-channel ordering queue
candidates.description: Routes W-channel data in an interconnect to the slave chosen by each accepted AW request, keeping a queue of destination port indices in address-acceptance order.

candidates.name: AXI response router
candidates.description: Steers B and R responses from slaves back to the originating master using a lookup table that records the source master port for each outstanding transaction ID.

candidates.name: AXI outstanding-transaction limiter
candidates.description: Throttles a master port's AR and AW handshakes based on configured maximums, keeping separate outstanding-read and outstanding-write counters along with the limit registers.

candidates.name: AXI exclusive access monitor
candidates.description: Supports AXI exclusive load/store pairs by tracking reservations, storing per-master reservation address, size and valid bits that are cleared by conflicting writes.

candidates.name: AXI-Stream switch
candidates.description: Routes AXI-Stream packets from several input ports to output ports according to TDEST, holding per-output current-input selection and a packet-in-progress lock cleared on TLAST.

candidates.name: AXI-Stream broadcaster
candidates.description: Copies each AXI-Stream beat to several downstream consumers, keeping a per-output delivered mask so the input beat is retired only after every output has taken it.

candidates.name: AXI QoS regulator
candidates.description: Shapes a master's bandwidth and latency by adjusting AxQOS or stalling requests, holding configured rate and burstiness registers, an accumulated byte budget and a latency target register.

candidates.name: Bus firewall
candidates.description: Checks each transaction's address, security attribute and master ID against programmable regions and blocks violators, storing region base/limit/permission registers and a captured violation log.

candidates.name: Bus timeout monitor
candidates.description: Watches outstanding transactions on a bus port and forces an error response if a slave stalls too long, keeping per-transaction cycle counters, a timeout threshold register and a sticky timeout status bit.

candidates.name: Bus performance monitor
candidates.description: Observes handshakes on an interconnect port and accumulates statistics, holding counters for transactions, bytes moved, stall cycles and cumulative latency plus a sampling-window register.

candidates.name: Address remap unit
candidates.description: Rewrites transaction addresses through programmable windows before decoding, such as aliasing boot ROM to address zero, storing per-window source base, size, target base and enable registers.

candidates.name: AHB split-transaction controller
candidates.description: Lets an AHB slave issue SPLIT responses and later signal readiness to resume, keeping a mask of split-pending masters and the HSPLIT bits it drives back to the arbiter.

candidates.name: DAMQ input buffer
candidates.description: A dynamically allocated multi-queue input buffer that stores flits for several virtual channels in one shared SRAM, keeping per-VC head and tail pointers, a next-pointer linked-list memory and a free-slot list.

candidates.name: Virtual-channel state table
candidates.description: Tracks per-input-VC progress through the router pipeline, holding for each VC a state field (idle, routing, waiting for VC, active), the computed output port and the assigned output VC.

candidates.name: Output VC status register
candidates.description: Records for each downstream virtual channel whether it is currently reserved by a packet, plus the identity of the input VC that holds it.

candidates.name: Separable switch allocator
candidates.description: Matches requesting input VCs to crossbar output ports each cycle using input-stage and output-stage arbitration, keeping per-input and per-output priority pointer registers.

candidates.name: Speculative switch allocator
candidates.description: Lets head flits bid for crossbar slots in parallel with VC allocation and gives non-speculative requests precedence, holding separate priority registers for the speculative and non-speculative request classes.

candidates.name: Table-based routing lookup
candidates.description: Maps a packet's destination ID to an output port through a programmable routing table memory, with configuration write registers for updating entries.

candidates.name: Lookahead route computation unit
candidates.description: Computes the output port a packet will take at the next-hop router and writes it into the flit header, keeping a registered copy of the current router's coordinates and the precomputed next-hop direction.

candidates.name: Odd-even adaptive output selector
candidates.description: Chooses among the minimal output directions permitted by odd-even turn rules by comparing downstream congestion indicators, holding registered coordinates and the latest congestion values for each candidate port.

candidates.name: Source-route header shifter
candidates.description: Pops the next hop field from a source-routed packet header to select the output port and shifts the remaining route bits, holding the current route vector register.

candidates.name: Output port wormhole lock
candidates.description: Reserves a crossbar output port for one input from head flit until tail flit passes, keeping a locked flag and the owning input index per output.

candidates.name: Flit type decoder
candidates.description: Classifies incoming flits as head, body, tail or single-flit and extracts destination, VC and message class fields into registered header fields.

candidates.name: Packetizer network interface
candidates.description: Splits outgoing messages from a core into header and payload flits for injection, holding the pending message register, a flit index counter and the assigned packet sequence number.

candidates.name: Deflection port assigner
candidates.description: In a bufferless router, assigns every arriving flit to some output port each cycle, deflecting losers to free ports by rank, and keeps per-flit age or hop-count fields used to rank them.

candidates.name: Age-based arbiter
candidates.description: Grants contending flits by oldest injection timestamp, holding a timestamp register per request slot and a local cycle counter for computing age.

candidates.name: Escape VC controller
candidates.description: Steers packets into a deadlock-free escape virtual channel restricted to dimension-order routing when adaptive VCs are blocked, keeping per-packet escape flags and a blocked-cycles counter.

candidates.name: Bubble flow control gate
candidates.description: Admits a packet into a ring or torus dimension only if enough free buffer slots would remain, keeping a free-slot count register for the downstream ring buffer.

candidates.name: Multicast replication unit
candidates.description: Forks a multicast flit to several output ports according to a destination bitmask, keeping a register of the ports still to be served for the current flit.

candidates.name: Regional congestion monitor
candidates.description: Aggregates local buffer occupancy with congestion values received from neighbors into a per-direction congestion metric, holding a filtered congestion register for each port.

candidates.name: Link retransmission buffer
candidates.description: Holds transmitted flits until the receiver acknowledges them and replays from the oldest unacknowledged flit on error, keeping a replay buffer, a send sequence number and a last-acked pointer.

candidates.name: Express bypass latch
candidates.description: Lets a flit skip the buffer-write and allocation stages when the input is idle and a lookahead signal has pre-reserved the crossbar, keeping a bypass-valid flag and the latched flit.

candidates.name: TDM slot table
candidates.description: Implements guaranteed-throughput circuit switching by mapping each time slot of a repeating frame to an input-output connection, holding a slot table memory and a current slot counter.

candidates.name: Link fault status register
candidates.description: Records which router links are disabled due to faults and masks them out of routing decisions, keeping a per-link fault bit vector and an error event counter per link.

candidates.name: On/off flow control signaler
candidates.description: Sends off and on signals upstream as input buffer occupancy crosses high and low thresholds, keeping the threshold registers and the current off-state flag.

candidates.name: Ring stop interface
candidates.description: Inserts and removes flits on a unidirectional ring, giving through-traffic priority over injection, and keeps a ring slot register, an injection queue head and a starvation counter that triggers slot reservation.

candidates.name: 1-Wire bus master
candidates.description: Generates reset/presence, write-slot and read-slot timing on a single open-drain line, keeping a slot timer, a bit counter, a shift register for the current byte and a presence-detected flag.

candidates.name: UART auto-baud detector
candidates.description: Measures the width of the start bit or a known sync character on the receive line to derive a baud divisor, holding an edge-capture timer, a measurement-state register and the resulting divisor register.

candidates.name: UART break detector
candidates.description: Flags a line held low for longer than a full character frame, keeping a low-duration bit-time counter and a sticky break-received status bit.

candidates.name: UART hardware flow control unit
candidates.description: Drives RTS from receive-buffer fill level and gates transmission on sampled CTS, keeping a synchronized CTS register, an RTS output register and programmable assert/deassert threshold registers.

candidates.name: UART line status block
candidates.description: Collects parity, framing, overrun and break errors from the receiver into a readable status word, holding sticky error flag registers and an interrupt-enable mask.

candidates.name: UART receive idle timeout
candidates.description: Signals that received characters are waiting but no new character has arrived for a programmed number of character times, keeping an idle bit-time counter, a timeout-threshold register and a timeout-pending flag.

candidates.name: UART multidrop address matcher
candidates.description: Recognizes 9-bit mode address characters on a shared serial bus and enables data reception only after its own address is seen, holding a station-address register, an address mask and a selected flag.

candidates.name: IrDA SIR encoder/decoder
candidates.description: Converts UART bits to 3/16-bit-time infrared pulses and back, keeping a sixteenth-bit phase counter, a pulse-width register and a received-pulse latch.

candidates.name: LIN bus controller
candidates.description: Sends and receives LIN frames including the break field, sync byte, protected identifier and classic or enhanced checksum, keeping a frame-phase state register, an identifier register, a data buffer and a running checksum register.

candidates.name: I2C start/stop condition detector
candidates.description: Watches SDA transitions while SCL is high to detect START, repeated START and STOP events, holding registered previous SCL/SDA samples and a bus-busy flag.

candidates.name: I2C spike suppression filter
candidates.description: Removes glitches shorter than a programmed width from SCL and SDA inputs, keeping a per-line sample shift register, a stable-output register and a filter-length configuration register.

candidates.name: I2C multi-master arbitration monitor
candidates.description: Compares the value driven on SDA against the sampled bus value during transmission to detect arbitration loss, holding the last driven bit, a lost-arbitration flag and the bit position where loss occurred.

candidates.name: I2C clock-stretch handler
candidates.description: Holds the master's SCL high phase until a slave releases the line and counts how long stretching lasts, keeping a stretch-duration counter, a stretching-active flag and a maximum-stretch limit register.

candidates.name: SMBus timeout and PEC unit
candidates.description: Monitors SMBus transactions for SCL-low timeouts and computes the CRC-8 packet error code over transferred bytes, keeping a low-time counter, a timeout flag and a PEC accumulator register.

candidates.name: I3C dynamic address assignment unit
candidates.description: Runs the ENTDAA procedure, arbitrating on 48-bit provisioned IDs and handing out dynamic addresses, keeping an ID shift register, a next-address register and a table of assigned addresses.

candidates.name: SPI chip-select sequencer
candidates.description: Asserts and deasserts individual slave-select lines with programmable setup, hold and inter-transfer delays, keeping a selected-slave register, a delay counter and a sequencing state register.

candidates.name: SPI daisy-chain controller
candidates.description: Clocks a single long frame through several cascaded SPI devices and latches it with a common chip-select release, holding a total chain-length register, a bit counter and a frame shift register.

candidates.name: Microwire interface
candidates.description: Implements the National Microwire half-duplex serial protocol with start bit, opcode, address and data phases, keeping a phase state register, an opcode/address shift register and a data shift register.

candidates.name: MDIO management master
candidates.description: Issues Clause 22/45 PHY register reads and writes over the MDC/MDIO two-wire interface, keeping a preamble counter, a 32-bit frame shift register, a turnaround phase flag and a read-data register.

candidates.name: Serial Wire Debug target port
candidates.description: Decodes SWD request packets, drives acknowledge and data phases with parity, and handles line turnaround, keeping a request register, a data shift register, a parity accumulator and a protocol-phase register.

candidates.name: Manchester decoder
candidates.description: Recovers data and clock from a Manchester-coded line by timing transitions against expected half and full bit periods, holding an edge-interval counter, the last line level and a decoded-bit shift register.

candidates.name: RS-485 driver-enable controller
candidates.description: Switches a half-duplex transceiver between transmit and receive, asserting driver enable before the first bit and releasing it after the final stop bit with a turnaround delay, keeping an enable register, a guard-time counter and a transmit-active flag.

candidates.name: Modbus RTU frame-gap timer
candidates.description: Delimits Modbus RTU frames by measuring silent intervals of 1.5 and 3.5 character times on the serial line, keeping an inter-character silence counter, a character-time threshold register and an end-of-frame flag.

candidates.name: WS2812 single-wire LED encoder
candidates.description: Translates 24-bit colour words into the timed high/low pulse pattern for addressable LED strings followed by a reset latch interval, keeping a pixel shift register, a bit counter, a pulse-width timer and a reset-gap counter.

candidates.name: Block lock state machine
candidates.description: Searches for valid 64b/66b sync headers by slipping bit positions until enough consecutive good headers are seen, keeping a slip-position register, a good-header counter, a bad-header counter and a lock flag.

candidates.name: Multi-lane deskew buffer
candidates.description: Aligns data from several lanes by delaying each lane until all have seen a common alignment marker, keeping per-lane delay FIFOs, per-lane marker-seen flags and an aligned flag.

candidates.name: PCIe LTSSM
candidates.description: Runs the PCIe link training and status state machine through Detect, Polling, Configuration, Recovery and L0 states, keeping a state register, timeout timers, training-set counters and negotiated link width and speed registers.

candidates.name: PRBS pattern generator
candidates.description: Produces PRBS7/15/31 test patterns for link bring-up, keeping a polynomial-select register, a seed register and the generator shift state.

candidates.name: PRBS checker with error counter
candidates.description: Self-synchronizes to an incoming PRBS stream and counts bit mismatches, keeping a local reference shift register, a sync flag and a saturating error counter.

candidates.name: Phase interpolator controller
candidates.description: Accumulates early/late votes into a phase code that steers a receive phase interpolator, keeping a vote integrator, a phase-code register and a frequency-tracking accumulator.

candidates.name: DFE tap adaptation engine
candidates.description: Adjusts decision-feedback equalizer tap weights using sign-sign LMS on slicer errors, keeping a coefficient register per tap, a history of past decided bits and a step-size register.

candidates.name: TX FIR de-emphasis unit
candidates.description: Computes pre-cursor, main and post-cursor transmit equalization drive levels from neighboring bits, keeping a short bit-history register and the cursor coefficient registers.

candidates.name: Eye scan monitor
candidates.description: Measures the receive eye by sampling at offset phases and voltages and comparing with the data slicer, keeping the current horizontal and vertical offset registers, a sample counter and a mismatch counter.

candidates.name: Lane polarity detector
candidates.description: Detects inverted differential pairs by recognizing inverted training symbols and then flips received bits, keeping an inversion flag per lane and a detection counter.

candidates.name: Lane reversal mapper
candidates.description: Remaps logical lane numbers to physical lanes when a link is wired in reverse order, keeping a reversal-enable register and the configured lane-mapping table.

candidates.name: 128b/130b encoder
candidates.description: Prepends a two-bit sync header to each 128-bit data or ordered-set block for PCIe Gen3+, keeping a block-type register, a symbol counter within the block and the staged block data.

candidates.name: Bit slip aligner
candidates.description: Rotates the deserialized word boundary one bit at a time on command to find word alignment, keeping a slip-count register, a previous-word register for concatenation and a slip-pending flag.

candidates.name: Multi-lane byte striper
candidates.description: Distributes a byte stream round-robin across active lanes for transmission, keeping a current-lane pointer, the active-lane-count register and per-lane staging registers.

candidates.name: NRZI encoder
candidates.description: Encodes data by toggling the line on one value and holding on the other, keeping the current line-level register.

candidates.name: MLT-3 encoder
candidates.description: Cycles the line through -1, 0, +1, 0 levels on each one bit for 100BASE-TX, keeping a two-bit level-sequence state register.

candidates.name: 4b/5b encoder
candidates.description: Maps 4-bit nibbles and control codes to 5-bit symbols with guaranteed transitions, keeping a registered input nibble, a control-select flag and the output symbol register.

candidates.name: PAM4 Gray symbol mapper
candidates.description: Groups pairs of bits into Gray-coded four-level PAM4 symbols with optional precoding, keeping a bit-pair staging register and a precoder previous-symbol register.

candidates.name: Bit stuffing unit
candidates.description: Inserts a zero after a run of consecutive ones to preserve transitions and frame delimiters, keeping a ones-run counter and a stall flag for the inserted bit.

candidates.name: Link replay buffer
candidates.description: Stores transmitted link-layer packets with sequence numbers until acknowledged and retransmits them on NAK or timeout, keeping the packet storage, next-transmit and last-acked sequence registers, a replay timer and a replay-count register.

candidates.name: Ethernet auto-negotiation engine
candidates.description: Exchanges link code words to agree on speed, duplex and pause abilities, keeping an arbitration state register, local and link-partner ability registers, a consistency-match counter and a link-timer.

candidates.name: Memory-to-memory copy engine
candidates.description: Copies a contiguous block from a source address to a destination address in bursts, holding source pointer, destination pointer, byte-count and control/status registers.

candidates.name: 2D strided transfer engine
candidates.description: Moves a rectangular region by transferring rows of fixed length and skipping a programmable stride between them, keeping row-length, row-count, source/destination stride and current row/column counters.

candidates.name: 3D tensor transfer engine
candidates.description: Walks a three-dimensional tensor with independent sizes and strides per dimension, storing per-dimension size, stride and loop-index registers plus base addresses.

candidates.name: Circular buffer DMA channel
candidates.description: Streams data into or out of a ring region in memory, wrapping the address back to the base on reaching the end, with base, size, current-offset and wrap-count registers.

candidates.name: Transfer interrupt generator
candidates.description: Raises half-transfer, transfer-complete and error interrupts for each channel, keeping per-channel pending, mask and clear registers.

candidates.name: Byte realignment unit
candidates.description: Shifts and merges data so an unaligned source stream lands correctly on an unaligned destination, holding a residual byte buffer, byte-offset register and valid-byte mask.

candidates.name: Data width packer/unpacker
candidates.description: Converts between narrow peripheral words and wide bus beats by packing or splitting lanes, storing a partial-word accumulator and lane-index counter.

candidates.name: Pattern fill engine
candidates.description: Writes a programmable constant or repeating pattern across a memory region without reading a source, keeping the pattern register, destination pointer and remaining-length counter.

candidates.name: Endianness byte-swap stage
candidates.description: Reorders bytes within each transferred word according to a per-channel swap mode, holding the swap-mode configuration and a registered data stage.

candidates.name: Completion ring writer
candidates.description: Writes completion records with status and transferred length into a host-visible ring after each transfer, keeping ring base, size, producer index and pending-record registers.

candidates.name: Descriptor prefetch cache
candidates.description: Fetches upcoming transfer descriptors ahead of use and holds them in a small local memory, with entry valid bits, tag addresses and a next-fetch pointer.

candidates.name: Write response tracker
candidates.description: Counts posted writes per channel and matches incoming write acknowledgments so a channel can report final completion, holding per-channel outstanding-write counters and error flags.

candidates.name: Channel context store
candidates.description: Saves and restores the full register context of suspended channels so many logical channels share fewer physical engines, using a context RAM indexed by channel number and an active-channel register.

candidates.name: Burst boundary splitter
candidates.description: Breaks a large request into bus bursts that respect maximum burst length and address-boundary limits, storing the current address, remaining bytes and the computed next-burst length.

candidates.name: Indexed gather engine
candidates.description: Reads an array of indices from memory and fetches the elements they point to into a dense destination, keeping index pointer, element base, element size and destination pointer registers.

candidates.name: Peripheral watermark trigger
candidates.description: Issues DMA requests when a peripheral FIFO level crosses programmable thresholds, holding the threshold registers, sampled level and request-pending flag.

candidates.name: Channel control register block
candidates.description: Exposes software-visible enable, pause, abort and priority controls for each DMA channel, storing per-channel control and status words.

candidates.name: DMA error capture unit
candidates.description: Records the first bus error, descriptor fault or alignment fault seen by a channel, latching the faulting address, error code and channel identifier.

candidates.name: Memory search/compare engine
candidates.description: Scans a memory region comparing each word against a key or a second region and stops on a match or mismatch, keeping key, mask, scan pointer and result-address registers.

candidates.name: Stream-to-memory writer
candidates.description: Accepts a packetized data stream and writes each packet to a memory buffer, recording packet length and end-of-packet status in buffer pointer, byte-count and length-capture registers.

candidates.name: Memory-to-stream reader
candidates.description: Reads a memory buffer and emits it as a stream with start and last markers on packet boundaries, keeping read pointer, remaining-length counter and packet-size registers.

candidates.name: Cache maintenance injector
candidates.description: Issues clean or invalidate operations over the address range a non-coherent DMA transfer touches, holding range start, range end and current line-address registers.

candidates.name: Address mode generator
candidates.description: Produces per-beat source and destination addresses in increment, decrement or fixed mode for each side of a transfer, storing mode bits, step size and the current address.

candidates.name: DMA trigger routing matrix
candidates.description: Routes hardware events from peripherals, timers and other channels to selected DMA channel request inputs, holding per-channel trigger-select registers and latched pending-request bits.

candidates.name: Edge-triggered interrupt latch
candidates.description: Captures rising or falling edges on an interrupt input into a sticky pending bit, keeping a previous-sample register and the pending flag until software clears it.

candidates.name: Level-sensitive interrupt gate
candidates.description: Passes an active-level interrupt line through to the controller while it is asserted, keeping a polarity-select register and a sampled-level register.

candidates.name: Interrupt mask register bank
candidates.description: Gates each interrupt source with a per-source enable bit, holding a mask register with separate set and clear write ports.

candidates.name: Programmable priority level array
candidates.description: Assigns a software-written priority value to each interrupt source, holding a per-source priority register array.

candidates.name: Priority threshold filter
candidates.description: Suppresses interrupts whose priority does not exceed the current per-processor threshold, keeping a threshold register for each target hart.

candidates.name: In-service register stack
candidates.description: Tracks which interrupt levels a processor is currently servicing to enable nesting, keeping an in-service bit vector and a running-priority register.

candidates.name: Claim/complete gateway
candidates.description: Hands the highest pending interrupt ID to a processor on a claim read and re-arms the source on a complete write, keeping per-source in-flight flags and the last claimed ID.

candidates.name: Vectored interrupt address generator
candidates.description: Forms the handler entry address from a base register plus the winning interrupt number scaled by the entry size, keeping a vector-base register and a vectored-mode bit.

candidates.name: Interrupt routing table
candidates.description: Steers each interrupt source to one or more target processors, holding a per-source target-select or affinity mask register.

candidates.name: Inter-processor interrupt generator
candidates.description: Lets one processor raise a software interrupt on another, keeping per-target IPI pending bits and a sender-ID register.

candidates.name: Message-signaled interrupt decoder
candidates.description: Converts memory-write transactions to a doorbell address into interrupt assertions, keeping an address-match register and a table of pending event IDs.

candidates.name: MSI-X vector table
candidates.description: Stores per-vector message address, data and mask entries in a RAM and emits a message write when a function signals a vector, keeping a pending-bit array for masked vectors.

candidates.name: Interrupt translation service
candidates.description: Maps a device ID and event ID pair to a physical interrupt number and target collection through cached translation tables, keeping a device table cache and a command queue pointer pair.

candidates.name: Locality-specific peripheral interrupt pending table
candidates.description: Holds a large memory-backed pending and enable bitmap for message interrupts, keeping a property table base register and a cached pending-table slice.

candidates.name: Interrupt coalescing timer
candidates.description: Delays and batches interrupt assertions until either an event count or a time limit is reached, keeping an event counter, a holdoff timer and their programmed limits.

candidates.name: Interrupt rate moderator
candidates.description: Enforces a minimum interval between successive interrupt assertions to a processor, keeping an inter-interrupt countdown and a deferred-pending flag.

candidates.name: Fast interrupt request bypass
candidates.description: Routes one designated high-urgency source directly to the processor's fast-interrupt pin ahead of the normal priority path, keeping a source-select register and an enable bit.

candidates.name: Non-maskable interrupt latch
candidates.description: Captures a non-maskable event and holds it until the processor acknowledges, keeping a pending flag and an NMI-in-progress flag that blocks re-entry.

candidates.name: Daisy-chain interrupt acknowledge cell
candidates.description: Passes an interrupt-acknowledge token down a chain of devices so the first requesting device claims it and places its vector on the bus, keeping a request flag and a local vector register.

candidates.name: Cascaded slave controller link
candidates.description: Connects a secondary interrupt controller into one input of a primary controller and forwards the slave's vector on acknowledge, keeping a cascade-identity register and a slave-mode configuration bit.

candidates.name: Interrupt preemption and tail-chaining unit
candidates.description: Decides whether a newly arriving interrupt preempts the running handler or chains directly after it without restoring context, keeping a priority-group split register and the active exception number.

candidates.name: Wake-up interrupt controller
candidates.description: Monitors masked interrupt inputs while the processor core is powered down and signals the power controller to wake it, keeping a copy of the wake-enable mask and a latched wake-source register.

candidates.name: Virtual interrupt list register file
candidates.description: Holds hypervisor-injected virtual interrupts for a guest processor, keeping per-entry virtual ID, priority, state and linked physical ID fields.

candidates.name: Interrupt pending snapshot register
candidates.description: Exposes a software-readable, atomically captured view of all raw and masked pending sources, keeping a raw-status register and a write-one-to-clear status register.

candidates.name: Spurious interrupt detector
candidates.description: Returns a reserved spurious vector when a claim finds no qualifying pending interrupt, keeping a spurious-vector register and a spurious-event counter.

candidates.name: Windowed watchdog
